author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.title: Research Summary: May 19, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on fundamental limitations of core LLM components and critical AI safety findings for deployed agents.

  • RoPE is proven to lose both locality bias and token relevance as context grows, explaining long-context degradation across all major LLMs
  • Negation Neglect reveals that finetuning on negated false claims paradoxically reinforces the falsehoods, a critical failure mode for safety training
  • Prompt injection is reframed via Contextual Integrity theory, arguing data-instruction separation defenses are fundamentally insufficient
  • RePlaid demonstrates continuous diffusion language models scale competitively with discrete approaches, challenging field assumptions

Safety monitoring faces compounding challenges: Classifier Context Rot shows frontier monitors (Opus 4.6, GPT 5.4, Gemini 3.1) miss dangerous actions 2-30x more at 800K tokens, while sleeper memory poisoning introduces stealthy attacks on persistent agent memory. Hybrid DeltaNet-Attention decoders are proven to solve retrieval tasks in O(1) chain-of-thought steps versus O(n) for pure attention, directly relevant to architectures like Qwen3-Next. Agent skill scaling laws reveal logarithmic routing accuracy decay with library size.

entry.title: An Information-Theoretic Criterion for Efficient Data Synthesis

author.name: Hanyu Li, Zhengqi Sun, Xiaotie Deng

entry.summary: Provides an information-theoretic framework explaining when synthetic data helps LLM training: only when the generation loop is 'information-open' (shaped by external signals like verifiers). Shows the data processing inequality predicts collapse in closed loops.

entry.title: Continuous Diffusion Scales Competitively with Discrete Diffusion for Language

author.name: Zhihan Yang, Wei Guo, Shuibai Zhang, Subham Sekhar Sahoo, Yongxin Chen, Arash Vahdat, Morteza Mardani, John Thickstun

entry.summary: Demonstrates that continuous diffusion language models can scale competitively with discrete approaches by aligning architectures. RePlaid achieves state-of-the-art for continuous diffusion LMs with only 20x compute gap vs autoregressive models, establishing first scaling laws for continuous DLMs.

entry.title: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections

author.name: Sahar Abdelnabi, Eugene Bagdasarian

entry.summary: Argues that prompt injection defenses based on data-instruction separation are fundamentally insufficient, reframing the problem through Contextual Integrity theory. Develops attack scenarios that manipulate norms and flow representations.

entry.title: Negation Neglect: When models fail to learn negations in training

author.name: harrymayne

entry.summary: Demonstrates that finetuning LLMs on documents containing false claims annotated with negations (flagging them as false) can paradoxically make models believe the claims are true. This 'negation neglect' occurs across all tested models and extends to epistemic qualifiers and behavioral warnings.

entry.title: Classifier Context Rot: Monitor Performance Degrades with Context Length

author.name: Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Shows that frontier LLM monitors (Opus 4.6, GPT 5.4, Gemini 3.1) miss dangerous actions 2x-30x more often when transcripts are prepended with 800K tokens of benign activity compared to original short transcripts. Proposes periodic reminder prompting as partial mitigation.

entry.title: Provably Shorter Scratchpads in Hybrid DeltaNet-Attention Decoders

author.name: Tomasz Steifer

entry.summary: Proves that hybrid DeltaNet-Attention decoders (as in Qwen3-Next) can solve parity-conditioned retrieval with O(1) chain-of-thought steps, while pure recurrent models cannot and pure attention requires linear steps.

entry.title: The Scaling Laws of Skills in LLM Agent Systems

author.name: Charles Chen, Qiming Yu, Yuhang Gu, Zhuoye Huang, Hanjing Li, Hongyu Liu, Simin Liu, Jinhao Liu, Dengyun Peng, Jiangyi Wang, Zheng Yan, Fanqing Meng, Ethan Qin, Carl Che, Mengkang Hu

entry.summary: Identifies two coupled scaling laws for skills in LLM agent systems: routing accuracy decays logarithmically with library size, and execution accuracy improves downstream decisions ~4x. A single parameter (routing decay slope) couples both laws across 15 frontier LLMs and 1,141 skills.

entry.title: Predictable Confabulations: Factual Recall by LLMs Scales with Model Size and Topic Frequency

author.name: Matthew L. Smith, Jonathan P. Shock, Samuel T. Segun, Iyiola E. Olatunji, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: Discovers that LLM factual recall follows a sigmoid function of log-linear combination of model parameter count and topic frequency in training data. These two variables explain 60% of variance across 16 dense models, providing the first scaling law linking factual recall to training-data composition.

entry.title: Overeager Coding Agents: Measuring Out-of-Scope Actions on Benign Tasks

author.name: Yubin Qu, Ying Zhang, Yanjun Zhang, Gelei Deng, Yuekang Li, Leo Yu Zhang, Yi Liu

entry.summary: Identifies 'overeager actions' where coding agents exceed their authorized scope on benign tasks (deleting unrelated files, rewriting configs). Introduces OverEager-Gen benchmark and finds Claude Code exhibits this behavior significantly.

entry.title: Fair outputs, Biased Internals: Causal Potency and Asymmetry of Latent Bias in LLMs for High-Stakes Decisions

author.name: Jagdish Tripathy, Marcus Buckmann

entry.summary: Reveals that instruction-tuned LLMs show no output-level bias in mortgage underwriting but retain and amplify biased demographic representations internally. Through activation steering, they show this suppressed information is causally potent and asymmetric across racial groups.

entry.title: Process Rewards with Learned Reliability

author.name: Jinyuan Li, Langlin Huang, Chengsong Huang, Shaoyang Xu, Donghong Cai, Yuyi Yang, Wenxuan Zhang, Jiaxin Huang

entry.summary: Proposes BetaPRM, a distributional Process Reward Model that predicts both step-level success probability and prediction reliability using Beta-Binomial likelihood, enabling downstream methods to know when to trust reward signals.

entry.title: Mixing Times of Glauber Dynamics on Masked Language Models

author.name: Suvadip Sana, Sami Wolf, Neer Mehta, Alina Shah, Aitzaz Shaikh, Janna Goodman, Lionel Levine

entry.summary: Studies iterative masked-token resampling in MLMs as Glauber dynamics Markov chains, showing that MLM conditionals are intrinsically incompatible (no consistent joint distribution). Provides theoretical analysis of mixing times under bounded cross-token influence.

entry.title: Where Pretraining writes and Alignment reads: the asymmetry of Transformer weight space

author.name: Valeria Ruscio, Eli-Shaoul Khedouri, Keiran Thompson

entry.summary: Characterizes the geometric asymmetry between pretraining and alignment in transformer weight space: alignment concentrates in read pathway (Q, K) along attention-input activation directions, while remaining isotropic in write pathway (O, FF2).

entry.title: The Unlearnability Phenomenon in RLVR for Language Models

author.name: Yulin Chen, He He, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: Reveals that in RLVR for LLMs, many hard examples remain unlearnable even when correct rollouts exist. Cross-example gradient analysis shows these have low gradient similarity and ungeneralizable reasoning patterns.

entry.title: Alignment Dynamics in LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yuhan Huang, Huanran Chen, Yinpeng Dong

entry.summary: Derives a closed-form update rule for alignment dynamics during LLM fine-tuning, decomposing alignment changes into competing components that explain alignment fragility. Provides a unified framework bridging parameter-space learning dynamics with function-space alignment behavior.

entry.title: Training Infinitely Deep and Wide Transformers

author.name: Rapha\"el Barboni, Maarten V. de Hoop, Takashi Furuya, Gabriel Peyr\'e

entry.summary: Develops a rigorous mathematical framework for training transformers in the mean-field regime where both depth and width tend to infinity, showing transformer training corresponds to controlling a neural PDE due to attention coupling token distributions.

entry.title: Flowing with Confidence

author.name: Friso de Kruiff, Dario Coscia, Max Welling, Erik Bekkers

entry.summary: Proposes Flow Matching with Confidence (FMwC), a method that adds input-dependent noise to generative flow models and propagates variance in closed form to yield per-sample confidence scores at standard sampling cost. This eliminates the need for expensive ensemble methods while enabling filtering, editing, and active learning applications.

entry.title: ESI-Bench: Towards Embodied Spatial Intelligence that Closes the Perception-Action Loop

author.name: Yining Hong, Jiageng Liu, Han Yin, Manling Li, Leonidas Guibas, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Yejin Choi

entry.summary: Introduces ESI-BENCH, a comprehensive benchmark for embodied spatial intelligence spanning 10 task categories grounded in Spelke's core knowledge systems. Tests agents that must actively decide what abilities to deploy rather than passively processing observations.

entry.title: PARALLAX: Separating Genuine Hallucination Detection from Benchmark Construction Artifacts

author.name: Khizar Hussain, Murat Kantarcioglu

entry.summary: Exposes critical flaws in hallucination detection benchmarks: four of six widely-used corpora embed ground-truth answers in input prompts, allowing a simple text-similarity baseline to achieve near-perfect detection without model internals access.

entry.title: Multi-agent AI systems outperform human teams in creativity

author.name: Tiancheng Hu, Yixuan Jiang, Haotian Li, Jos\'e Hern\'andez-Orallo, Xing Xie, Nigel Collier, David Stillwell, Luning Sun

entry.summary: Demonstrates that multi-agent LLM teams substantially outperform human teams in creativity (Cohen's d=1.50) across 4,541 AI-generated ideas and 341 human-team ideas on six problem-solving tasks. The advantage is driven by novelty while maintaining comparable usefulness.

entry.title: Trust No Tool: Evaluating and Defending LLM Agents under Untrusted Tool Feedback

author.name: Lecheng Yan, Ruizhe Li, Xicheng Han, Wenxi Li, Binwu Wang, Longyue Wang, Chenyang Lyu, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: Studies 'cognitive poisoning' where malicious tools behave normally during exploration but become harmful when hidden conditions align. Introduces TRUST-Bench with 1,970 hidden-trigger episodes and proposes defenses.

entry.title: Dexora: Open-source VLA for High-DoF Bimanual Dexterity

author.name: Zongzheng Zhang, Jingrui Pang, Zhuo Yang, Kun Li, Minwen Liao, Saining Zhang, Guoxuan Chi, Jinbang Guo, Huan-ang Gao, Modi Shi, Dongyun Ge, Yao Mu, Jiayuan Gu, Rui Chen, Hao Dong, Huazhe Xu, Li Yi, Yixin Zhu, Hang Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Shanghang Zhang, Guocai Yao, Jianyu Chen, Hongyang Li, Hao Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces Dexora, the first open-source Vision-Language-Action (VLA) system for dual-arm, dual-hand high-DoF dexterous manipulation. Uses a hybrid teleoperation pipeline combining exoskeleton for arm motion and Apple Vision Pro for finger tracking.

entry.title: UAM: A Dual-Stream Perspective on Forgetting in VLA Training

author.name: Jianke Zhang, Yuanfei Luo, Yucheng Hu, Xiaoyu Chen, Yanjiang Guo, Ziyang Liu, Hongbin Xu, Tian Lan, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: Reveals that VLA fine-tuning systematically erodes VLM multimodal competence ('embodiment tax'), and proposes UAM with a parallel Dorsal Expert inspired by the brain's two-stream visual system to separate semantic and visuomotor processing.

entry.title: Agentic Discovery of Neural Architectures: AIRA-Compose and AIRA-Design

author.name: Alberto Pepe, Chien-Yu Lin, Despoina Magka, Bilge Acun, Yannan Nellie Wu, Anton Protopopov, Carole-Jean Wu, Yoram Bachrach

entry.summary: AIRA-Compose and AIRA-Design use 11 LLM agents to autonomously discover novel neural architectures beyond standard Transformers, finding architectures that outperform Llama 3.2 at 1B scale under a 24-hour compute budget.

entry.title: DeltaPrompts: Escaping the Zero-Delta Trap in Multimodal Distillation

author.name: Jaehun Jung, Hyunwoo Kim, Brandon Cui, Ximing Lu, David Acuna, Prithviraj Ammanabrolu, Yejin Choi

entry.summary: Reveals that up to 69% of prompts in standard VLM distillation datasets are 'zero-delta' (teacher and student already agree), providing minimal learning signal. Proposes DeltaPrompts to select maximally informative prompts for distillation.

entry.title: How Few-Shot Examples Add Up: A Causal Decomposition of Function Vectors in In-Context Learning

author.name: Entang Wang, Yiwei Wang, Aleksandra Bakalova, Michael Hahn

entry.summary: Shows that n-shot function vectors in ICL are well-approximated by linear combinations of example-level sub-FVs, and that models contextualize individual examples to adaptively reweight which demonstrations dominate based on informativeness.

entry.title: Propagation of Chaos in Contextual Flow Maps

author.name: Shi Chen, Zhengjiang Lin, Kaizhao Liu, Philippe Rigollet

entry.summary: Develops quantitative theory of transformers in the large-context regime using contextual flow maps and McKean-Vlasov dynamics, establishing propagation of chaos bounds showing context length acts as a statistical resource.

entry.title: Symmetry-Compatible Principle for Optimizer Design: Embeddings, LM Heads, SwiGLU MLPs, and MoE Routers

author.name: Tim Tsz-Kit Lau, Weijie Su

entry.summary: Introduces a symmetry-compatible principle for optimizer design where gradient updates should be equivariant under symmetry groups of weight blocks, deriving novel update rules for embeddings, LM heads, SwiGLU MLPs, and MoE routers.

entry.title: Forecasting Downstream Performance of LLMs With Proxy Metrics

author.name: Arkil Patel, Siva Reddy, Marius Mosbach, Dzmitry Bahdanau

entry.summary: Proposes proxy metrics for forecasting downstream LLM performance by aggregating token-level statistics (entropy, top-k accuracy, expert token rank) from next-token distributions over expert-written solutions. These proxies consistently outperform cross-entropy loss for early training decisions.

entry.title: The Point of No Return: Counterfactual Localization of Deceptive Commitment in Language-Model Reasoning

author.name: Scott Merrill, Shashank Srivastava

entry.summary: Introduces counterfactual localization for identifying when in a reasoning trace an LLM becomes committed to deception. Constructs five environments where deception emerges from strategic incentives and measures commitment probability at each prefix.

entry.title: Remembering More, Risking More: Longitudinal Safety Risks in Memory-Equipped LLM Agents

author.name: Ahmad Al-Tawaha, Shangding Gu, Peizhi Niu, Ruoxi Jia, Ming Jin

entry.summary: Studies temporal memory contamination in LLM agents: how memory accumulated during earlier independent tasks can degrade safety on later unrelated tasks. Introduces evaluation methodology for longitudinal safety degradation.

entry.title: Grokking as Structural Inference: Transformers Need Bayesian Lottery Tickets

author.name: Kai Hidajat, Solden Stoll, Joseph An

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical framework explaining grokking in Transformers through attention as implicit Bayesian inference over task dependency graphs, proving generalization requires both MLP capacity bounds and a Bayesian structural condition on attention.

entry.title: NOVA: Fundamental Limits of Knowledge Discovery Through AI

author.name: Salman Avestimehr, Ken Duffy, Muriel M\'edard

entry.summary: NOVA introduces a theoretical framework modeling the 'generate, verify, accumulate, retrain' loop of AI self-improvement, identifying conditions for success and failure modes including a 'contamination trap' where false positives accumulate as easy knowledge is exhausted.

entry.title: HoloMotion-1 Technical Report

author.name: Maiyue Chen, Kaihui Wang, Bo Zhang, Xihan Ma, Zhiyuan Yang, Yi Ren, Qijun Huang, Zihao Zhu, Yucheng Wang, Zhizhong Su

entry.summary: Presents HoloMotion-1, a humanoid motion foundation model for zero-shot whole-body motion tracking that scales training with hybrid motion data from in-the-wild videos combined with motion capture data. This addresses the limitation of MoCap-only training for humanoid robot control.

entry.title: When Is Rank-1 Steering Cheap? Geometry, Granularity, and Budgeted Search

author.name: John T. Robertson, Jianing Zhu, Haris Vikalo, Zhangyang Wang

entry.summary: This paper reframes the variability in activation steering effectiveness across concepts as a search difficulty problem rather than a fundamental limitation. It formalizes rank-1 steering as budget-constrained optimization and shows geometry-guided search can find effective interventions with far fewer evaluations.

entry.title: DCFold: Efficient Protein Structure Generation with Single Forward Pass

author.name: Zhe Zhang, Yuanning Feng, Yuxuan Song, Keyue Qiu, Hao Zhou, Wei-Ying Ma

entry.summary: DCFold achieves AlphaFold3-level protein structure prediction accuracy with a single forward pass (15x faster) using Dual Consistency training with a novel Temporal Geodesic Matching scheduler, enabling practical deployment for virtual screening and protein design.

entry.title: General Preference Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Muhammad Umer, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Ahsan Bilal, Arslan Chaudhry, Andreas Haupt, Sanmi Koyejo, Emily Fox, John M. Cioffi

entry.summary: Proposes General Preference RL that uses a multi-dimensional General Preference Model instead of scalar reward models for LLM alignment, bridging the gap between verifiable-reward RL (for math/code) and preference optimization (for open-ended tasks).

entry.title: VeriCache: Turning Lossy KV Cache into Lossless LLM Inference

author.name: Jiayi Yao, Samuel Shen, Kuntai Du, Shaoting Feng, Dongjoo Seo, Rui Zhang, Yuyang Huang, Yuhan Liu, Shan Lu, Junchen Jiang

entry.summary: Presents VeriCache, a framework that ensures identical output to full-KV-cache decoding while preserving high throughput of lossy KV cache compression methods, using compressed cache for draft generation and verifying against full cache.

entry.title: CHI-Bench: Can AI Agents Automate End-to-End, Long-Horizon, Policy-Rich Healthcare Workflows?

author.name: Haolin Chen, Deon Metelski, Leon Qi, Tao Xia, Joonyul Lee, Steve Brown, Kevin Riley, Frank Wang, T. Y. Alvin Liu, Hank Capps MD, Zeyu Tang, Xiangchen Song, Lingjing Kong, Fan Feng, Tianyi Zeng, Zhiwei Liu, Zixian Ma, Hang Jiang, Fangli Geng, Yuan Yuan, Chenyu You, Qingsong Wen, Hua Wei, Yanjie Fu, Yue Zhao, Carl Yang, Biwei Huang, Kun Zhang, Caiming Xiong, Sanmi Koyejo, Eric P. Xing, Philip S. Yu, Weiran Yao

entry.summary: Introduces CHI-Bench, a benchmark for healthcare workflow automation testing three underrepresented capabilities: policy density, multi-role composition, and multilateral interaction. Covers prior authorization, utilization management, and care management across 87 MCP tools.

entry.title: Full Attention Strikes Back: Transferring Full Attention into Sparse within Hundred Training Steps

author.name: Yanke Zhou, Yiduo Li, Hanlin Tang, Maohua Li, Kan Liu, Lan Tao, Lin Qu, Yuan Yao, Xiaoxing Ma

entry.summary: Shows that full-attention LLMs are intrinsically sparse and can be converted to highly sparse models with only ~100 training steps using a 16-dimensional indexer for long-range retrieval, achieving efficiency without native sparse training.

entry.title: Medical Context Distorts Decisions in Clinical Vision Language Models

author.name: David Restrepo, Ira Ktena, Maria Vakalopoulou, Stergios Christodoulidis, Enzo Ferrante

entry.summary: Identifies three failure modes in clinical vision-language models: over-reliance on text over images, spurious reliance on irrelevant clinical history, and prompt sensitivity. Shows VLM decisions are dominated by text modality even when visual evidence contradicts it.

entry.title: Qumus: Realization of An Embodied AI Quantum Material Experimentalist

author.name: Lihan Shi, Zhaoyi Joy Zheng, Xinzhe Juan, Yimin Wang, Ming Yin, Mayank Sengupta, Kristina Wolinski, Yanyu Jia, Jingzhi Shi, Derek Saucedo, Neill Saggi, Haosen Guan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ali Yazdani, Mengdi Wang, Sanfeng Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Qumus, the first AI quantum materials experimentalist - an embodied multi-agent system integrated with a robotic mini-laboratory for creating and processing 2D materials and van der Waals structures autonomously.

entry.title: Prospective multi-pathogen disease forecasting using autonomous LLM-guided tree search

author.name: Sarah Martinson, Michael P. Brenner, Martyna Plomecka, Brian P. Williams, Nicholas G. Reich, Zahra Shamsi

entry.summary: An autonomous LLM-guided tree search system generates diverse disease forecasting models for influenza, COVID-19, and RSV in real-time, producing ensembles that match or outperform expert-curated models during the 2025-2026 US respiratory season.

entry.title: AstraFlow: Dataflow-Oriented Reinforcement Learning for Agentic LLMs

author.name: Haizhong Zheng, Yizhuo Di, Jiahui Wang, Shuowei Jin, Xueshen Liu, Yongji Wu, Z. Morley Mao, Ion Stoica, Jiawei Zhao, Beidi Chen

entry.summary: Proposes AstraFlow, a dataflow-oriented RL system for training agentic LLMs that replaces conventional trainer-centered control with principled dataflow abstractions, supporting multi-policy collaborative training on heterogeneous compute.

entry.title: DashAttention: Differentiable and Adaptive Sparse Hierarchical Attention

author.name: Yuxiang Huang, Nuno M. T. Gon\c{c}alves, Federico Alvetreti, Lei Li, Xu Han, Edoardo M. Ponti, Andr\'e F. T. Martins, Marcos V. Treviso

entry.summary: Proposes DashAttention, which uses α-entmax transformation to adaptively select variable numbers of KV blocks in hierarchical attention, replacing fixed top-k selection. Keeps the entire hierarchy fully differentiable and achieves better efficiency-quality trade-offs.

entry.title: Ghosted Layers: Unconstrained Activation Alignment for Recovering Layer-Pruned LLMs

author.name: Vincent-Daniel Yun, Junhyuk Jo, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy, Sunwoo Lee

entry.summary: Proposes 'Ghosted Layers,' a training-free recovery module for layer-pruned LLMs that derives a closed-form optimal linear operator to reconstruct activation discrepancies introduced by pruned layers, showing this is the unconstrained optimum.

entry.title: RoadmapBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Agentic Software Development Across Version Upgrades

author.name: Xinbo Xu, Ruihan Yang, Haiyang Shen, Wendong Xu, Bofei Gao, Ruoyu Wu, Kean Shi, Weichu Xie, Xuanzhong Chen, Ming Wu, Jason Zeng, Michael Heinrich, Elvis Zhang, Liang Chen, Kuan Li, Baobao Chang

entry.summary: Presents RoadmapBench, a benchmark of 115 long-horizon coding tasks from real open-source version upgrades across 17 repositories and 5 languages, requiring agents to implement multi-target functionality from roadmap instructions.

entry.title: Constrained Code Generation with Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Lize Shao, Michael Cardei, Zichen Xie, Ferdinando Fioretto, Wenxi Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CDC (Constrained Diffusion for Code), a training-free neurosymbolic framework that integrates constraint satisfaction into discrete diffusion denoising for code generation, enforcing functionality and security constraints during generation.

entry.title: Imperfect World Models are Exploitable

author.name: Logan Mondal Bhamidipaty, Esmeralda S. Whitammer, David Abel, Mykel J. Kochenderfer, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

entry.summary: Proposes a formal definition of model exploitation in RL (where a world model implies wrong policy ordering), proves it's essentially unavoidable on large policy sets, and develops a general theory connecting reward hacking and model exploitation.

entry.title: PACER: Acyclic Causal Discovery from Large-Scale Interventional Data

author.name: Ramon Vi\~nas Torn\'e, S\'ilvia F\`abregas Salazar, Soyon Park, Ivo Alexander Ban, Artyom Gadetsky, Nikita Doikov, Maria Brbi\'c

entry.summary: Introduces PACER, a scalable framework for causal discovery from large-scale interventional data that guarantees acyclicity by construction through parameterizing distributions over DAGs via variable permutations and edge probabilities.

entry.title: Identifiable Token Correspondence for World Models

author.name: Youngin Kim (Interdisciplinary Program in Artificial Intelligence, Seoul National University), Ray Sun (Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Seoul National University), Inho Kim (Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Seoul National University), Bumsoo Park (KRAFTON), Hyun Oh Song (Interdisciplinary Program in Artificial Intelligence, Seoul National University, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Seoul National University)

entry.summary: Formulates next-frame prediction in world models as structured probabilistic inference with latent token correspondence variables, where each token is either copied from the previous frame or newly generated. Addresses temporal inconsistency issues like object duplication/disappearance.

entry.title: Decoupling KL and Trajectories: A Unified Perspective for SFT, DAgger, Offline RL, and OPD in LLM Distillation

author.name: Anhao Zhao, Haoran Xin, Yingqi Fan, Junlong Tong, Wenjie Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Decouples prefix source and KL direction in LLM distillation, showing that the prevailing SFT/OPD paradigms implicitly couple two orthogonal choices. Establishes gradient-level identities connecting forward/reverse KL to SFT and DAgger.

entry.title: Probing for Representation Manifolds in Superposition

author.name: Alexander Modell

entry.summary: Introduces the Manifold Probe for discovering representation manifolds in superposition in LLMs, generalizing linear probes to learn multi-dimensional feature spaces. Demonstrates causal influence by steering Llama 2-7b's completions about temporal knowledge.

entry.title: State Contamination in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents

author.name: Yian Wang, Agam Goyal, Yuen Chen, Hari Sundaram

entry.summary: Studies 'memory laundering' in LLM agents where toxic content gets compressed into innocuous-seeming memory summaries that evade detectors but still influence future generations, demonstrating a novel safety failure mode.

entry.title: Evaluating Deep Research Agents on Expert Consulting Work: A Benchmark with Verifiers, Rubrics, and Cognitive Traps

author.name: Tanmay Asthana, Aman Saksena, Divyansh Sahu

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for evaluating deep research agents on consulting-style analytical deliverables, testing Claude Opus 4.6, OpenAI o3-deep-research, and Gemini 3.1 Pro deep-research on 42 expert-authored prompts with rubric-based scoring.

entry.title: EnvFactory: Scaling Tool-Use Agents via Executable Environments Synthesis and Robust RL

author.name: Minrui Xu, Zilin Wang, Mengyi DENG, Zhiwei Li, Zhicheng Yang, Xiao Zhu, Yinhong Liu, Boyu Zhu, Baiyu Huang, Chao Chen, Heyuan Deng, Fei Mi, Lifeng Shang, Xingshan Zeng, Zhijiang Guo

entry.summary: Introduces EnvFactory, a framework that automatically synthesizes executable environments and realistic training data for tool-use RL agents. Addresses the bottleneck of scalable environment creation and generates natural human-intent queries rather than over-specified instructions.

entry.title: Artificial Intolerance: Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation Skews Large Language Model Decision-Making

author.name: Jen-tse Huang, Didi Zhou, Faith Kamau, Amy Oh, Anne R. Links, Mark Dredze, Mary Catherine Beach, Somnath Saha

entry.summary: Demonstrates that stigmatizing language in clinical notes causes all nine evaluated frontier LLMs to exhibit substantial bias in clinical decision-making, with effects scaling with stigma intensity across four medical conditions.

entry.title: Language-Switching Triggers Take a Latent Detour Through Language Models

author.name: Francis Kulumba, Wissam Antoun, Th\'eo Lasnier, Beno\^it Sagot, Djam\'e Seddah

entry.summary: Identifies a three-phase circuit underlying a language-switching backdoor attack in an 8B-parameter LLM: early attention composition, mid-layer propagation in an orthogonal subspace, and final-layer MLP conversion to target language logits.

entry.title: Firefly: Illuminating Large-Scale Verified Tool-Call Data Generation from Real APIs

author.name: Yuxuan Lu, Ziyi Wang, Yingzhou Lu, Yisi Sang, Jiri Gesi, Xianfeng Tang, Yimeng Zhang, Zhenwei Dai, Hui Liu, Hanqing Lu, Chen Luo, Qi He, Benoit Dumoulin, Jing Huang, Dakuo Wang

entry.summary: Presents FireFly, a pipeline for generating verified tool-call training data from real-world MCP servers by inverting the synthesis pipeline: exploring APIs first, then synthesizing tasks backward from observed outcomes to guarantee label correctness.

entry.title: $f$-Trajectory Balance: A Loss Family for Tuning GFlowNets, Generative Models, and LLMs with Off- and On-Policy Data

author.name: Jake Fawkes, Jason Hartford

entry.summary: Extends trajectory balance loss for GFlowNets to the full family of f-divergences, showing that on-policy gradients correspond to the f-divergence while off-policy the loss retains the same global minimizer. Provides theoretical unification of training objectives.

entry.title: Latent Video Prediction Learns Better World Models

author.name: Ali J Alrasheed, Aryan Yazdan Parast, Basim Azam, James Bailey, Naveed Akhtar

entry.summary: Presents systematic study comparing four video foundation models (V-JEPA 2.1, V-JEPA 2, VideoPrism, VideoMAEv2) across five robustness axes, finding that latent-prediction models consistently outperform pixel-prediction models as world models.

entry.title: CPMobius: Iterative Coach-Player Reasoning for Data-Free Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ran Li, Zeyuan Liu, Yinghao Chen, Bingxiang He, Jiarui Yuan, Zixuan Fu, Weize Chen, Jinyi Hu, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: Introduces CPMöbius, a data-free RL framework for training reasoning LLMs through Coach-Player collaboration, where a coach generates problems and a player solves them, eliminating dependence on human-curated training data.

entry.title: SURGE: Approximation-free Training Free Particle Filter for Diffusion Surrogate

author.name: Lifu Wei, Yinuo Ren, Naichen Shi, Yiping Lu

entry.summary: Introduces URGE, a derivative-free inference-time scaling algorithm for diffusion models that performs path-wise importance reweighting via Girsanov change of measure. Requires no score, Hessian, or PDE evaluation, just multiplicative weights and periodic resampling.

entry.title: Breakeven complexity: A new perspective on neural partial differential equation solvers

author.name: Yijing Zhang, Nicholas Roberts, Tanya Marwah, Mikhail Khodak

entry.summary: Proposes 'breakeven complexity' - a metric counting forward solves before a neural PDE solver becomes cost-effective relative to classical solvers, accounting for up-front training costs and the fact that classical solvers can also produce low-fidelity solutions.

entry.title: A Few GPUs, A Whole Lotta Scale: Faithful LLM Training Emulation with PrismLLM

author.name: Shaoke Xi, ChonLam Lao, Boyi Jia, Jiaqi Gao, Zhipeng Zhang, Jiamin Cao, Brian Sutioso, Erci Xu, Minlan Yu, Kui Ren, Yong Li, Zhengping Qian, Ennan Zhai, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Presents PrismLLM, a system for faithfully emulating large-scale LLM training behavior on just a few GPUs, enabling engineers to reproduce production behaviors for debugging and optimization without requiring full-scale clusters.

entry.title: GRASP: Learning to Ground Social Reasoning in Multi-Person Non-Verbal Interactions

author.name: Junho Kim, Xu Cao, Houze Yang, Bikram Boote, Ana Jojic, Fiona Ryan, Bolin Lai, Sangmin Lee, James M. Rehg

entry.summary: Introduces GRASP, a large-scale social reasoning dataset (290K QA pairs, 749 hours video) connecting high-level social QA with fine-grained gaze and gesture events for training MLLMs on multi-person non-verbal interaction understanding.

entry.title: A Theory of Training Profit-Optimal LLMs

author.name: Sophie Hao, William Merrill

entry.summary: Develops an economic model combining LLM scaling laws with microeconomic theory to characterize rational behavior of LLM training firms, analyzing how quality improvements translate to revenue and whether they offset training/inference costs.

entry.title: Revisiting the Adam-SGD Gap in LLM Pre-Training: The Role of Large Effective Learning Rates

author.name: Athanasios Glentis, Dawei Li, Chung-Yiu Yau, Mingyi Hong

entry.summary: Attributes the Adam-SGD performance gap in LLM pre-training to SGD's inability to sustain effective learning rates comparable to Adam's. Identifies that small gradient norms and large weight-to-gradient ratios necessitate large effective learning rates that SGD cannot maintain.

entry.title: Pointwise Generalization in Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Shaojie Li, Yunbei Xu

entry.summary: Establishes a pointwise generalization theory for deep neural networks using a Riemannian Dimension derived from learned feature representations across layers, providing hypothesis-dependent, representation-aware generalization bounds.

entry.title: Generating Pretraining Tokens from Organic Data for Data-Bound Scaling

author.name: Zichun Yu, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Introduces SynPro, a synthetic data generation framework for LLM pretraining that rephrases and reformats organic data to facilitate deeper learning when real data is limited, using RL-optimized generators.

entry.title: GIM: Evaluating models via tasks that integrate multiple cognitive domains

author.name: Rohit Patel, Alexandre Rezende, Steven McClain

entry.summary: Introduces GIM (Grounded Integration Measure), a benchmark of 820 problems where difficulty comes from integrating multiple cognitive operations over accessible knowledge rather than requiring esoteric knowledge or purely abstract reasoning. Addresses benchmark saturation.

entry.title: Roll Out and Roll Back: Diffusion LLMs are Their Own Efficiency Teachers

author.name: Fanqin Zeng, Feng Hong, Geng Yu, Huangjie Zheng, Xiaofeng Cao, Ya Zhang, Bo Han, Yanfeng Wang, Jiangchao Yao

entry.summary: Addresses the quality-speed trade-off in Diffusion LLMs by introducing revokable parallel decoding and a training method that distills reliable denoising order. Achieves significant speedups while maintaining generation quality.

entry.title: Monitoring the Internal Monologue: Probe Trajectories Reveal Reasoning Dynamics

author.name: Maciej Chrab\k{a}szcz, Aleksander Szymczyk, Marcin Sendera, Tomasz Trzci\'nski, Sebastian Cygert

entry.summary: Investigates using probes on hidden representations of reasoning models across token generation to create 'probe trajectories' that predict future model behavior. Finds trajectory-level signals are more informative than single static predictions for safety monitoring.

entry.title: Entropy-Gradient Inversion: Moving Toward Internal Mechanism of Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Junyao Yang, Chen Qian, Kun Wang, Linfeng Zhang, Quanshi Zhang, Yong Liu, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: Identifies 'Entropy-Gradient Inversion' as a robust negative correlation between token entropy and logit gradients that serves as a geometric fingerprint for reasoning capability in Large Reasoning Models. Uses this for training optimization.

entry.title: NEWTON: Agentic Planning for Physically Grounded Video Generation

author.name: Yuxiang Feng, Juncheng Wang, Chao Xu, Yijie Qian, Huihan Wang, Wenlong Hou, Yang Liu, Baigui Sun, Yong Liu, Shujun Wang

entry.summary: NEWTON identifies a 'specification bottleneck' in video generation where text prompts cannot fully specify physical dynamics, and proposes an agentic framework where video generation becomes one tool in a physics-aware planning system.

entry.title: SMCEvolve: Principled Scientific Discovery via Sequential Monte Carlo Evolution

author.name: Jiachen Jiang, Huminhao Zhu, Zhihui Zhu

entry.summary: SMCEvolve recasts LLM-driven program evolution as Sequential Monte Carlo sampling from a reward-tilted distribution, providing principled mechanisms for parent resampling, mutation acceptance, and convergence control with theoretical finite-sample complexity bounds.

entry.title: From I/O to Code with Discovery Agent

author.name: Yihong Dong, Jiaru Qian, Haoran Zhang, Peixu Wang, Binhua Li, Zhi Jin, Yongbin Li, Ge Li, Xiaokang Yang, Xue Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes DIO-Agent, a discovery agent that synthesizes programs from input-output examples (IO2Code) using evolutionary search over discrete program space guided by LLMs. This addresses the harder problem of inferring program logic from computational behavior rather than natural language descriptions.

entry.title: On the Fragility of Data Attribution When Learning Is Distributed

author.name: Xian Gao, Bo Hui, Min-Te Sun, Wei-Shinn Ku

entry.summary: Demonstrates that data attribution in distributed learning is fragile - a single participant can substantially inflate its measured attribution value while preserving global utility through latent optimization of synthetic batches.

entry.title: AI-Mediated Communication Can Steer Collective Opinion

author.name: Stratis Tsirtsis, Kai Rawal, Chris Russell, Brent Mittelstadt, Sandra Wachter

entry.summary: Shows empirically and theoretically that AI mediating human communication (e.g., editing posts on social media) can introduce directional biases and steer collective opinion formation on contested topics.

entry.title: ProxyKV: Cross-Model Proxy Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Junjie Li, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: ProxyKV proposes using a lightweight small model as an asynchronous proxy to score KV cache importance for a larger target model, bridging the gap between fast heuristic pruning and expensive high-precision methods. The HybridAxialMapper handles architectural differences between models of different sizes within the same family.

entry.title: MLReplicate: Benchmarking Autonomous Research Systems for Machine Learning Reproducibility

author.name: Sasi Kiran Gaddipati, Diyana Muhammed, Farhana Keya, Gollam Rabby, S\"oren Auer

entry.summary: MLReplicate benchmarks 6 autonomous research systems on ML reproducibility tasks from ICML 2025 outstanding papers, using dual-protocol evaluation combining automated and human assessment.

entry.title: Learning How to Cube

author.name: Ferhat Erata, Sam Kouteili, Thanos Typaldos, Timos Antonopoulos, Robert B. Jones, Byron Cook, Ruzica Piskac

entry.summary: Introduces a neuro-symbolic framework for learning SAT cubing heuristics using MCTS-based data curation and two-stage post-training (SFT+DPO) of a 4B-parameter model, surpassing frontier models on SAT competition benchmarks.

entry.title: Confidence Geometry Reveals Trace-Level Correctness in Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Shuo Liu, Ding Liu, Shi-Ju Ran

entry.summary: Shows that token-level confidence trajectories during LLM reasoning encode a geometric signature correlated with final-answer correctness, without needing access to reasoning text or hidden states.

entry.title: Why Do Reasoning Models Lose Coverage? The Role of Data and Forks in the Road

author.name: Ngoc-Hieu Nguyen, Parshin Shojaee, Phuc Minh Nguyen, Nan Zhang, Chandan K Reddy, Khoa D Doan, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates why reasoning models trained via SFT lose pass@k coverage despite improving pass@1, hypothesizing that 'forks in the road' in training data where multiple valid reasoning paths exist cause coverage shrinkage.

entry.title: Dimension-Free Convergence of Discrete Diffusion Models: Adjoint Equations Induce the Right Space

author.name: Kelvin Kan, Xingjian Li, Benjamin J. Zhang, Tuhin Sahai, Stanley Osher, Markos A. Katsoulakis

entry.summary: Develops dimension-free convergence guarantees for discrete diffusion models using an adjoint-equation framework, providing first bounds free of state space size S and applicable to both masked and uniform priors.

entry.title: The Neural Tangent Kernel for Classification

author.name: Jonathan Plenk, Sergio Calvo-Ordonez, Alvaro Cartea, Yarin Gal, Mark van der Wilk, Kamil Ciosek

entry.summary: Extends Neural Tangent Kernel theory to classification losses by identifying conditions under which wide networks remain in the lazy training regime. Shows that parameter-space regularization ensures a constant NTK during training for classification, resolving a long-standing limitation.

entry.title: SNLP: Layer-Parallel Inference via Structured Newton Corrections

author.name: Ligong Han, Kai Xu, Hao Wang, Akash Srivastava

entry.summary: SNLP (Structured Newton Layer Parallelism) proposes treating the hidden-state trace across Transformer layers as a nonlinear equation to be solved in parallel, using architecture-induced surrogate Jacobians for efficient Newton-style updates.

entry.title: Beyond Inference-Time Search: Reinforcement Learning Synthesizes Reusable Solvers

author.name: Soheyl Massoudi, Gabriel Apaza, Milad Habibi, Mark Fuge

entry.summary: Demonstrates that reinforcement learning can train code LLMs to synthesize reusable solvers for combinatorial optimization problem families, shifting reasoning cost from inference-time to training. Shows significant improvement over base-model sampling on a constrained quadratic knapsack variant.

entry.title: Post-Trained MoE Can Skip Half Experts via Self-Distillation

author.name: Xingtai Lv, Li Sheng, Kaiyan Zhang, Yichen You, Siyan Gao, Xueheng Luo, Yuxin Zuo, Yuchen Fan, Junlin Yang, Ganqu Cui, Bingning Wang, Fan Yang, Youbang Sun, Ning Ding, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces ZEDA, a framework that transforms post-trained static MoE models into dynamic ones through self-distillation, allowing easy tokens to skip half of experts during inference with minimal performance loss.

entry.title: Diffusion Models, Denoiser Architecture and Creativity

author.name: Itamar Levine, Yair Weiss

entry.summary: Investigates why diffusion models can generate creative (novel) images rather than memorizing training data, providing theoretical analysis showing creativity emerges from interaction between denoiser architecture and target distribution.

entry.title: Weak-to-Strong Elicitation via Mismatched Wrong Drafts

author.name: Wei Deng

entry.summary: Proposes using mathematically wrong drafts from a smaller model, mismatched to the current problem, to improve a stronger learner's GRPO training. The mismatch itself is shown to be an active ingredient, yielding improvements on MATH-500 and AIME benchmarks over standard on-policy GRPO.

entry.title: Feature Learning in Linear-Width Two-Layer Networks: Two vs. One Step of Gradient Descent

author.name: Behrad Moniri, Hamed Hassani

entry.summary: Provides full characterization of features learned during the second step of gradient descent in linear-width two-layer networks, going beyond single-step analysis to reveal richer spectral structure and overcome information exponent limitations.

entry.title: Scale-Invariant Neural Network Optimization: Norm Geometry and Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Jiayu Zhang, Tianyi Lin

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of scale-invariant neural network optimization methods under heavy-tailed noise with general input-output matrix norms. Establishes dimension dependence bounds and convergence guarantees for these practically important optimizers.

entry.title: Language Acquisition Device in Large Language Models

author.name: Masato Mita, Taiga Someya, Ryo Yoshida, Yohei Oseki

entry.summary: Inspired by Chomsky's Language Acquisition Device hypothesis, proposes pre-pretraining LLMs on a formal language (MP-STRUCT) encoding hierarchical composition, feature dependencies, and displacement. Shows 500-step PPT matches strong baselines in token efficiency.

entry.title: OProver: A Unified Framework for Agentic Formal Theorem Proving

author.name: David Ma, Kaijing Ma, Shawn Guo, Yunfeng Shi, Enduo Zhao, Jiajun Shi, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Gavin Cheung, Jiaheng Liu, Zili Wang

entry.summary: Presents OProver, a unified agentic framework for formal theorem proving in Lean 4 that iteratively revises failed proofs using retrieval and compiler feedback, trained through continued pretraining and iterative post-training with RL.

entry.title: Transitivity Meets Cyclicity: Explicit Preference Decomposition for Dynamic Large Language Model Alignment

author.name: Yucong Huang, Xiucheng Li, Kaiqi Zhao, Jing Li

entry.summary: Proposes the Hybrid Reward-Cyclic (HRC) model using game-theoretic decomposition to disentangle preferences into transitive and cyclic components, with Dynamic Self-Play Preference Optimization (DSPPO) for alignment to Nash equilibrium.

entry.title: Stop When Reasoning Converges: Semantic-Preserving Early Exit for Reasoning Models

author.name: Dehai Min, Giovanni Vaccarino, Huiyi Chen, Yongliang Wu, Gal Yona, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes a semantic-preserving early exit method for reasoning models that detects when reasoning has converged (semantic redundancy) rather than relying on answer-level signals. This prevents both premature exits and wasteful overthinking in chain-of-thought generation.

entry.title: Self-Improving CAD Generation Agents with Finite Element Analysis as Feedback

author.name: Guijin Son, Jehyun Park, Seyeon Park, Sunghee Ahn, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: Introduces a task formulation requiring models to produce fully assembled multi-part STEP files from engineering briefs, validated via finite element analysis (FEA). Finds that GPT-5.5 and Claude struggle with real engineering validation.

entry.title: When Vision Speaks for Sound

author.name: Xiaofei Wen, Wenjie Jacky Mo, Xingyu Fu, Rui Cai, Tinghui Zhu, Wendi Li, Yanan Xie, Muhao Chen, Peng Qi

entry.summary: Identifies an 'audio-visual Clever Hans effect' where video MLLMs appear to understand audio but actually exploit visual-acoustic correlations without verifying audio streams. Introduces Thud probing framework.

entry.title: A Distributional View for Visual Mechanistic Interpretability: KL-Minimal Soft-Constraint Principle

author.name: Guancheng Zhou, Yisi Luo, Zhengfu He, Zhenyu Jin, Xuyang Ge, Wentao Shu, Deyu Meng, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Establishes a theoretical distributional framework for visual mechanistic interpretability, modeling feature influence on natural image distributions via KL-minimal optimization. Identifies statistical biases in previous MI paradigms.

entry.title: Why We Look Where We Look: Emergent Human-like Fixations of a Foveated Visual Language Model Maximizing Scene Understanding

author.name: Shravan Murlidaran, Ziqi Wen, Sana Shehabi, Miguel P. Eckstein

entry.summary: Shows that a foveated visual language model trained to maximize scene comprehension exhibits emergent human-like fixation patterns, suggesting free-viewing fixations optimize scene understanding.

entry.title: Xiaomi EV World Model: A Joint World Model Integrating Reconstruction and Generation for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Lijun Zhou, Hongcheng Luo, Zhenxin Zhu, Cheng Chi, Mingfei Tu, Kaixin Xiong, Lei Gong, Zhanqian Wu, Zehan Zhang, Fangzhen Li, Hao Li, Yingying Shen, Jiale He, Haohui Zhu, Shan Zhao, Kai Wang, Zhiwei Zhan, Yuechuan Pu, Kaiyuan Tan, Ruiling Yang, Xianqi Wang, Tianyi Yan, Jiawei Zhou, Lei Zhang, Jingyang Zhao, Xi Zhou, Chitian Sun, Chenming Wu, Jiong Deng, Hongwei Xie, Ming Lu, Kun Ma, Long Chen, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Bing Wang, Haiyang Sun

entry.summary: Xiaomi presents a unified world model system for autonomous driving combining WorldRec (feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction from sparse queries) and WorldGen (bidirectional pretraining + causal fine-tuning for video generation). This represents a comprehensive industrial approach to world models integrating both reconstruction and generation capabilities.

entry.title: GeoFlow: Enforcing Implicit Geometric Consistency in Video Generation

author.name: Jan Ackermann, Shengqu Cai, Boyang Deng, Zhengfei Kuang, Songyou Peng, Gordon Wetzstein

entry.summary: GeoFlow introduces a geometry-consistency reward for video generation that measures whether motion is compatible with a coherent scene, using rigid flow verification for backgrounds and appearance preservation for moving objects. From Stanford (Wetzstein lab).

entry.title: NeuroMAS: Multi-Agent Systems as Neural Networks with Joint Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoran Lu, Luyang Fang, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma

entry.summary: Proposes NeuroMAS, treating multi-agent LLM systems as trainable neural-network-like architectures where agents are nodes and text signals are edges, trained via reinforcement learning rather than hand-designed workflows.

entry.title: Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh More Compute

author.name: Eugene Koran, Yejun Yun, Samantha Tetef, Benjamin Arnav, Pablo Bernabeu-P\'erez

entry.summary: Shows that combining diverse monitoring signals into ensembles significantly improves detection of misaligned AI agent actions, with diverse 3-monitor ensembles outperforming individual monitors and homogeneous ensembles on coding tasks with adversarial inputs.

entry.title: Always Learning, Always Mixing: Efficient and Simple Data Mixing All The Time

author.name: Michael Y. Hu, Apurva Gandhi, Kyunghyun Cho, Tal Linzen, Pratyusha Sharma

entry.summary: OP-Mix introduces an on-policy data mixing algorithm that treats data composition as a unified online decision-making problem throughout the model training lifecycle, including pretraining and continual learning.

entry.title: DrugSAGE:Self-evolving Agent Experience for Efficient State-of-the-Art Drug Discovery

author.name: Yikun Zhang, Xiwei Cheng, Tianyu Liu, Yuanqi Du, Wengong Jin

entry.summary: Proposes DrugSAGE, a self-evolving agent framework that accumulates and reuses experience across drug discovery tasks to efficiently build SOTA predictive models, maintaining cross-task memory of verified skills and effective strategies.

entry.title: ASRU: Activation Steering Meets Reinforcement Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jiahui Guang, Yingjie Zhu, Cuiyun Gao, Haiyan Wang, Jing Li, Di Shao, Zhaoquan Gu

entry.summary: Proposes ASRU, a multimodal LLM unlearning framework combining activation steering with reinforcement learning to achieve controllable forgetting while maintaining generation quality and avoiding hallucinated responses.

entry.title: Feedback World Model Enables Precise Guidance of Diffusion Policy

author.name: Tuo An, Jindou Jia, Gen Li, Jingliang Li, Chuhao Zhou, Pengfei Liu, Bofan Lyu, Jiaqi Bai, Xinying Guo, Geng Li, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes feedback world model for robot control that closes the loop between prediction and observation at inference time, maintaining a lightweight feedback state that corrects model predictions based on actual execution outcomes.

entry.title: Global Convergence of Sampling-Based Nonconvex Optimization through Diffusion-Style Smoothing

author.name: Zeji Yi, Chaoyi Pan, Guanya Shi, Guannan Qu

entry.summary: Establishes non-asymptotic convergence analysis for sampling-based optimization (cross-entropy method, evolutionary algorithms) by recasting them as gradient descent on smoothed objectives, revealing a coverage-optimality trade-off.

entry.title: DynMuon: A Dynamic Spectral Shaping View of Muon

author.name: Fangzhou Wu, Rikhav Shah, Sandeep Silwal, Qiuyi Zhang

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of Muon optimizer through 'spectral shaping' lens, showing that the optimal power parameter p for U*Sigma^p*V^T depends on curvature, noise, and training stage, revealing dynamic scheduling benefits.

entry.title: How Off-Policy Can GRPO Be? Mu-GRPO for Efficient LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Minghao Tian, Yunfei Xie, Chen Wei

entry.summary: Proposes Mu-GRPO that organizes RLVR training into few large sequential stages with high rollout staleness, showing GRPO can tolerate much more off-policy data than assumed, with 2.4x throughput improvement.

entry.title: OSCAR: Offline Spectral Covariance-Aware Rotation for 2-bit KV Cache Quantization

author.name: Zhongzhu Zhou, Donglin Zhuang, Jisen Li, Ziyan Chen, Shuaiwen Leon Song, Ben Athiwaratkun, Xiaoxia Wu

entry.summary: OSCAR proposes attention-aware covariance-based rotations and clipping for INT2 KV-cache quantization, with a fully deployable custom kernel. Achieves accurate 2-bit quantization by aligning with attention's actual covariance structures.

entry.title: InfoFlow: A Framework for Multi-Layer Transformer Analysis

author.name: Penghao Yu, Haotian Jiang, Zeyu Bao, Qianxiao Li

entry.summary: InfoFlow establishes that multi-layer Transformers have fundamentally different approximation capabilities from single-layer ones, proving exponential separation and identifying two structural mechanisms (iterative refinement and information routing) that explain depth benefits.

entry.title: Dual-Rate Diffusion: Accelerating diffusion models with an interleaved heavy-light network

author.name: Grigory Bartosh, David Ruhe, Emiel Hoogeboom, Jonathan Heek, Thomas Mensink, Tim Salimans

entry.summary: Dual-Rate Diffusion accelerates diffusion model inference by interleaving a heavy context encoder (evaluated sparsely) with a light denoising model at every step, matching baseline quality while significantly reducing compute on ImageNet.

entry.title: DBES: A Systematic Benchmark and Metric Suite for Evaluating Expert Specialization in Large-Scale MoEs

author.name: Jing Wang, Hongxuan Lu, Jazze Young, Shu Wang, Zhimin Xin

entry.summary: Introduces DBES, a diagnostic framework with five metrics for evaluating expert specialization in MoE models. Reveals distinct specialization paradigms: Qwen shows modular specialization while DeepSeek and GLM use distributed collaboration.

entry.title: Aligned Training: A Parameter-Free Method to Improve Feature Quality and Stability of Sparse Autoencoders (SAE)

author.name: Micha{\l} Brzozowski, Neo Christopher Chung

entry.summary: Proposes aligned training, a parameter-free reparameterization of sparse autoencoders that eliminates dead features and improves stability across training seeds by aligning encoder and decoder weights.

entry.title: The Range Shrinks, the Threat Remains: Re-evaluating LLM Package Hallucinations on the 2026 Frontier-Model Cohort

author.name: Aleksandr Churilov (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: Replicates the Spracklen et al. package hallucination study on 2026 frontier models, finding rates between 4.62-6.10% - significantly lower than older models but still present, with concerning repetition patterns enabling slopsquatting attacks.

entry.title: How does feature learning reshape the function space?

author.name: Jo\~ao Lobo, Bruno Loureiro, Long Tran-Than, Fanghui Liu

entry.summary: Precisely characterizes how the function space of a two-layer neural network evolves during gradient descent, proving that after a large gradient step the feature distribution becomes a target-dependent spiked Gaussian covariance inducing a data-adaptive kernel.

entry.title: What is Holding Back Latent Visual Reasoning?

author.name: Andr\'e G. Viveiros, Nuno Gon\c{c}alves, Andr\'e F. T. Martins, Matthias Lindemann

entry.summary: Investigates latent visual reasoning in VLMs, finding that model accuracy is unaffected when latent tokens are replaced by uninformative dummy tokens, indicating latent chain-of-thought provides minimal causal benefit.

entry.title: Can Adaptive Gradient Methods Converge under Heavy-Tailed Noise? A Case Study of AdaGrad

author.name: Zijian Liu

entry.summary: Provides first theoretical analysis of whether AdaGrad can converge under heavy-tailed gradient noise without algorithmic modifications like clipping. Takes a step toward explaining why adaptive methods work well in practice despite heavy-tailed noise.

entry.title: MixSD: Mixed Contextual Self-Distillation for Knowledge Injection

author.name: Jiarui Liu, Lechen Zhang, Yongjin Yang, Yinghui He, Yingheng Wang, Weihao Xuan, Zhijing Jin, Mona Diab

entry.summary: Proposes MixSD, a teacher-free method for knowledge injection that constructs supervision by mixing tokens from two conditionals of the base model itself - one with the new fact in context and one without - to avoid distribution shift and capability degradation.

entry.title: Multilingual jailbreaking of LLMs using low-resource languages

author.name: Dylan Marx, Marcel Dunaiski

entry.summary: Investigates multilingual jailbreaking of LLMs using low-resource African languages (Afrikaans, Kiswahili, isiXhosa, isiZulu). Finds that multi-turn conversations in these languages can achieve high harmful response rates (up to 83.6% for GPT-4o-mini).

entry.title: SD-Search: On-Policy Hindsight Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Reasoning

author.name: Yufei Ma, Zihan Liang, Ben Chen, Zhipeng Qian, Huangyu Dai, Lingtao Mao, Xuxin Zhang, Chenyi Lei, Wenwu Ou

entry.summary: Proposes SD-Search for search-augmented reasoning that derives step-level supervision from the policy itself through on-policy hindsight self-distillation, without requiring external teacher models or annotations.

entry.title: PySIFT: GPU-Resident Deterministic SIFT for Deep Learning Vision Pipelines

author.name: Sivakumar K. S., Mohammad Daniyalur Rahman, Gopi Raju Matta

entry.summary: Demonstrates that classical SIFT with DSP multi-scale pooling outperforms learned neural descriptors (HardNet, OriNet) on multiple benchmarks while being 2-18x faster, arguing for 'compose with SIFT' rather than 'replace SIFT'.

entry.title: Low Latency Gaze Tracking via Latent Optical Sensing

author.name: Yidan Zheng, Matheus Souza, Kaizhang Kang, Qiang Fu, Hadi Amata, Wolfgang Heidrich

entry.summary: Presents a gaze tracking system using passive optical encoding with a microlens array and binary mask, eliminating high-bandwidth image readout by performing feature extraction in the optical domain with a 4x4 sensor.

entry.title: Starve to Perceive: Taming Lazy Perception in VLMs with Constrained Visual Bandwidth

author.name: Yuhuan Wu, Cong Wei, Fangzhen Lin, Wenhu Chen, Haozhe Wang

entry.summary: Introduces 'Starve to Perceive' training paradigm that constrains visual bandwidth to force VLMs to develop genuine active perception capabilities rather than relying on coarse global views plus language priors (lazy perception).

entry.title: Is VLA Reasoning Faithful? Probing Safety of Chain-of-Causation

author.name: Nicanor Mayumu, Xiaoheng Deng, Patrick Mukala

entry.summary: First systematic study of faithfulness in VLA driving models, finding only 42.5% reasoning fidelity, 94 missed pedestrians, 97.7% trajectory fragility under perturbations, and 48.3% reasoning-action consistency in Alpamayo-R1-10B.

entry.title: WavFlow: Audio Generation in Waveform Space

author.name: Feiyan Zhou, Luyuan Wang, Shoufa Chen, Zhe Wang, Zhiheng Liu, Yuren Cong, Xiaohui Zhang, Fanny Yang, Belinda Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces WavFlow, a framework that generates high-fidelity audio directly in raw waveform space using flow matching, bypassing latent-space compression. Uses waveform patchification and amplitude lifting for stable optimization.

entry.title: How useful is cross-domain generalization for training LLM monitors?

author.name: Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Studies cross-domain generalization of single-token classification training for LLM monitors, finding that adjacent task training helps, instruction-following training preserves uplift while mitigating failures, and benefits transfer to thinking and summarization modes.

entry.title: ICRL: Learning to Internalize Self-Critique with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jianbo Lin, Xiaomin Yu, Yi Xin, Yifu Guo, Zhuosong Jiang, Zhongqi Yue, Weishi Wang, Heqing Zou, Chengwei Qin, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: ICRL proposes jointly training a solver and critic from a shared backbone using RL, so that critique-induced improvements become internalized as unassisted capability. The critic is rewarded based on the solver's subsequent performance gain.

entry.title: Quantization Undoes Alignment: Bias Emergence in Compressed LLMs Across Models and Precision Levels

author.name: Plawan Kumar Rath, Rahul Maliakkal

entry.summary: Comprehensive study showing that post-training quantization reintroduces bias in aligned LLMs, with controlled evaluation across three models at five precision levels on 12,148 BBQ benchmark items.

entry.title: Is One Score Enough? Rethinking the Evaluation of Sequentially Evolving LLM Memory

author.name: Songwei Dong, Zihan Chen, Chengshuai Shi, Peng Wang, Jundong Li, Cong Shen

entry.summary: Introduces SeqMem-Eval, a diagnostic evaluation framework for sequentially evolving LLM memory that goes beyond aggregate metrics to evaluate how memory states change over time, detecting failure modes like forgetting and negative transfer.

entry.title: GRLO: Towards Generalizable Reinforcement Learning in Open-Ended Environments from Zero

author.name: Shangjian Yin, Yu Fu, Yue Dong, Zhouxing Shi

entry.summary: Proposes GRLO for generalizable reinforcement learning in open-ended environments, addressing the challenge that in-domain RL training requires substantial GPU resources and domain-specific data while seeking transfer across tasks.

entry.title: Detecting Privilege Escalation in Polyglot Microservices via Agentic Program Analysis

author.name: Penghui Li, Hong Yau Chong, Yinzhi Cao, Junfeng Yang

entry.summary: Presents Neo, an agentic program analysis framework combining LLMs with classic program analysis to detect privilege escalation vulnerabilities in polyglot microservice architectures.

entry.title: Who Owns This Agent? Tracing AI Agents Back to Their Owners

author.name: Ruben Chocron, Doron Jonathan Ben Chayim, Eyal Lenga, Gilad Gressel, Alina Oprea, Yisroel Mirsky

entry.summary: Addresses the accountability gap for AI agents by proposing methods to trace harmful agents back to deploying accounts, relevant for both misconfigured benign agents and deliberately malicious ones.

entry.title: Preference Instability in Reward Models: Detection and Mitigation via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Shunchang Liu, Xin Chen, Belen Martin Urcelay, Francesco Croce

entry.summary: Analyzes preference instability in reward models using sparse autoencoders to identify unstable features, proposing SAE-based methods to detect and mitigate contradictory preferences under semantic-preserving perturbations.

entry.title: Seeking the Unfamiliar but Memorable: Conceptual Creativity as Meta-Learning

author.name: Mengye Ren

entry.summary: Proposes creativity as producing stimuli that are unfamiliar to an adaptive observer but quickly learnable, formalized as a Creator-Appraiser meta-learning pair where the Appraiser's improvement becomes the Creator's reward.

entry.title: Wavelet Flow Matching for Multi-Scale Physics Emulation

author.name: Gabriele Accarino, Juan Nathaniel, Carla Roesch, Pierre Gentine, Sara Shamekh, Duncan Watson-Parris, Viviana Acquaviva

entry.summary: Wavelet Flow Matching performs optimal-transport flow matching directly in wavelet space for physics emulation, leveraging hierarchical U-Net structure to jointly predict transport across scales without a separately trained autoencoder.

entry.title: Does Weight Decay Enhance Training Stability?

author.name: Marius Saether, Amir Kolic, Tomaso Poggio, Pierfrancesco Beneventano

entry.summary: Investigates whether weight decay stabilizes training dynamics at the Edge of Stability, finding it slows progressive sharpening and reveals architecture-dependent phase transitions (dampening in CNNs, oscillation replacement in MLPs).

entry.title: Scalable Knowledge Editing for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs via Tensor-Structured Updates

author.name: Roman Maksimov, Vladimir Aletov, Dmitry Bylinkin, Daniil Medyakov, Vladimir Solodkin, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Proposes a MEMIT-like knowledge editing framework for MoE-based LLMs that exploits tensor structure to formulate editing at the per-expert level, using Woodbury identity to avoid full matrix inversions.

entry.title: TIER: Trajectory-Invariant Execution Rewards for Multi-Step Tool Composition

author.name: Anay Kulkarni, ChiaEn Lu, Dheeraj Mekala, Jayanth Srinivasa, Gaowen Liu, Jingbo Shang

entry.summary: TIER proposes trajectory-invariant execution rewards for multi-step tool use RL, deriving supervision from function schemas and runtime execution rather than reference trajectories, providing dense interpretable feedback.

entry.title: Learning-Zone Energy: Online Data Selection for Efficient RL Post-Training

author.name: Peng Cui, Boyao Yang, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes Learning-Zone Energy (LZE) for online data selection in RL post-training of LLMs, concentrating compute on prompts at the model's active learning frontier rather than distributing uniformly across all difficulty levels.

entry.title: OpenJarvis: Personal AI, On Personal Devices

author.name: Jon Saad-Falcon, Avanika Narayan, Robby Manihani, Tanvir Bhathal, Herumb Shandilya, Hakki Orhun Akengin, Gabriel Bo, Andrew Park, Matthew Hart, Caia Costello, Chuan Li, Christopher R\'e, Azalia Mirhoseini

entry.summary: Introduces OpenJarvis, a decomposed personal AI stack that optimizes individual primitives (prompts, tools, memory, runtime) for local models, closing 25-39pp accuracy gap between cloud and local models through systematic optimization.

entry.title: FishBack: Pullback Fisher Geometry for Optimal Activation Steering in Transformers

author.name: Sihan Wang, Jiayi Zhao

entry.summary: Shows that the Fisher information metric pulled back through transformer layers deviates 97% from Euclidean in GPT-2, and derives closed-form optimal activation steering directions using this pullback geometry.

entry.title: Step-wise Rubric Rewards for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Weichu Xie, Haozhe Zhao, Wenpu Liu, Yongfu Zhu, Liang Chen, Minghao Ye, Zirong Chen, Yuqi Xu, Shuai Dong, Ziyue Wang, Xinbo Xu, Kean Shi, Ruoyu Wu, Xiaoying Zhang, Wenqi Shao, Baobao Chang, Nan Duan, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes step-wise rubric rewards for LLM reasoning that assign different rewards to individual reasoning steps rather than aggregating into a single scalar, finding 18.2% of steps in correct answers are wrong yet positively rewarded.

entry.title: Adaptive Generate-Rank-Verify: Inference-Time Search with Costly Verification

author.name: Shaddin Dughmi, Mahdi Haghifam, Yusuf Hakan Kalayci

entry.summary: Formalizes inference-time scaling with expensive verifiers as 'generative active search' - a cost-sensitive first-positive search problem. Characterizes optimal policies and provides regret bounds for adaptive generate-rank-verify pipelines common in math reasoning and code generation.

entry.title: Learning over Positive and Negative Edges with Contrastive Message Passing

author.name: Peter Pao-Huang, Charilaos I. Kanatsoulis, Michael Bereket, Jure Leskovec

entry.summary: Proposes Contrastive Message Passing (CMP) for GNNs that reasons over both positive (existing) and negative (absent) edges, with theoretical analysis proving information gain from negative edges in settings with low label rates, high homophily, and high density. Authored by Jure Leskovec's group.

entry.title: The Expressive Power of Low Precision Softmax Transformers with (Summarized) Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Moritz Br\"osamle, Stephan Eckstein

entry.summary: Proves that standard softmax Transformers with low precision (rounded activations/weights) and logarithmic depth/width can simulate Turing machines with chain-of-thought, bridging the gap between theoretical expressivity results and practical architectures.

entry.title: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?

author.name: David Chanin

entry.summary: Audits SAE benchmarks (SAEBench) and finds that two key metrics (TPP and SCR) fail reliability tests and should not be used for SAE evaluation. Other metrics show higher noise and lower discriminability than assumed.

entry.title: Generating Physically Consistent Molecules with Energy-Based Models

author.name: Christoph Griesbacher, Lea Bogensperger, Andreas Habring, Thomas Pock

entry.summary: Introduces EBMol, an energy-based model for molecular generation that learns atom-additive scalar potentials using a flow-inspired training objective, restoring the physical inductive bias of Boltzmann distributions without explicit simulation during training.

entry.title: Position: Weight Space Should Be a First-Class Generative AI Modality

author.name: Zhangyang Wang, Peihao Wang, Kai Wang

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that neural network weight spaces should be treated as a first-class generative AI modality, with model checkpoints as structured data that can be generated on demand for task adaptation.

entry.title: Bridging the Modality Bottleneck in Pathology MIL through Virtual Molecular Staining

author.name: Yucheng Xing, Pei Liu, Jingying Ma, Ruping Hong, Jiangdong Qiu, Tianyu Liu, Kai He, Ling Huang, Mengling Feng

entry.summary: Introduces MIST, a plug-in MIL projection layer for computational pathology that uses paired spatial transcriptomics during training to create virtual molecular stains, bridging the morphology-molecular gap in whole-slide analysis.

entry.title: Mechanistically Interpretable Neural Encoding Reveals Fine-Grained Functional Selectivity in Human Visual Cortex

author.name: Idan Daniel Grosbard, Mor Geva, Galit Yovel

entry.summary: Introduces MINE, a framework applying mechanistic interpretability tools to neural encoding models to identify specific image features driving voxel-level brain activity in human visual cortex.

entry.title: Voice ''Cloning'' is Style Transfer

author.name: Kaitlyn Zhou, Federico Bianchi, Martijn Bartelds, Anna Pot, Yongchan Kwon, James Zou

entry.summary: Demonstrates that voice cloning models don't faithfully clone voices but systematically apply style transfer, making cloned voices sound more authoritative, warm, and trustworthy than originals according to human annotators.

entry.title: Why Do Safety Guardrails Degrade Across Languages?

author.name: Max Zhang, Ameen Patel, Sang T. Truong, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Group IRT framework to analyze why LLM safety guardrails degrade in non-English languages, decoupling factors like language-agnostic robustness, prompt hardness, and cross-lingual safety gaps.

entry.title: Self-Distillation is Optimal Among Spectral Shrinkage Estimators in Spiked Covariance Models

author.name: Radu Lecoiu, Debarghya Mukherjee, Pragya Sur

entry.summary: Proves that s-step self-distillation achieves optimal performance among spectral shrinkage estimators for spiked covariance models, and that fewer steps are strictly suboptimal.

entry.title: Simple Approximation and Derivative Free Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models via Sequential Monte Carlo on Path Measures

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Weizhong Wang, Yinuo Ren, Jose Blanchet, Yiping Lu

entry.summary: Introduces URGE, a derivative-free inference-time scaling algorithm for diffusion models that uses path-wise importance reweighting via Girsanov change of measure, requiring no score or gradient evaluations.

entry.title: Prompt2Fingerprint: Plug-and-Play LLM Fingerprinting via Text-to-Weight Generation

author.name: Sixu Chen, Xiang Chen, Hongyao Yu, Jiaxin Hong, Hao Fang, Shuoyang Sun, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: Introduces Prompt2Fingerprint (P2F), a framework that uses text-to-weight generation to create unique fingerprints for LLMs without requiring separate fine-tuning for each identity. This reformulates fingerprinting as conditional parameter generation, dramatically improving scalability of model provenance tracking.

entry.title: Vision-OPD: Learning to See Fine Details for Multimodal LLMs via On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Qianhao Yuan, Jie Lou, Xing Yu, Hongyu Lin, Le Sun, Xianpei Han, Yaojie Lu

entry.summary: Proposes Vision-OPD, a self-distillation framework that transfers a multimodal LLM's stronger regional perception (from evidence-centered crops) to its full-image policy, addressing the regional-to-global perception gap in fine-grained visual understanding.

entry.title: PluRule: A Benchmark for Moderating Pluralistic Communities on Social Media

author.name: Zoher Kachwala, Bao Tran Truong, Rasika Muralidharan, Haewoon Kwak, Jisun An, Filippo Menczer

entry.summary: Introduces PluRule, a multimodal, multilingual benchmark for community-specific content moderation across 1,989 Reddit communities with 2,885 rules in 9 languages. Shows even GPT-5.2 struggles significantly with pluralistic rule application.

entry.title: Mixture of Experts for Low-Resource LLMs

author.name: Ori Bar Joseph, Smadar Arvatz, Noam Kayzer, Dan Revital, Sarel Weinberger

entry.summary: Analyzes routing dynamics in Mixture-of-Experts models for low-resource languages (Hebrew), finding that both Transformer and hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE models exhibit 'deep-layer routing collapse' for underrepresented languages. Continual pre-training on balanced bilingual data corrects this imbalance.

entry.title: KVDrive: A Holistic Multi-Tier KV Cache Management System for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Jian Lin, Jiazhi Mi, Zicong Hong, Haodong Wang, Qianli Liu, Haodyue Zhang, Peng Li, Song Guo

entry.summary: Presents KVDrive, a multi-tier KV cache management system spanning GPU, DRAM, and SSD for long-context LLM inference. Takes a systems perspective on the transfer bottleneck rather than pursuing greater sparsity.

entry.title: Algorithmic Cultivation: How Social Media Feeds Shape User Language

author.name: Olivia Pal, Agam Goyal, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: Large-scale longitudinal study (235M posts, 4M users on Bluesky) examining how sustained algorithmic feed exposure shapes user language. Uses quasi-experimental matching to compare users exposed to News, Science, and Blacksky feeds.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory Correction from Cross-layer Evidence for Hallucination Reduction

author.name: Tej Sanibh Ranade

entry.summary: Introduces TRACE, a method for hallucination reduction that uses cross-layer evidence from intermediate transformer layers, showing that factual evidence is sometimes present internally but suppressed in later layers.

entry.title: Scalable Environments Drive Generalizable Agents

author.name: Jiayi Zhang, Fanqi Kong, Guibin Zhang, Maojia Song, Zhaoyang Yu, Jianhao Ruan, Jinyu Xiang, Bang Liu, Chenglin Wu, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that generalizable AI agents require environment scaling (expanding diverse rule-sets) rather than just collecting more trajectories in fixed environments. Proposes a taxonomy for environment diversity.

entry.title: Auditing Multimodal LLM Raters: Central Tendency Bias in Clinical Ordinal Scoring

author.name: Jiaqing Zhang, Sandeep Elluri, Bhanu Cherukuvada, Yonah Joffe, Jessica Sena, Miguel Contreras, Scott Siegel, Subhash Nerella, Catherine Price, Parisa Rashidi

entry.summary: Audits multimodal LLMs as clinical raters, finding that all LLM families exhibit central tendency bias (compressing toward middle scores) on ordinal clinical scales, even when overall accuracy appears competitive.

entry.title: Mamba-VGGT: Persistent Long-Sequence Video Geometry Grounded Transformer via External Sliding Window Mamba Memory

author.name: Tianchen Deng, Zhenxiang Xiong, Nailin Wang, Fangjinhua Wang, Jiuming Liu, Jianfei Yang, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: Extends Visual Geometry Grounded Transformers (VGGT) with a Sliding Window Mamba memory module to handle long video sequences for 3D reconstruction without catastrophic geometric forgetting. Combines selective state-space modeling with external memory tokens to maintain global geometric priors.

entry.title: Rethinking Point Clouds as Sequences: A Causal Next-Token Predictive Learning Framework

author.name: Yumeng Yao, Jingzhi Dong, Haowen Gu, Tao Chen, Zonghan Wu, Xiaoshui Huang, Yazhou Yao

entry.summary: Introduces PointNTP, reformulating point cloud pre-training as causal next-token prediction in latent space, aligning 3D understanding with the predictive pre-training paradigm used in language models.

entry.title: GEM: Gaussian Evolution Model for Occupancy Forecasting and Motion Planning

author.name: Cheng Chen, Hao Huang, Saurabh Bagchi

entry.summary: Proposes GEM, a Gaussian Evolution Model for non-autoregressive occupancy forecasting using continuous 4D Gaussian primitives with learned dynamics for autonomous driving.

entry.title: Imaging Hidden Objects with Consumer LiDAR via Motion Induced Sampling

author.name: Siddharth Somasundaram, Aaron Young, Akshat Dave, Adithya Pediredla, Ramesh Raskar

entry.summary: Demonstrates non-line-of-sight imaging with consumer LiDAR devices using multi-frame fusion inspired by burst photography and synthetic aperture radar, overcoming low signal quality limitations.

entry.title: Vision Foundation Models as Generalist Tokenizers for Image Generation

author.name: Anlin Zheng, Qi Han, Xin Wen, Chuofan Ma, Lanxi Gong, Gang Yu, Xiangyu Zhang, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: Proposes VFMTok, a generalist image tokenizer built on frozen vision foundation models with region-adaptive quantization to eliminate spatial redundancy and semantic reconstruction objectives. Works in both discrete and continuous latent spaces.

entry.title: Incantation: Natural Language as the Action Interface for Multi-Entity Video World Models

author.name: Shangwen Zhu, Qianyu Peng, Zhao Pu, Zhilei Shu, Xiangrui Ke, Zhaohu Xing, Zizhao Tong, Zeqing Wang, Xinyu Cui, Huangji Wang, Jian Zhao, Yeying Jin, Fan Cheng, Ruili Feng

entry.summary: Incantation proposes natural language as the action interface for interactive video world models, enabling per-frame multi-entity control and cross-entity concept transfer without fixed rendering pipelines. First model with per-0.25s natural language conditioning.

entry.title: Leveraging Latent Visual Reasoning in Silence

author.name: Dongyao Zhu, Zhen Wang, Xi Xiao, Han Jiang, Saeed Vahidian, Wei-Lun Chao, Tanya Berger-Wolf, Yu Su, Raju Vatsavai, Jianyang Gu

entry.summary: Investigates whether latent visual reasoning tokens are necessary at inference time, finding that replacing them with noise causes little degradation. Argues their value is as training-time scaffolding rather than inference-time format, with latent tokens guiding learning.

entry.title: Watermarks Attack Watermarks: Re-Watermarking as a Generic Removal Strategy

author.name: Maria Bulychev, Neil G. Marchant, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein

entry.summary: Demonstrates that watermarks can be used to attack other watermarks - re-watermarking as a generic removal strategy. Shows that the properties sought by watermarks (imperceptible changes triggering detectors) are analogous to attack requirements.

entry.title: WorldArena 2.0: Extending Embodied World Model Benchmarking on Modality, Functionality and Platform
