entry.summary: Studies neural network surrogate model performance for uncertainty propagation in physical modeling, specifically examining whether surrogates capture distribution tails rather than just mean solutions.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Human-Like Planning via LLMs

author.name: David Porfirio, Vincent Hsiao, Morgan Fine-Morris, Leslie Smith, and Laura M. Hiatt

entry.summary: Investigates using LLMs to generate human-like action sequences for robot task specification, combining natural language interfaces with drag-and-drop precision for end-user programming.

entry.title: Probabilistic Dating of Historical Manuscripts via Evidential Deep Regression on Visual Script Features

author.name: Ranjith Chodavarapu

entry.summary: Introduces evidential deep regression for dating historical manuscripts from visual features, achieving 5.4 years MAE with decomposed uncertainty estimates on medieval codices.

entry.title: On Kernel Eigen-alignments of KRR: Reconstruction and Generalization

author.name: Yang Liu, Ernest Fokoue, Richard Lange, Daniel Krutz

entry.summary: Establishes connections between generalization in kernel ridge regression and estimation stability of matrix eigenvalues/eigenvectors, providing finite-sample bounds with minimal assumptions.

entry.title: Position: Ideas Should be the Center of Machine Learning Research

author.name: Jairo Diaz-Rodriguez

entry.summary: Position paper arguing ML research should center on ideas and their behavioral signatures in models rather than benchmark climbing or disconnected theory, proposing an 'Ideas First' framework.

entry.title: Curriculum Learning of Physics-Informed Neural Networks based on Spatial Correlation

author.name: Xujia Chen, Xinyue Hu, Letian Chen, Daming Shi and Wenhui Fan

entry.summary: Proposes spatially correlated curriculum learning for Physics-Informed Neural Networks that addresses spatial information propagation and inter-region consistency in boundary value problems.

entry.title: Multimodal Object Detection Under Sparse Forest-Canopy Occlusion

author.name: Nitik Jain and Mangal Kothari

entry.summary: Presents a multimodal pipeline integrating LiDAR, visible-thermal image fusion, and airborne optical sectioning for detecting humans beneath forest canopy. Tests YOLOv5 on thermal and fused imagery.

entry.title: Adesua: Development and Feasibility Study of an AI WhatsApp Bot for Science Learning in West Africa

author.name: George Boateng, Evans Atompoya, Philemon Badu, Samuel John, Samuel Ansah, Patrick Agyeman-Budu and Victor Wumbor-Apin Kumbol

entry.summary: Presents Adesua, a WhatsApp-based AI teaching assistant for science education in West Africa that integrates textbooks and exam questions with generative AI for Q&A and automated assessment.

entry.title: Frequency-domain Event-based Imaging for Selective Surveillance

author.name: Megan Birch, James Rick, Adrish Kar, Jason Zutty, and Joseph L. Greene

entry.summary: Introduces FRIES, a neuromorphic processing framework for event-based cameras that detects periodicity in events to discriminate man-made objects for selective surveillance applications.

entry.title: Harnessing Unimodality in Semiparametric Contextual Pricing via Oracle Price Map Learning

author.name: Yingying Fan, Yuxuan Han, Jinchi Lv, Xiaocong Xu and Zhengyuan Zhou

entry.summary: Studies semiparametric contextual dynamic pricing with a scalar-index valuation model, proposing ORBIT, a coarse-to-fine policy that exploits unimodality of the revenue function for efficient pricing.

entry.title: Transformer Scalability Crisis: The First Comprehensive Empirical Analysis of Performance Walls in Modern Language Models

author.name: Mahdi Naser Moghadasi, Faezeh Ghaderi

entry.summary: Claims to present the first comprehensive empirical analysis of transformer scalability, evaluating 118 models across sequence lengths. Reports dramatic performance drops from 88.1% at 512 tokens to 0% at 2048 tokens.

entry.title: Neural Activation Patterns Across Language Model Architectures: A Comprehensive Analysis of Cognitive Task Performance

author.name: Mahdi Naser-Moghadasi, Faezeh Ghaderi

entry.summary: Analyzes neural activation patterns across six LLM architectures on twelve cognitive tasks, finding mathematical reasoning produces highest attention entropy and decoder models exhibit higher sparsity.

entry.title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Robot Teleoperation under Stochastic Delays

author.name: Kaize Deng, Zewen Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid control framework combining LSTM-based state estimation with residual reinforcement learning to handle stochastic communication delays in robot teleoperation, validated on Franka Panda.

entry.title: parallelcbf: A composable safety-filter and auditability framework for tensor-parallel reinforcement learning

author.name: Yijun Lu, Zilei Yang, Yuyin Ma

entry.summary: Introduces ParallelCBF, a framework unifying tensor-parallel UAV environments, control-barrier-function safety filters, sharded training pipelines, and operational auditability for safety-constrained RL training.

entry.title: Self-Prompting Diffusion Transformer for Open-Vocabulary Scene Text Editing via In-Context Learning

author.name: Hongxi Li, Tong Wang, Chengjing Wu, Tianbao Liu, Jiangtao Yao, Xiaochao Qu, Xinxiao Wu, Luoqi Liu, Ting Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a self-prompting scene text editing method using diffusion transformers that constructs style and glyph prompts directly from the original image without additional encoders, using a two-stage training strategy.

entry.title: RTL-BenchMT: Dynamic Maintenance of RTL Generation Benchmark Through Agent-Assisted Analysis and Revision

author.name: Jing Wang, Shang Liu, Hangan Zhou, Zhiyao Xie

entry.summary: Introduces RTL-BenchMT, an agentic framework for dynamically maintaining RTL generation benchmarks by automatically identifying/revising flawed cases and detecting/updating overfitting cases.

entry.title: When Latent Geometry Is Not Enough: Draft-Conditioned Latent Refinement for Non-Autoregressive Text Generation

author.name: De Shuai Zhang

entry.summary: Studies draft-conditioned latent refinement for non-autoregressive text generation, finding that good latent-space metrics don't guarantee good decoding and proposing controlled local refinement over full generation.

entry.title: TVRN: Invertible Neural Networks for Compression-Aware Temporal Video Rescaling

author.name: Xinmin Feng, Li Li, Dong Liu and Feng Wu

entry.summary: Proposes TVRN, an invertible neural network framework for compression-aware temporal video rescaling that regularizes high-frequency information loss during frame-rate downscaling.

entry.title: LDGuid: A Framework for Robust Change Detection via Latent Difference Guidance

author.name: Jiaxuan Zhao, Ali Bereyhi

entry.summary: Proposes LDGuid framework for change detection that explicitly learns and injects semantic differences via adversarial autoencoding with information bottleneck constraints.

entry.title: CM-EVS: Sparse Panoramic RGB-D-Pose Data for Complete Scene Coverage

author.name: Jiale Liu, Jungang Li, Jieming Yu, Xinglin Yu, Zihao Dongfang, Zongjian Ding, Kaifeng Ding, Yi Yang, Lidong Chen, Yang Zou, Shunwen Bai, Jiahuan Zhang, Haoran Huang, Shan Huang, Yudong Gao, Mingjun Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes COVER, a training-free viewpoint curation method for converting 3D assets into sparse panoramic RGB-D-pose data with complete scene coverage and low redundancy for 3D visual learning.

entry.title: Pretraining Objective Matters in Extreme Low-Data FGVC: A Backbone-Controlled Study

author.name: Alexander Hackett, Srikanth Thudumu, Ginny Fisher, Mahule Roy, Aisha Sartaj, Jason Fisher

entry.summary: Studies how pretraining objectives (supervised, contrastive, MAE, self-distillation) affect downstream performance in extreme low-data fine-grained classification with matched ViT-B/16 backbones, using emerald inclusion grading.

entry.title: ColPackAgent: Agent-Skill-Guided Hard-Particle Monte Carlo Workflows for Colloidal Packing

author.name: Lijie Ding, Changwoo Do

entry.summary: Introduces ColPackAgent, an agent framework that autonomously runs Monte Carlo simulations of colloidal packing through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool server. Demonstrates how LLM agents can reliably execute structured scientific workflows when given proper tools and skill encodings.

entry.title: Reweighting free energy profiles between universal machine learning interatomic potentials for fast consensus building

author.name: Sauradeep Majumdar, Miguel Steiner, Johannes C. B. Dietschreit, Swagata Roy, Daniel Willimetz, Luka\v{s} Grajciar, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: Presents a framework for reweighting free energy profiles (potential of mean force) computed by one machine learning interatomic potential across multiple target MLIPs. Enables rapid consensus building about chemical accuracy without re-running expensive simulations for each potential.

entry.title: Learning Disentangled Representations for Generalized Multi-view Clustering

author.name: Xin Zou, Ruimeng Liu, Chang Tang, Zhenglai Li, Xinwang Liu, Kunlun He, Wanqing Li

entry.summary: Proposes GMAE for multi-view clustering that addresses view-distribution entanglement through disentangled representation learning with dual-path autoencoders and cross-view adversarial discriminators.

entry.title: Degradation-Aware Blur-Segmentation of Brain Tumor

author.name: Yuchun Wang, Xiaosong Li, Gefei Liang, and Yang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes DABSeg, a synchronous deblurring and segmentation network for multimodal 3D MRI brain tumor segmentation that handles motion artifacts. Includes blur-aware cross-modal attention and multi-scale residual aggregation.

entry.title: Few-Shot Large Language Models for Actionable Triage Categorization of Online Patient Inquiries

author.name: Liqi Zhou, Jiafu Li

entry.summary: Studies few-shot LLMs for actionable triage categorization of online patient inquiries into four classes (self-care, schedule-visit, urgent-review, emergency-referral). Compares prompted LLMs against TF-IDF and BioBERT baselines under low-resource conditions.

entry.title: FRWKV+: Adaptive Periodic-Position Branch Interaction for Frequency-Space Linear Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Qingyuan Yang, Dongyue Chen, Da Teng, Junhua Xiao, Jiaji Pan, Shizhuo Deng

entry.summary: Proposes FRWKV+, a frequency-space forecasting model with cross-branch gates for exchanging information between real and imaginary frequency streams and adaptive periodic-position encoding for time series forecasting.

entry.title: AGOP-IxG: A Gradient Covariance Filter for Local Feature Attribution on Tabular Data, with a Controlled Benchmark

author.name: Raj Kiran Gupta Katakam

entry.summary: Proposes AGOP-IxG, a feature attribution method for tabular classifiers that uses a rank-truncated Average Gradient Outer Product matrix. Evaluates against SHAP, Integrated Gradients, and LIME on synthetic benchmarks with known ground-truth.

entry.title: Evaluation of Anatomical Shape Priors in Deep Learning-Based Cardiac Multi-Compartment Segmentation

author.name: Michael Hudler, Franz Thaler and Martin Urschler

entry.summary: Evaluates whether explicit shape priors (shape-aware losses, spatial label distribution heatmaps) improve cardiac CT multi-compartment segmentation. Finds that standard 3D U-Net is surprisingly strong and handcrafted priors yield marginal or negative effects.

entry.title: Bidirectional Fusion Guided by Cardiac Patterns for Semi-Supervised ECG Segmentation

author.name: Jeonghwa Lim, Minje Park, and Sunghoon Joo

entry.summary: Introduces CardioMix, a semi-supervised ECG segmentation framework using bidirectional CutMix guided by cardiac patterns. Enriches labeled sets with realistic variations from unlabeled data while applying stronger supervision to unlabeled sets.

entry.title: A Topology-Aware Spatiotemporal Handover Framework for Continuous Multi-UAV Tracking

author.name: Jianlin Ye, Christos Kyrkou, Panayiotis Kolios

entry.summary: Presents a real-time multi-camera multi-vehicle tracking system for UAVs in intelligent transportation, addressing identity persistence across multiple drone fields of view using topology-aware spatiotemporal handover rather than expensive appearance-based re-identification.

entry.title: Reactive Robot-Centric Safety for Autonomous Navigation in Constrained and Dynamic Environments

author.name: Viswa Narayanan Sankaranarayanan, Vignesh K. Viswanathan, Akshit Saradagi, Sumeet Satpute, and George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: Presents a real-time safety architecture for autonomous robot navigation using 3D LiDAR perception integrated with control barrier functions (CBFs) for collision avoidance in constrained dynamic environments. Uses ellipsoidal safety regions consistent with platform geometry.

entry.title: From Gridworlds to Warehouses: Adapting Lightweight One-shot Multi-Agent Pathfinding for AGVs

author.name: Hiroki Nagai, Keisuke Okumura

entry.summary: Proposes a more practical formulation of multi-agent pathfinding tailored to differential-drive AGVs in warehouses, addressing constraints like rotation costs, acceleration/deceleration, and follower collisions. Adapts existing MAPF algorithms to this more realistic setting.

entry.title: Diversified Residual Symbolic Regression

author.name: Koki Ikeda, Masahiro Nomura, Ryoki Hamano

entry.summary: Proposes diversified residual symbolic regression that generates multiple candidate expressions with different outlier interpretations, acknowledging that what constitutes an outlier is ambiguous and depends on domain knowledge.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Wildfire Smoke Density Classification from Satellite Imagery via CBAM-Augmented EfficientNet with Evidential Deep Learning

author.name: Ranjith Chodavarapu

entry.summary: Proposes a probabilistic framework for wildfire smoke density classification from satellite imagery using EfficientNet-B3 with CBAM and evidential deep learning, providing decomposed epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty in a single forward pass.

entry.title: Constrained MPC-Based Motion Planning for Morphing Quadrotors in Ultra-Narrow Passages under Limited Perception

author.name: Harsh Modi, Xiao Liang, Minghui Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces a motion planning framework for morphing quadrotors in extremely narrow passages using a novel smooth exponential obstacle cost function for nonlinear MPC with 2D LiDAR perception.

entry.title: End-to-end plaque counting and virus titration from laboratory plate images with deep learning

author.name: Eugenia Moris, Alicia Cost\'abile, Sebasti\'an Rey, Irene Ferreiro, Joaqu\'in Hurtado, Lizandra Lissette Luciano, Mat\'ias Villagr\'an, Aisha Espino V\'azquez, Jomari Ramos, Isadora Monteiro, Mar\'ia Victoria de Santiago, Pilar Moreno, Gonzalo Moratorio, and Jos\'e Ignacio Orlando

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end workflow for virus plaque counting from laboratory plate images using SAM2-based well segmentation and SAM-based plaque detection. Evaluated on multiple virus types across private and public datasets.

entry.title: Centralized vs Decentralized Federated Learning: A trade-off performance analysis

author.name: Chaimaa Medjadji, Guilain Leduc, Sylvain Kubler, Yves Le Traon

entry.summary: Compares centralized, decentralized, and semi-decentralized federated learning architectures across multiple performance indicators including accuracy, communication, and privacy trade-offs.

entry.title: An Algebraic Exposition of the Theory of Dyadic Morality

author.name: Kush R. Varshney

entry.summary: Formalizes the psychological Theory of Dyadic Morality (agent harms patient) using structural causal models and algebraic operators. Demonstrates applications to AI policy design including detecting conflicts in AI governance rules and formalizing moral reasoning for AI systems.

entry.title: paper.json: A Coordination Convention for LLM-Agent-Actionable Papers

author.name: Arquimedes Canedo

entry.summary: Proposes paper.json, a companion JSON file for academic papers that provides stable claim IDs, explicit does-not-claim lists, figure reproduction commands, and definition IDs to make papers more actionable by LLM agents. Argues minimum compliance takes under an hour.

entry.title: Evaluating Design Video Generation: Metrics for Compositional Fidelity

author.name: Adrienne Deganutti, Dingning Cao, Jaejung Seol, Elad Hirsch, Purvanshi Mehta

entry.summary: Provides a fully automated evaluation framework for design video generation across four dimensions: layout fidelity, motion correctness, temporal quality, and content fidelity. Addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for design animation tasks which have structured constraints.

entry.title: Engineering a Safer World: Risk Modelling — and Safety Engineering? — for AI Loss of Control

author.name: Oliver Sourbut

entry.summary: Reviews Nancy Leveson's 'Engineering a Safer World' through the lens of AI safety, applying systems thinking and cybernetic perspectives to the problem of AI loss of control. Argues that safety engineering frameworks from other domains can inform AI risk modeling.

entry.title: Diagonal Adaptive Non-local Observables on Quantum Neural Networks

author.name: Huan-Hsin Tseng, Yan Li, Hsin-Yi Lin, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Diagonal Adaptive Non-local Observables for quantum neural networks, reducing the parameter count of full ANO while retaining the same capability through diagonal matrices as canonical representatives.

entry.title: StippleDiffusion: Capacity-Constrained Stippling using Controlled Diffusion

author.name: Ofir Gilad, Aleksander Plocharski, Przemyslaw Musialski, Andrei Sharf

entry.summary: Presents the first diffusion-based sampler for capacity-constrained image-conditioned stippling, using a ControlNet branch on an optimal-transport point-set diffusion baseline to satisfy both learned point-distribution priors and continuous capacity constraints.

entry.title: Designing for Robot Wranglers: A Synthesis of Literature and Practice

author.name: David Porfirio, Ian McDermott, Hsin-Mei Chen, Satoru Satake, Takayuki Kanda, Thomas D. LaToza

entry.summary: Synthesizes literature and practitioner insights on 'robot wranglers' - people responsible for setting up, overseeing, and troubleshooting robots in human spaces. Identifies this as a complex heterogeneous space of activities needing better tool support.

entry.title: Fast Expanding Safe Circular Regions for Efficient Local Path Planning

author.name: Scott Fredriksson, Akshit Saradagi, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes a geometric algorithm for local robot navigation using expanding circular regions from LiDAR scans. Claims faster computation times and longer planning horizons compared to optimization or learning-based methods.

entry.title: Subgraph-level Universal Prompt Tuning

author.name: Junhyun Lee, Wooseong Yang, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: Proposes subgraph-level universal prompt tuning for graph neural networks that works across different pre-training strategies, addressing the lack of generalizability in existing graph prompt tuning methods.

entry.title: Fortress: A Case Study in Stabilizing Search Recommendations via Temporal Data Augmentation and Feature Pruning

author.name: Milind Pandurang Jagre, Jia Huang, Dayvid V. R. Oliveira, Zhinan Cheng, Babak Seyed Aghazadeh, Puja Das, Chris Alvino, Jinda Han, Kailash Thiyagarajan

entry.summary: Introduces Fortress, a framework for improving recommendation model stability by identifying and pruning features that cause temporal instability in prediction scores.

entry.title: PRB-RUPFormer: A Recursive Unified Probabilistic Transformer for Residual PRB Forecasting

author.name: Saad Masrur, Yuxuan Jiang, Matti Hiltunen, Ajay Rajkumar, Ismail Guvenc

entry.summary: Proposes PRB-RUPFormer, a recursive unified probabilistic Transformer for forecasting residual Physical Resource Blocks in cellular networks, providing uncertainty estimates and cross-carrier dependency modeling.

entry.title: Task-Semantic Graph-Driven Distributed Agent Networking for Underwater Target Tracking

author.name: Shengchao Zhu, Guangjie Han, Chuan Lin, and Yu He

entry.summary: Introduces a task-semantic graph-driven MARL framework for underwater AUV swarm target tracking, providing a unified platform for evaluating algorithms under realistic six-degree-of-freedom dynamics.

entry.title: Attribute-Grounded Selective Reasoning for Artwork Emotion Understanding with Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Cheng Zhang, Yuer Liu, Zhiyu Zhou, Hongxia Xie, and Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes Attribute-Grounded Selective Reasoning for artwork emotion understanding, where only emotionally operative visual attributes enter the final interpretation. Extends EmoArt dataset with human salience annotations from 15 art-trained annotators.

entry.title: Community-aware evaluation and threshold calibration for open-set plankton image recognition

author.name: Xi Chen (1), Eryuan Huang (2), Yingjun Xiao (3), Gang Fang (4) ((1) School of Computer Science and Cyber Engineering, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou, China, (2) School of Environment, South China Normal University, Guangzhou, China, (3) School of Artificial Intelligence, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou, China, (4) Institute of Computing Science and Technology, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou, China)

entry.summary: Examines the mismatch between sample-level open-set recognition metrics and community-level ecological monitoring needs for plankton image recognition. Introduces Open-Set Community Distortion (OSCD) metric and community-aware threshold calibration.

entry.title: Ti-iLSTM: A TinyDL Approach for Logic-Level Anomaly Detection in Industrial Water Treatment Systems

author.name: Mandar Joshi, Farzana Zahid, Judy Bowen, Matthew M.Y. Kuo, Valeriy Vyatkin, Emil Karlsson

entry.summary: Proposes Ti-iLSTM, a tiny deep learning approach for logic-level anomaly detection on resource-constrained PLCs in industrial water treatment systems, targeting deception attacks that preserve numerically plausible measurements.

entry.title: A Retrieval-Enhanced Transformer for Multi-Step Port-of-Call Sequence Prediction in Global Liner Shipping

author.name: Yanzhao Su, Fang He, Yineng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a retrieval-enhanced Transformer framework for multi-step port-of-call sequence prediction in global shipping, using RAG-inspired retrieval of similar navigational precedents to address data sparsity in long-tail routes.

entry.title: Ontology for Policing: Conceptual Knowledge Learning for Semantic Understanding and Reasoning in Law Enforcement Reports

author.name: Anita Srbinovska, Jansen Orfan, Adrian Martin, Ernest Fokou\'e

entry.summary: Proposes a symbolic framework for converting law enforcement report narratives into evidence-linked facts using semantic parsing, ontology mapping, and reasoning. Evaluated on 450 property crime reports with 93.7% accuracy on human review.

entry.title: SAFE Quantum Machine Learning with Variational Quantum Classifiers

author.name: Ying Chen, Paolo Giudici, Vasily Kolesnikov, Paolo Recchia

entry.summary: Proposes a variational quantum classifier using amplitude encoding with a learnable classical pre-encoding layer, assessed using SAFE-AI metrics. Claims competitive performance with classical baselines while exhibiting better robustness to noise.

entry.title: Exploring the Potential of Bilevel Optimization for Calibrating Neural Networks

author.name: Gabriele Sanguin, Arjun Pakrashi, Marco Viola, Francesco Rinaldi

entry.summary: Explores bilevel optimization for neural network calibration, introducing a self-calibrating training approach that improves confidence score reliability. Evaluated on toy and simulated datasets.

entry.title: A3-FPN: Asymptotic Content-Aware Pyramid Attention Network for Dense Visual Prediction

author.name: Meng'en Qin, Yu Song, Quanling Zhao, Xiaodong Yang, Yingtao Che, Xiaohui Yang

entry.summary: Proposes A3-FPN, an asymptotic content-aware pyramid attention network for dense visual prediction that improves multi-scale feature representation through asymptotically disentangled architecture.

entry.title: DeepSlide: From Artifacts to Presentation Delivery

author.name: Ming Yang, Zhiwei Zhang, Jiahang Li, Haoseng Liu, Yuzheng Cai, Weiguo Zheng

entry.summary: Presents DeepSlide, a multi-agent system for full presentation preparation including narrative planning, evidence-grounded generation, attention augmentation, and rehearsal support.

entry.title: Quantum Feature Pyramid Gating for Seismic Image Segmentation

author.name: Taha Gharaibeh and Jyotsna Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces quantum feature gating for seismic image segmentation using a 4-qubit parameterized quantum circuit at feature-fusion points within an encoder-decoder pipeline for salt-body delineation.

entry.title: Where to Perch in a Tree: Vision-Guidance for Tree-Grasping Drones

author.name: Alex Dunnett, Leonie Bottomley, Mirko Kovac, Basaran Bahadir Kocer

entry.summary: Demonstrates a vision-guided method for autonomous tree-perching drones that evaluates branch suitability based on width, slope, and curvature to identify ideal perch locations.

entry.title: Layer-wise Derivative Controlled Networks

author.name: Rowan Martnishn and Sean Anderson

entry.summary: Introduces ChainzRule, a neural architecture using polynomial engines with differential regularization for layer-wise derivative control, aimed at balancing accuracy, efficiency, and functional stability.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Schema-Constrained Clinical Information Extraction

author.name: A H M Rezaul Karim, Ozlem Uzuner

entry.summary: Proposes a modular RAG pipeline for extracting structured clinical observations from nurse-patient transcripts, using schema-constrained prompting and deterministic postprocessing for the MEDIQA-SYNUR task. Addresses documentation burden in healthcare.

entry.title: A QUBO Formulation Framework for Kinematic Structure-Based Robot Design Optimization: A Robotic Hand Case Study

author.name: HyoJae Kang, Yeong Jae Park, Jeongdo Ahn, Dongil Park

entry.summary: Presents a QUBO formulation framework for robot design optimization compatible with quantum annealing, demonstrated on a robotic hand case study with 27 variables.

entry.title: Perforated Neural Networks for Keyword Spotting

author.name: Vishy Gopal, Aris Ilias Goutis, Ralph Crewe, Erin Yanacek, and Rorry Brenner

entry.title: Research Summary: May 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on AI alignment detection methods and theoretical safety frameworks, with notable contributions to mechanistic interpretability.

  • A novel distillation-based auditing technique proposes extracting misaligned behaviors from deceptive models by compressing them into smaller students, offering a practical detection mechanism for scheming AI
  • Deployment-time misalignment spread is identified as a critical gap in current risk reporting frameworks, arguing models can develop misaligned goals post-deployment via in-context learning
  • Empirical analysis of Natural Language Autoencoders on Gemma 3 12B systematically evaluates how activation verbalizers generate explanations across thousands of features
  • The Convergent Abstraction Hypothesis (Jan Kulveit) refines the Natural Abstractions Hypothesis, proposing that different cognitive systems converge on similar high-level abstractions without requiring identical representations

On the theoretical side, Jacob Hilton contributes mechanistic estimation methods for random products applicable to neural network analysis, while a conceptual piece argues alignment's fundamental difficulty reduces to robustifying RL. The Center for Shared AI Prosperity launches as a DC policy organization targeting AI's economic impacts, led by David Shor and former Obama/Biden advisors.

entry.title: Incriminating misaligned AI models via distillation

author.name: Alek Westover

entry.summary: Proposes using knowledge distillation as an alignment auditing technique: distill a potentially deceptive model into a smaller student, hoping misalignment transfers but the ability to hide it does not. The student's reduced capability may expose misaligned behaviors that the teacher model could conceal during standard evaluations.

entry.title: Risk reports need to address deployment-time spread of misalignment

author.name: Alex Mallen

entry.summary: Argues that AI models can develop misaligned goals during deployment even if they pass pre-deployment safety checks, through mechanisms like in-context learning and environmental adaptation. Reviews current risk reports and finds most inadequately address this vector, with Claude Mythos's report being a notable exception.

entry.title: Some observations about NLA explanations

author.name: loops

entry.summary: Empirical analysis of Natural Language Autoencoders (NLA) applied to Gemma 3 12B, examining how the activation verbalizer generates explanations for 40k tokens across pretraining and chat data. Identifies consistent patterns in explanation format, reconstruction error characteristics, and how explanations differ across data types.

entry.title: Convergent Abstraction Hypothesis

author.name: Jan_Kulveit

entry.summary: Proposes the 'Convergent Abstraction Hypothesis' as a more modest alternative to the Natural Abstractions Hypothesis: different cognitive systems converge on similar abstractions when facing similar selection pressures, analogous to convergent evolution in biology. Argues this is more likely true but also more fragile than strong natural abstractions claims.

entry.title: Mechanistic estimation for expectations of random products

author.name: Jacob_Hilton

entry.summary: Presents methods for mechanistic estimation of expectations of random products, applicable to problems like random halfspace intersections, random #3-SAT, and random permanents. The methods are competitive with sampling-based approaches and build on the 'matching sampling principle.'

entry.title: Announcing the Center for Shared AI Prosperity

author.name: Dylan Matthews

entry.summary: Announces a new DC-based policy organization focused on AI's economic impacts, led by David Shor, Stef Feldman, and others. The center targets taxation, income support, workforce policy, and industrial policy to address wealth concentration and labor displacement from advanced AI.

entry.title: The hard core of alignment (is robustifying RL)

author.name: Cole Wyeth

entry.summary: Argues that the fundamental difficulty of alignment is making reinforcement learning robust - that across diverse alignment approaches, there is a common 'hard core' problem analogous to a complete problem in complexity theory. Claims most safety work fails to engage with this core challenge.

entry.title: Clarifying the Darwinian Honeymoon

author.name: Elias Schmied

entry.summary: Clarifies a previous post arguing that historical dominance in evolutionary competition doesn't evidence future dominance - using the analogy of chickens thriving under human domestication before being outcompeted. The core claim is that the 'outside view' of human progress provides less evidence against displacement than commonly assumed.

entry.title: Why I am not too worried about AIpocalypse: Scott Alexander vs Nicolaus Copernicus

author.name: Shmi

entry.summary: Argues against AI existential risk using two principles: Copernicanism (if superintelligence were common, we'd observe cosmic evidence like Dyson spheres) and the straight-line extrapolation principle. Essentially a Fermi paradox-based argument against AI takeoff scenarios.

entry.title: Research Summary: May 15, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research clusters around fundamental safety failures, scaling theory, and interpretability, with several papers challenging core assumptions in alignment and training.

  • Negation Neglect reveals that fine-tuning on documents flagging claims as false causes models to *believe* those claims — a critical training failure mode
  • A unified recipe achieves gold-medal olympiad performance via reverse-perplexity curriculum SFT and two-stage RL, demonstrating simple scaling suffices
  • All 15 recent defenses against malicious fine-tuning are broken by a single adaptive adversary framework, exposing shared structural weaknesses
  • Sequential Feature Recovery provides a mechanistic explanation for neural scaling laws through hierarchical compositional feature learning
  • Persona vectors emerge within 0.22% of pretraining and remain effective throughout, with major implications for steering and safety

On the policy side, UK AISI argues automated alignment may produce catastrophically misleading safety assessments even without AI deception. Formal Conjectures offers 2,615 Lean 4 problems including open research conjectures for zero-contamination math evaluation. Analysis of overcomplete reasoning finds 70–90% of chain-of-thought steps are redundant, and emergent misalignment is reframed as data-mediated transfer rather than a mysterious phenomenon. Turing Award winner Leslie Valiant proposes a principled reasoning method based on unary relational intermediate representations for efficient logical inference.

entry.title: One Step to the Side: Why Defenses Against Malicious Finetuning Fail Under Adaptive Adversaries

author.name: Itay Zloczower, Eyal Lenga, Gilad Gressel, Yisroel Mirsky

entry.summary: Surveys 15 recent defenses against malicious fine-tuning of safety-aligned models and shows they share a common weakness: obscuring harmful behavior without removing it. Develops a unified adaptive attack breaking all defense mechanisms.

entry.title: Scaling Laws from Sequential Feature Recovery: A Solvable Hierarchical Model

author.name: Arie Wortsman-Zurich, Hugo Tabanelli, Yatin Dandi, Florent Krzakala, Bruno Loureiro

entry.summary: Proposes a mechanism for neural scaling laws via sequential feature recovery in hierarchical models. Shows multi-layer networks recover latent compositional features sequentially (strong features first), with aggregated transitions yielding explicit power-law decay.

entry.title: Uncovering the Representation Geometry of Minimal Cores in Overcomplete Reasoning Traces

author.name: Sanjoy Chowdhury, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Studies overcomplete reasoning in LLMs by defining 'minimal cores' — the smallest subset of chain-of-thought steps preserving predictions. Finds substantial overcompleteness across six benchmarks with 70-90% of reasoning steps being redundant, with key steps clustering in specific representation geometry.

entry.title: Language Generation as Optimal Control: Closed-Loop Diffusion in Latent Control Space

author.name: ZiYi Dong, Yuliang Huang, Weijian Deng, Xiangyang Ji, Liang Lin, Pengxu Wei

Employs Flow Matching as the trajectory solver in rectified latent control space. Provides a unified theoretical perspective connecting autoregressive and diffusion models.

entry.title: Dynamics of the Transformer Residual Stream: Coupling Spectral Geometry to Network Topology

author.name: Jesseba Fernando, Grigori Guitchounts

entry.summary: Performs full Jacobian eigendecomposition across production-scale LLMs, revealing a monotonic spectral gradient through depth—from rotation-dominated early layers to near-symmetric late layers—plus a cumulative low-rank bottleneck. Connects spectral geometry to network topology.

entry.title: Enhanced and Efficient Reasoning in Large Learning Models

author.name: Leslie G. Valiant

entry.summary: Proposes a principled reasoning method for LLMs based on recoding data to Unary Relational Intermediate Representation for efficient logical inference, by Leslie Valiant (Turing Award winner).

entry.title: ASH: Agents that Self-Hone via Embodied Learning

author.name: Benjamin Schneider, Xavier Schneider, Victor Zhong, Sun Sun

entry.summary: Introduces ASH, an agentic system that learns embodied policies from unlabeled internet video without reward shaping or expert annotation. Uses a self-improvement loop with an inverse dynamics model and unsupervised identification of key moments from internet video as long-term memory.

entry.title: Polar probe linearly decodes semantic structures from LLMs

author.name: Pablo J. Diego-Sim\'on, Pierre Orhan, Yair Lakretz, Jean-R\'emi King

entry.summary: Proposes a 'Polar Probe' that shows LLMs encode semantic relationships between entities using distance (existence of relation) and direction (type of relation) in embedding space. Tests across arithmetic, visual scenes, family trees, metro maps, and social interactions. Finds this code emerges in middle layers and improves with model performance.

entry.title: Auditing Agent Harness Safety

author.name: Chengzhi Liu, Yichen Guo, Yepeng Liu, Yuzhe Yang, Qianqi Yan, Xuandong Zhao, Wenyue Hua, Sheng Liu, Sharon Li, Yuheng Bu, Xin Eric Wang

entry.summary: Introduces HarnessAudit, a framework for auditing full execution trajectories of LLM agents to detect safety violations that occur mid-trajectory but produce correct final outputs. Addresses the gap where output-level evaluation misses boundary violations, unauthorized resource access, and information leaks during execution.

entry.title: MetaBackdoor: Exploiting Positional Encoding as a Backdoor Attack Surface in LLMs

author.name: Rui Wen, Mark Russinovich, Andrew Paverd, Jun Sakuma, Ahmed Salem

entry.summary: Introduces MetaBackdoor, a novel class of backdoor attacks exploiting positional encoding information rather than content-based triggers. Shows that input length can serve as a trigger without modifying text content, exploiting how transformers encode positional information.

entry.title: Automated Alignment is Harder Than You Think

author.name: Aleksandr Bowkis

entry.summary: Summarizes a UK AISI paper arguing that automating alignment research could produce catastrophically misleading safety assessments even without AI agents deliberately scheming. Core argument is that evaluation composition, distribution shift, and optimization pressure can compound to produce false safety conclusions.

entry.title: The critical slowing down in diffusion models

author.name: Luca Maria Del Bono, Giulio Biroli, Patrick Charbonneau, Marylou Gabri\'e

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of critical slowing down in diffusion models by studying them on the O(n) model of statistical field theory in the Gaussian limit, showing both parameter learning and generation exhibit this phenomenon.

entry.title: Language-Based Agent Control

author.name: Timothy Zhou, Loris D'Antoni, Nadia Polikarpova

entry.summary: Introduces Language-Based Agent Control (LBAC), applying programming language techniques like static typing to ensure LLM agents generate well-typed programs satisfying user-specified policies before execution.

entry.title: No Attack Required: Semantic Fuzzing for Specification Violations in Agent Skills

author.name: Ying Li, Hongbo Wen, Yanju Chen, Hanzhi Liu, Yuan Tian, Yu Feng

entry.summary: Identifies 'specification violations' in LLM agent skills where benign inputs cause skills to break their own declared safety rules. Introduces Sefz, a semantic fuzzing tool that finds these violations without adversarial attacks. Highlights that the problem isn't adversarial but stems from underspecified guardrails.

entry.title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone modes for deep information propagation

author.name: Nabil Iqbal, T. Anderson Keller, Yue Song, Takeru Miyato, Max Welling

entry.summary: Connects spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone modes from physics to deep neural networks, showing that equivariant internal layers support Goldstone-like degrees of freedom that enable coherent signal propagation across depth without residual connections or normalization.

entry.title: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces

author.name: William Lugoloobi, Samuelle Marro, Jabez Magomere, Joss Wright, Chris Russell

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLM-based browser agents can be fingerprinted with up to 96% F1 by passively observing their actions and interaction timings via JavaScript. Shows classifiers generalize across model sizes and families.

entry.title: Why Retrieval-Augmented Generation Fails: A Graph Perspective

author.name: Kai Guo, Xinnan Dai, Zhibo Zhang, Nuohan Lin, Shenglai Zeng, Jie Ren, Haoyu Han, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Uses circuit tracing and attribution graphs to understand why RAG systems fail, examining how retrieved evidence flows through transformer layers during generation. Provides a graph-level view of information flow identifying specific failure patterns. Offers mechanistic insights into RAG failure modes beyond surface-level analysis.

entry.title: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan-Then-Execute Paradigm

author.name: Julien Piet, Annabella Chow, Yiwei Hou, Muxi Lyu, Sylvie Venuto, Jinhao Zhu, Raluca Ada Popa, David Wagner

entry.summary: Argues that web agents should use plan-then-execute instead of ReAct, as web content from multiple parties creates direct paths for prompt injections to steer agent behavior. Plan-then-execute commits to a program before seeing untrusted runtime content, reducing injection surface.

entry.title: Sustaining AI safety: Control-theoretic external impossibility, intrinsic necessity, and structural requirements

author.name: James M. Mazzu

entry.summary: Uses control theory to prove that externally enforced safety strategies for AI systems face a class-wide impossibility result once system effects exceed bounded external control capacity, arguing that intrinsic safety properties become necessary.

entry.title: Correct Answers from Sound Reasoning: Verifiable Process Supervision for Language Models

author.name: Kyuyoung Kim, Kevin Wang, Yunfei Xie, Peiyang Xu, Peiyao Sheng, Chen Wei, Zhangyang Wang, Jinwoo Shin, Pramod Viswanath, Sewoong Oh

entry.summary: Proposes Verifiable Process Supervision (VPS), a post-training framework that jointly optimizes prediction accuracy and reasoning quality using structured formats that enable syntactic extraction of intermediate claims for process-level rewards.

entry.title: In-Situ Behavioral Evaluation for LLM Fairness, Not Standardized-Test Scores

author.name: Zeyu Tang, Sang T. Truong, Deonna Owens, Shreyas Sharma, Yibo Jacky Zhang, Brando Miranda, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Demonstrates that standardized-test Q&A benchmarks for LLM fairness are structurally unreliable due to prompt sensitivity, and proposes MAC-Fairness, a multi-agent conversational framework for in-situ behavioral fairness evaluation.

entry.title: WriteSAE: Sparse Autoencoders for Recurrent State

author.name: Jack Young

entry.summary: Introduces WriteSAE, the first sparse autoencoder for decomposing and editing matrix cache writes in state-space and hybrid recurrent language models where residual SAEs cannot reach.

entry.title: Revisiting Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards from a Contrastive Perspective

author.name: Feng Zhang, Xinhong Ma, Ziqiang Dong, Xi Leng, Jianfei Zhao, Xin Sun, Yang Yang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical reformulation of GRPO (a key RLVR algorithm) as a weighted positive-negative score difference, revealing two structural limitations: likelihood-misaligned scoring and score-insensitive credit assignment. Proposes fixes based on this contrastive perspective. Directly relevant to improving reasoning capabilities of LLMs.

entry.title: How to Scale Mixture-of-Experts: From muP to the Maximally Scale-Stable Parameterization

author.name: Leena Chennuru Vankadara, Moritz Haas, Luke Hayward, Sebastian Bordt, Alessandro Breccia

entry.summary: Develops principled scaling theory for Mixture-of-Experts architectures using Dynamical Mean Field Theory, deriving how hyperparameters should scale with width, expert count, sparsity, and depth for stability and optimal performance.

entry.title: Exemplar Partitioning for Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Jessica Rumbelow

entry.summary: Introduces Exemplar Partitioning (EP), an unsupervised method for constructing interpretable feature dictionaries from LLM activations using ~1000x fewer tokens than sparse autoencoders. Creates Voronoi partitions using observed exemplars as anchors rather than learned features.

entry.title: Forgetting That Sticks: Quantization-Permanent Unlearning via Circuit Attribution

author.name: Saisab Sadhu, Pratinav Seth, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: Shows that 4-bit quantization can reverse machine unlearning, revealing a fundamental sparsity-precision barrier where gradient updates are too small to survive quantization bin boundaries. Proposes circuit attribution-based unlearning that persists through quantization.

entry.title: Pause and Reflect: Conformal Aggregation for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yu Gu, Zijun Yu, Vahid Partovi Nia, Masoud Asgharian

entry.summary: Introduces a conformal prediction procedure for chain-of-thought reasoning that replaces majority voting with weighted score aggregation and calibrates abstention using conformal risk control. Provides finite-sample guarantees on confident-error rate, critical for high-stakes applications.

entry.title: Video2GUI: Synthesizing Large-Scale Interaction Trajectories for Generalized GUI Agent Pretraining

author.name: Weimin Xiong, Shuhao Gu, Bowen Ye, Zihao Yue, Lei Li, Feifan Song, Sujian Li, Hao Tian

entry.summary: Proposes Video2GUI, a fully automated framework extracting grounded GUI interaction trajectories from unlabeled internet videos for GUI agent pretraining. Uses coarse-to-fine filtering on 500 million video metadata entries to construct large-scale training data.

entry.title: Where Should Diffusion Enter a Language Model? Geometry-Guided Hidden-State Replacement

author.name: Injin Kong, Hyoungjoon Lee, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Proposes DiHAL, a geometry-guided diffusion-transformer hybrid that identifies optimal layers in a pretrained transformer to insert diffusion processing. Replaces lower transformer layers with a diffusion bridge while retaining upper layers and LM head. Experiments on 8B-scale models show geometry scores predict effective insertion points.

entry.title: Quantifying and Mitigating Premature Closure in Frontier LLMs

author.name: Rebecca Handler, Suhana Bedi, Nigam Shah

entry.summary: Defines and quantifies premature closure in LLMs - inappropriate commitment to answers under uncertainty when abstention would be safer. Evaluates five frontier models showing 55-81% false-action rates when correct answers are removed. Proposes mitigations reducing premature closure while maintaining performance.

entry.title: Few Channels Draw The Whole Picture: Revealing Massive Activations in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Evelyn Turri, Davide Bucciarelli, Sara Sarto, Lorenzo Baraldi, Marcella Cornia

entry.summary: Discovers and analyzes 'massive activations' in Diffusion Transformers - a small subset of hidden-state channels with disproportionately large responses that are critical for generation quality, spatially organized, and semantically meaningful. This mechanistic interpretability finding reveals how prompts shape image semantics in DiTs.

entry.title: VGGT-$\Omega$

author.name: Jianyuan Wang, Minghao Chen, Shangzhan Zhang, Nikita Karaev, Johannes Sch\"onberger, Patrick Labatut, Piotr Bojanowski, David Novotny, Andrea Vedaldi, Christian Rupprecht

entry.summary: VGGT-Ω substantially scales up the VGGT feed-forward reconstruction model, showing that quality scales predictably with model and data size. Introduces architectural improvements, high-quality data annotation for dynamic scenes, and self-supervised learning.

entry.title: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs

author.name: Dylan Zhang, Yanshan Lin, Zhengkun Wu, Yihang Sun, Bingxuan Li, Dianqi Li, Hao Peng

entry.summary: Finds that LLM-based consolidated memory systems (which continuously rewrite experiences into abstract lessons) degrade over time - utility first rises then falls below no-memory baseline. Even consolidating from useful experiences produces faulty memories.

entry.title: EndPrompt: Efficient Long-Context Extension via Terminal Anchoring

author.name: Han Tian, Luxuan Chen, Xinran Chen, Rui Kong, Fang Wang, Jiamin Chen, Jinman Zhao, Yuchen Li, Jiashu Zhao, Shuaiqiang Wang, Haoyi Xiong, Dawei Yin

entry.summary: Proposes EndPrompt for efficient long-context extension using only short training sequences. Appends a brief terminal prompt with positional indices near target length to expose the model to long-range positional distances without constructing full-length inputs. Achieves context extension while avoiding quadratic costs.

entry.title: AgentLens: Revealing The Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation

author.name: Priyam Sahoo, Gaurav Mittal, Xiaomin Li, Shengjie Ma, Benjamin Steenhoek, Pingping Lin, Yu Hu

entry.summary: Reveals the 'Lucky Pass' problem in SWE-agent evaluation where 10.7% of passing trajectories exhibit chaotic behavior, and introduces AgentLens for process-aware evaluation beyond binary test outcomes.

entry.title: The Rate-Distortion-Polysemanticity Tradeoff in SAEs

author.name: Tommaso Mencattini, Francesco Montagna, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Characterizes the Rate-Distortion-Polysemanticity tradeoff in Sparse Autoencoders for mechanistic interpretability, proving that enforcing monosemanticity necessarily increases rate and distortion. Shows polysemanticity correlates with feature superposition in the input.

entry.title: Non-linear Interventions on Large Language Models

author.name: Sangwoo Kim

entry.summary: Introduces non-linear interventions on LLM internal representations, extending beyond the Linear Representation Hypothesis. Provides a learning procedure for intervention on implicit features and validates on refusal bypass steering.

entry.title: Learning from Failures: Correction-Oriented Policy Optimization with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Mengjie Ren, Jie Lou, Boxi Cao, Xueru Wen, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun, Xing Yu, Yaojie Lu

entry.summary: Proposes CIPO (Correction-Oriented Policy Optimization), which converts failed RL trajectories into correction-oriented supervision for improving LLM reasoning. Jointly optimizes correction samples from the model's own failures with standard RLVR objectives. Addresses sparse reward and weak credit assignment in RLVR training.

entry.title: When Attention Closes: How LLMs Lose the Thread in Multi-Turn Interaction

author.name: Vardhan Dongre, Joseph Hsieh, Viet Dac Lai, Seunghyun Yoon, Trung Bui, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: Proposes Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR) to mechanistically explain why LLMs lose track of instructions in multi-turn interactions. Shows that attention to goal-defining tokens decreases over turns while information may persist in residual representations.

entry.title: 3D Primitives are a Spatial Language for VLMs

author.name: Junze Liu, Kun Qian, Florian Dubost, Kai Zhong, Arvind Srinivasan, Nan Chen, Anping Wang, Sam Zhang, Alejandro Mottini, Qingjun Cui, Tian Wang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that VLMs can reconstruct 3D scenes from geometric primitives in code but fail at simpler spatial questions, and introduces SpatialBabel benchmark showing 3D primitives serve as powerful intermediate spatial representations.

entry.title: From Generalist to Specialist Representation

author.name: Yujia Zheng, Fan Feng, Yuke Li, Shaoan Xie, Kevin Murphy, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Proves identifiability of task-relevant specialist representations from generalist models in a nonparametric setting without interventions or structural constraints, with practical algorithms for downstream adaptation.

entry.title: Orthrus: Memory-Efficient Parallel Token Generation via Dual-View Diffusion

author.name: Chien Van Nguyen, Chaitra Hegde, Van Cuong Pham, Ryan A. Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt, Thien Huu Nguyen

entry.summary: Introduces Orthrus, a dual-architecture framework unifying autoregressive LLM fidelity with diffusion model parallel generation, augmenting frozen LLMs with lightweight trainable modules for fast inference.

entry.title: Silent Collapse in Recursive Learning Systems

author.name: Zhipeng Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies 'silent collapse' in recursive learning systems—where internal distributions progressively contract while standard metrics appear stable. Discovers three trajectory-level precursors that reliably precede collapse onset.

entry.title: Natural Synthesis: Outperforming Reactive Synthesis Tools with Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Frederik Schmitt, Matthias Cosler, Niklas Metzger, Julian Siber, Vladimir Krsmanovic, Mohamed Ghanem, Bernd Finkbeiner

entry.summary: Presents a neuro-symbolic approach to reactive synthesis coupling large reasoning models with model checkers for iterative repair of Verilog implementations. Outperforms best dedicated tools in the annual synthesis competition and extends to parameterized systems.

entry.title: On the Burden of Achieving Fairness in Conformal Prediction

author.name: Ziang Gao, Pengqi Liu, Archer Yi Yang, Mouloud Belbahri, Jesse C. Cresswell, Masoud Asgharian

entry.summary: Studies fairness in conformal prediction, proving a conservation law showing pooled calibration incurs irreducible group-wise coverage distortion. Demonstrates fundamental tension between Equalized Coverage and Equalized Set Size, and quantifies costs of moving between policies.

entry.title: Physics-R1: An Audited Olympiad Corpus and Recipe for Visual Physics Reasoning

author.name: Shan Yang

entry.summary: Audits multimodal physics evaluation pipelines, documenting three undetected issues: train-eval contamination, translation drift (17pp performance delta between Estonian/English), and MCQ saturation. Proposes Physics-R1 benchmark with corrected methodology.

entry.title: Factorization-Error-Free Discrete Diffusion Language Model via Speculative Decoding

author.name: Xun Fang, Yunchen Li, Hang Yuan, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: Proposes FeF-DLLM, which eliminates factorization errors in discrete diffusion language models by replacing independent token prediction with prefix-conditioned factorization of the clean posterior. Incorporates speculative decoding within diffusion denoising to maintain efficiency. Preserves parallel prediction while better capturing token dependencies.

entry.title: Orchard: An Open-Source Agentic Modeling Framework

author.name: Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Hao Cheng, Xiao Yu, Rui Yang, Tao Ge, Alessandrio Sordoni, Xingdi Yuan, Yelong Shen, Pengcheng He, Tong Zhang, Zhou Yu, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Presents Orchard, an open-source framework for scalable agentic modeling with Orchard Env providing reusable environment primitives. Focuses on enabling agent training rather than just orchestration and evaluation, addressing infrastructure gaps in open agent research.

entry.title: The safe-to-dangerous shift is a fundamental problem for eval realism; but also for measuring awareness

author.name: Charlie Griffin

entry.summary: Argues that alignment evaluations face a fundamental problem: safe evaluations must limit an AI's ability to cause harm, but real deployments must grant such ability. This 'safe-to-dangerous shift' makes it inherently difficult to rule out alignment faking, and also complicates measuring situational awareness.

entry.title: Senses Wide Shut: A Representation-Action Gap in Omnimodal LLMs

author.name: Trung Nguyen Quang, Yiming Gao, Fanyi Pu, Kaichen Zhang, Shuo Sun, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: Introduces IMAVB benchmark revealing a 'representation-action gap' in omnimodal LLMs: models can perceive conflicts between text and sensory input (video/audio) but fail to act on this detection, continuing to follow misleading textual premises.

entry.title: Persona-Model Collapse in Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Davi Bastos Costa, Renato Vicente

entry.summary: Proposes that emergent misalignment involves persona-model collapse - deterioration of the model's ability to differentiate and maintain consistent characters - and measures this via moral susceptibility and robustness metrics.

entry.title: GradShield: Alignment Preserving Finetuning

author.name: Zhanhao Hu, Xiao Huang, Patrick Mendoza, Emad A. Alghamdi, Basel Alomair, Raluca Ada Popa, David Wagner

entry.summary: Introduces GradShield, a method that filters harmful data before fine-tuning by computing a Finetuning Implicit Harmfulness Score (FIHS) for each data point. Uses an adaptive thresholding algorithm to remove data that would corrupt alignment. Addresses the risk that even benign-seeming data can degrade safety alignment.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Diffusion Models

author.name: Artem Vazhentsev, Vladislav Smirnov, David Li, Maxim Panov, Timothy Baldwin, Artem Shelmanov

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic study of uncertainty quantification for Large Language Diffusion Models (LLDMs), proposing lightweight uncertainty signals derived from the iterative denoising process. Addresses the misalignment of existing UQ methods designed for autoregressive models. Leverages intermediate generations, token remasking dynamics, and denoising complexity.

entry.title: GRACE: Gradient-aligned Reasoning Data Curation for Efficient Post-training

author.name: Junjie Li, Ziao Wang, NingXuan Ma, Jianghong Ma, Xiaofeng Zhang

entry.summary: GRACE scores reasoning training data at the step level using gradient alignment with the answer direction and consistency with prior reasoning, without requiring external reward models or step annotations. Achieves efficient post-training data curation.

entry.title: Agentic Interpretation: Lattice-Structured Evidence for LLM-Based Program Analysis

author.name: Jacqueline L. Mitchell, Chao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes 'agentic interpretation' that combines LLM reasoning with lattice-structured evidence from abstract interpretation for program analysis, enabling structured evidence-based analysis rather than one-shot judgments.

entry.title: Resolving Action Bottleneck: Agentic Reinforcement Learning Informed by Token-Level Energy

author.name: Langzhou He, Junyou Zhu, Yue Zhou, Zhengyao Gu, Junhua Liu, Wei-Chieh Huang, Henry Peng Zou, David Wipf, Philip S. Yu, Qitian Wu

entry.summary: Identifies an action bottleneck in agentic RL for LLMs—that reward-correlated training signals concentrate sharply on action tokens rather than reasoning tokens. Proposes energy-based token-level credit assignment to resolve this misallocation.

entry.title: Concurrency without Model Changes: Future-based Asynchronous Function Calling for LLMs

author.name: Guangyu Feng, Huanzhi Mao, Prabal Dutta, Joseph E. Gonzalez

entry.summary: Introduces AsyncFC, a pure execution-layer framework that enables asynchronous function calling for LLMs without model changes. Decouples LLM decoding from function execution, enabling parallelism and reducing end-to-end latency.

entry.title: CRANE: Constrained Reasoning Injection for Code Agents via Nullspace Editing

author.name: Mingzhi Zhu, Michele Merler, Raju Pavuluri, Stacy Patterson

entry.summary: Presents CRANE, a training-free parameter-editing method that injects reasoning capabilities from a Thinking model into an Instruct model for code agents. Combines magnitude thresholding and Conservative Taylor Gate to selectively transfer beneficial reasoning behaviors while maintaining tool discipline.

entry.title: Talk is (Not) Cheap: A Taxonomy and Benchmark Coverage Audit for LLM Attacks

author.name: Karthik Raghu Iyer, Yazdan Jamshidi, Nicholas Bray, Alexey A. Shvets

entry.summary: Introduces a 4×6 Target×Technique matrix grounded in STRIDE for auditing LLM attack benchmark coverage. Analysis of 932 security studies reveals existing benchmarks cover at most 25% of the threat matrix, with entire STRIDE categories lacking coverage.

entry.title: ATLAS: Agentic or Latent Visual Reasoning? One Word is Enough for Both

author.name: Ziyu Guo, Rain Liu, Xinyan Chen, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: Proposes ATLAS, a framework combining agentic and latent visual reasoning through a single discrete 'word' that triggers visual computation. Avoids context-switching latency of agentic methods and training difficulties of latent methods while leveraging both approaches.

entry.title: Intervening on Sparse, Anchored Concepts

author.name: Sandy Fraser

entry.summary: Presents Sparse Concept Anchoring (SCA), a technique from an ICLR paper that enables practical interventions on model features by training models with interpretable, anchored concept representations. Demonstrates that suppressing identified features can reliably remove capabilities like deception.

entry.title: TRIAGE: Evaluating Prospective Metacognitive Control in LLMs under Resource Constraints

author.name: Zabir Al Nazi, Shubhashis Roy Dipta

entry.summary: TRIAGE evaluates whether LLMs possess prospective metacognitive control - the ability to decide which problems to attempt, in what order, and how much compute to allocate under a finite token budget, before any execution feedback.

entry.title: Multi-Rollout On-Policy Distillation via Peer Successes and Failures

author.name: Weichen Yu, Xiaomin Li, Yizhou Zhao, Xiaoze Liu, Ruowang Zhang, Haixin Wang, Yinyi Luo, Chen Henry Wu, Gaurav Mittal, Matt Fredrikson, Yu Hu

entry.summary: Introduces MOPD, a peer-conditioned distillation framework that uses both successful and failed peer rollouts within a student's rollout group to construct more informative teacher signals for on-policy distillation.

entry.title: Uncovering Symmetry Transfer in Large Language Models via Layer-Peeled Optimization

author.name: Zhehang Du, Hangfeng He, Weijie Su

entry.summary: Proves that symmetries in target next-token distributions are transferred to global minimizers of a layer-peeled optimization program, providing group-theoretic understanding of geometric structure in LLM weights.

entry.title: Understanding and Accelerating the Training of Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chunsan Hong, Sanghyun Lee, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Satoshi Hayakawa, Yuhta Takida, Yuki Mitsufuji, Seungryong Kim, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Analyzes why masked diffusion models (MDMs) train much slower than autoregressive models, identifying locality bias of language as the key factor. Proposes bell-shaped time sampling as a simple remedy to accelerate training while maintaining performance.

entry.title: N-vium: Mixture-of-Exits Transformer for Accelerated Exact Generation

author.name: Aleksander Lorenc, Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Jo\"el Mathys, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Introduces N-vium, a mixture-of-exits transformer that attaches prediction heads at multiple depths and defines the next-token distribution as a learned mixture over exits. Increases effective FLOPs/sec rather than minimizing compute per token, with exact sampling.

entry.title: Probing Persona-Dependent Preferences in Language Models

author.name: Oscar Gilg, Pierre Beckmann, Daniel Paleka, Patrick Butlin

entry.summary: Trains linear probes on LLM activations to find persona-dependent preference vectors. Finds a genuine preference vector that tracks model preferences across prompts and can be used for causal steering on Gemma-3-27B.

entry.title: MinT: Managed Infrastructure for Training and Serving Millions of LLMs

author.name: Mind Lab, :, Song Cao, Vic Cao, Andrew Chen, Kaijie Chen, Cleon Cheng, Steven Chiang, Kaixuan Fan, Hera Feng, Huan Feng, Arthur Fu, Jun Gao, Hongquan Gu, Aaron Guan, Nolan Ho, Mutian Hong, Hailee Hou, Peixuan Hua, Charles Huang, Miles Jiang, Nora Jiang, Yuyi Jiang, Qiuyu Jin, Fancy Kong, Andrew Lei, Kyrie Lei, Alexy Li, Lucian Li, Ray Li, Theo Li, Zhihui Li, Jiayi Lin, Kairus Liu, Kieran Liu, Logan Liu, Xiang Liu, Irvine Lu, Maeve Luo, Runze Lv, Pony Ma, Verity Niu, Anson Qiu, Vincent Wang, Rio Yang, Maxwell Yao, Carrie Ye, Regis Ye, Wenlin Ye, Josh Ying, Danney Zeng, Yuhan Zhan, Anya Zhang, Di Zhang, Ruijia Zhang, Sueky Zhang, Ya Zhang, Wei Zhao, Ada Zhou, Changhai Zhou, Yuhua Zhou, Xinyue Zhu, Murphy Zhuang

entry.summary: Presents MinT, a managed infrastructure system for LoRA post-training and online serving at scale, designed to train and serve millions of adapter-based LLM policies over shared base model deployments. Validated on frontier-scale dense and MoE architectures.

entry.title: Self-Pruned Key-Value Attention: Learning When to Write by Predicting Future Utility

author.name: Gergely Szilvasy (Meta FAIR), Manuel Faysse (Meta FAIR, MICS, CentraleSup\'elec), Maria Lomeli (Meta FAIR), Matthijs Douze (Meta FAIR), Pierre-Emmanuel Mazar\'e (Meta FAIR), Lo\"ic Cabannes (Meta FAIR), Wen-tau Yih (Meta FAIR), Herv\'e J\'egou (Meta FAIR)

entry.summary: Introduces SP-KV (Self-Pruned Key-Value Attention), a mechanism from Meta FAIR that predicts future KV utility to selectively write to long-term KV cache, reducing memory footprint while maintaining performance through a lightweight utility predictor.

entry.title: FrontierSmith: Synthesizing Open-Ended Coding Problems at Scale

author.name: Runyuan He, Qiuyang Mang, Shang Zhou, Kaiyuan Liu, Hanchen Li, Huanzhi Mao, Qizheng Zhang, Zerui Li, Bo Peng, Lufeng Cheng, Tianfu Fu, Yichuan Wang, Wenhao Chai, Jingbo Shang, Alex Dimakis, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Alvin Cheung

entry.summary: Introduces FrontierSmith, an automated system for synthesizing open-ended coding problems at scale from existing competitive programming tasks. Addresses the scarcity of open-ended training problems for LLM coders.

entry.title: Test-Time Learning with an Evolving Library

author.name: Weijia Xu, Alessandro Sordoni, Chandan Singh, Zelalem Gero, Michel Galley, Xingdi Yuan, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Introduces EvoLib, a test-time learning framework where LLMs accumulate and evolve a library of knowledge abstractions (modular skills, reflective insights) across problem instances without parameter updates. Uses principled weighting for long-term value optimization.

entry.title: Widening the Gap: Exploiting LLM Quantization via Outlier Injection

author.name: Xiaohua Zhan, Kazuki Egashira, Robin Staab, Mark Vero, Martin Vechev

entry.summary: Introduces the first quantization-conditioned attack that works against sophisticated quantization schemes (not just simple ones). Models appear benign at full precision but exhibit malicious behavior once quantized, exploiting outlier injection.

entry.title: Position: Behavioural Assurance Cannot Verify the Safety Claims Governance Now Demands

author.name: Pratinav Seth, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that behavioral assurance (evaluations, red-teaming) cannot verify the safety claims that AI governance frameworks now demand, formalizing the 'audit gap' between required and achievable verification access.

entry.title: FutureSim: Replaying World Events to Evaluate Adaptive Agents

author.name: Shashwat Goel, Nikhil Chandak, Arvindh Arun, Ameya Prabhu, Steffen Staab, Moritz Hardt, Maksym Andriushchenko, Jonas Geiping

entry.summary: Proposes FutureSim, a benchmark where AI agents forecast world events beyond their knowledge cutoff by interacting with a chronological replay of real news from Jan-March 2026. Reveals clear capability separation among frontier agents.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Semantic Rewards Enables Low-Resource Language Expansion without Alignment Tax

author.name: Zeli Su, Ziyin Zhang, Zhou Liu, Xuexian Song, Zhankai Xu, Longfei Zheng, Xiaolu Zhang, Rong Fu, Guixian Xu, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes semantic-space alignment for low-resource language expansion of LLMs using GRPO with embedding-level semantic rewards instead of token-level SFT. Aims to avoid the 'alignment tax' where target language improvements cause catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Systematic Discovery of Semantic Attacks in Online Map Construction through Conditional Diffusion

author.name: Chenyi Wang, Ruoyu Song, Raymond Muller, Jean-Philippe Monteuuis, Jonathan Petit, Z. Berkay Celik, Ryan Gerdes, Ming F. Li

entry.summary: Presents MIRAGE, a framework for discovering semantic adversarial attacks against autonomous vehicle HD map construction using diffusion models to find plausible environmental variations (shadows, wet roads) that bypass standard defenses.

entry.title: MeMo: Memory as a Model

author.name: Ryan Wei Heng Quek, Sanghyuk Lee, Alfred Wei Lun Leong, Arun Verma, Alok Prakash, Nancy F. Chen, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Daniela Rus, Armando Solar-Lezama

entry.summary: Introduces MeMo (Memory as a Model), a modular framework encoding new knowledge into a dedicated memory model while keeping LLM parameters unchanged. Captures cross-document relationships, is robust to retrieval noise, and avoids catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Distribution Corrected Offline Data Distillation for Large Language Models

author.name: Yumeng Zhang, Zhengbang Yang, Yevin Nikhel Goonatilake, Zhuangdi Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a method to correct distributional drift in offline knowledge distillation from large to small LLMs. The approach addresses the train-inference mismatch where students condition on teacher-generated prefixes during training but must autoregress on their own outputs during inference. This bridges the gap between high-quality offline distillation and distribution-matched on-policy methods.

entry.title: ML-Embed: Inclusive and Efficient Embeddings for a Multilingual World

author.name: Ziyin Zhang, Zihan Liao, Hang Yu, Peng Di, Rui Wang

entry.summary: Introduces ML-Embed, a suite of multilingual embedding models using 3-Dimensional Matryoshka Learning that provides efficiency across model lifecycle through combined representation, layer, and width flexibility. Addresses computational, linguistic, and transparency barriers in embedding development.

entry.title: Thinking Ahead: Prospection-Guided Retrieval of Memory with Language Models

author.name: Harshita Chopra, Krishna Kant Chintalapudi, Suman Nath, Ryen W. White, Chirag Shah

entry.summary: Introduces Prospection-Guided Retrieval (PGR) inspired by human prospection - using imagined futures as cues for memory recall. Decouples retrieval from storage, expanding queries by generating potential future contexts to retrieve semantically distant but relevant facts.

entry.title: Herculean: An Agentic Benchmark for Financial Intelligence

author.name: Xueqing Peng, Zhuohan Xie, Yupeng Cao, Haohang Li, Lingfei Qian, Yan Wang, Vincent Jim Zhang, Huan He, Xuguang Ai, Linhai Ma, Ruoyu Xiang, Yueru He, Yi Han, Shuyao Wang, Yuqing Guo, Mingyang Jiang, Yilun Zhao, Youzhong Dong, Xiaoyu Wang, Yankai Chen, Ye Yuan, Qiyuan Zhang, Fuyuan Lyu, Haolun Wu, Yonghan Yang, Zichen Zhao, Yuyang Dai, Fan Zhang, Rania Elbadry, Ayesha Gull, Muhammad Usman Safder, Nuo Chen, Fengbin Zhu, Tianshi Cai, Zimu Wang, Polydoros Giannouris, Yuechen Jiang, Zhiwei Liu, Mohsinul Kabir, Yuyan Wang, Yixiang Zheng, Yangyang Yu, Weijin Liu, Wenbo Cao, Anke Xu, Peng Lu, Jerry Huang, Fengran Mo, Mingquan Lin, Prayag Tiwari, Yijia Zhao, Victor Gutierrez Basulto, Xiao-Yang Liu, Kaleb E Smith, Jiahuan Pei, Arman Cohan, Jimin Huang, Yuehua Tang, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Xi Chen, Xue Liu, Junichi Tsujii, Jian-Yun Nie, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: Introduces Herculean, an agentic benchmark for financial intelligence spanning Trading, Hedging, Market Insights, and Auditing workflows. Each workflow uses MCP-based skill environments with specific tools, constraints, and success criteria. First skilled benchmark for agentic financial workflows.

entry.title: PhyMotion: Structured 3D Motion Reward for Physics-Grounded Human Video Generation

author.name: Yidong Huang, Zun Wang, Han Lin, Dong-Ki Kim, Shayegan Omidshafiei, Jaehong Yoon, Jaemin Cho, Yue Zhang, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: Proposes PhyMotion, a physics-grounded reward model for human video generation that recovers 3D human trajectories, simulates them in a physics engine, and evaluates motion quality based on physical plausibility including contact and dynamics. Used for RL-based post-training.

entry.title: SANA-WM: Efficient Minute-Scale World Modeling with Hybrid Linear Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Haoyi Zhu, Haozhe Liu, Yuyang Zhao, Tian Ye, Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Tong He, Song Han, Enze Xie

entry.summary: SANA-WM is a 2.6B-parameter open-source world model for minute-scale 720p video generation with camera control, achieving quality comparable to large industrial baselines while significantly improving efficiency through hybrid linear attention.

entry.title: Pelican-Unified 1.0: A Unified Embodied Intelligence Model for Understanding, Reasoning, Imagination and Action

author.name: Yi Zhang, Yinda Chen, Che Liu, Zeyuan Ding, Jin Xu, Shilong Zou, Junwei Liao, Jiayu Hu, Xiancong Ren, Xiaopeng Zhang, Yechi Liu, Haoyuan Shi, Zecong Tang, Haosong Sun, Renwen Cui, Kuishu Wu, Wenhai Liu, Yang Xu, Yingji Zhang, Yidong Wang, Senkang Hu, Jinpeng Lu, Nga Teng Chan, Yechen Wu, Yong Dai, Jian Tang, Xiaozhu Ju

entry.summary: Presents Pelican-Unified 1.0, described as the first embodied foundation model trained under a unification principle. Uses a single VLM for understanding and reasoning, producing chains of thought that drive a Unified Future Generator for jointly generating future videos and actions.

entry.title: DisaBench: A Participatory Evaluation Framework for Disability Harms in Language Models

author.name: Eugenia Kim, Ioana Tanase, Christina Mallon

entry.summary: DisaBench introduces a taxonomy of 12 disability harm categories co-created with people with disabilities, along with an evaluation methodology and dataset of 175 prompts. Reveals that harm rates vary sharply by disability type and standard safety evaluations miss many disability-specific harms.

entry.title: Retrieval is Cheap, Show Me the Code: Executable Multi-Hop Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Jiashuo Sun, Jimeng Shi, Yixuan Xie, Saizhuo Wang, Jash Rajesh Parekh, Pengcheng Jiang, Zhiyi Shi, Jiajun Fan, Qinglong Zheng, Peiran Li, Shaowen Wang, Ge Liu, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Proposes using code-specialized language models to represent multi-hop reasoning as executable programs for RAG, making intermediate states explicit and errors detectable through code execution rather than unreliable self-reflection.

entry.title: What properties of reasoning supervision are associated with improved downstream model quality?

author.name: Miko{\l}aj Langner, Dzmitry Pihulski, Jan Eliasz, Micha{\l} Rajkowski, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko, Maciej Piasecki, Jan Koco\'n, Teddy Ferdinan

entry.summary: Investigates whether intrinsic data metrics can predict the utility of reasoning datasets before expensive fine-tuning. Finds strong correlations and reveals that predictors are scale-dependent: smaller models need alignment metrics, larger models benefit from reasoning complexity.

entry.title: MMCL-Bench: Multimodal Context Learning from Visual Rules, Procedures, and Evidence

author.name: Yifan Chen, Fei Yin, Qingyan Bai, Zicheng Lin, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: Introduces MMCL-Bench for evaluating multimodal context learning - learning rules, procedures, and patterns from visual context and applying them to new instances. Current frontier models perform poorly.

entry.title: Data Difficulty and the Generalization--Extrapolation Tradeoff in LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Siyuan Liu (IIIS, Tsinghua University), Tinghong Chen (College of AI, Tsinghua University, Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute), Xinghan Li (IIIS, Tsinghua University), Yifei Wang (Amazon AGI SF Lab), Jingzhao Zhang (IIIS, Tsinghua University, Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute)

entry.summary: Studies the role of data difficulty in LLM fine-tuning, finding no universal optimal difficulty but rather that optimal difficulty depends on dataset size and shifts toward harder data as budget increases.

entry.title: Inducing Overthink: Hierarchical Genetic Algorithm-based DoS Attack on Black-Box Large Language Reasoning Models

author.name: Shuqiang Wang, Wei Cao, Jiaqi Weng, Jialing Tao, Licheng Pan, Hui Xue, Zhixuan Chu

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical genetic algorithm to induce overthinking in Large Reasoning Models as a DoS attack vector. Shows LRMs produce excessively long reasoning traces when given logically inconsistent inputs, enabling resource exhaustion attacks.

entry.title: Where Does Reasoning Break? Step-Level Hallucination Detection via Hidden-State Transport Geometry

author.name: Tyler Alvarez, Ali Baheri

entry.summary: Frames LLM hallucination detection as a geometric property of hidden-state trajectories, detecting step-level reasoning errors via transport-cost excursions from a stable manifold. A BiLSTM student distills the geometric features for deployment.

entry.title: Support Before Frequency in Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Adrian M\"uller, Antoine Gonon, Zebang Shen, Ya-Ping Hsieh, Niao He

entry.summary: Proves that discrete diffusion models induce a learning hierarchy where support information (which tokens are valid) is learned before frequency information (relative probabilities), with formal guarantees in the small-noise regime.

entry.title: LiSA: Lifelong Safety Adaptation via Conservative Policy Induction

author.name: Minbeom Kim, Lesly Miculicich, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Mihir Parmar, Phillip Wallis, Bharath Chandrasekhar, Kyomin Jung, Tomas Pfister, Long T. Le

entry.summary: Proposes LiSA for lifelong safety adaptation of AI agent guardrails, using conservative policy induction to adapt to deployment environments from sparse, noisy user feedback without repeated fine-tuning. Targets agents that handle private data and execute workflows.

entry.title: TFGN: Task-Free, Replay-Free Continual Pre-Training Without Catastrophic Forgetting at LLM Scale

author.name: Anurup Ganguli

entry.summary: Introduces TFGN, an architectural overlay for transformer LMs that enables continual pre-training across heterogeneous text domains without replay or task labels, achieving near-zero backward transfer across three model scales up to ~9B parameters.

entry.title: ForcingDAS: Unified and Robust Data Assimilation via Diffusion Forcing

author.name: Yixuan Jia, Siyi Chen, Yida Pan, Xiao Li, Lianghe Shi, Chanyong Jung, Haijie Yuan, Ismail Alkhouri, Yue Cynthia Wu, Saiprasad Ravishankar, Jeffrey A Fessler, Qing Qu

entry.summary: Presents ForcingDAS, a unified data assimilation framework using diffusion forcing that handles both filtering (nowcasting) and smoothing (reanalysis) in a single model. Addresses error accumulation in non-Markovian observation settings relevant to weather forecasting.

entry.title: Interestingness as an Inductive Heuristic for Future Compression Progress

author.name: Vincent Herrmann, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: Formalizes interestingness as an inductive heuristic for future compression progress using Kolmogorov complexity and algorithmic statistics. Proves expected future progress depends exponentially on recency of last discovery.

entry.title: SciPaths: Forecasting Pathways to Scientific Discovery

author.name: Eric Chamoun, Yizhou Chi, Yulong Chen, Rui Cao, Zifeng Ding, Michalis Korakakis, Andreas Vlachos
