entry.summary: Introduces SciPaths, a benchmark for forecasting scientific discovery pathways - identifying enabling contributions required to realize a target contribution and grounding them in prior work. Contains 262 expert-annotated and 2,444 silver pathways from ML/NLP papers.

entry.title: Streaming Speech-to-Text Translation with a SpeechLLM

author.name: Titouan Parcollet, Shucong Zhang, Xianrui Zheng, Rogier C. van Dalen

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based architecture for real streaming speech-to-text translation where the model learns when to emit output tokens based on available audio context, rather than waiting for complete utterances or using fixed intervals. Combines speech recognition and translation in a single SpeechLLM.

entry.title: PREPING: Building Agent Memory without Tasks

author.name: Yumin Choi, Sangwoo Park, Minki Kang, Jinheon Baek, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Studies pre-task memory construction for agents, enabling them to build procedural memory before encountering target-environment tasks using self-generated synthetic practice. Addresses the cold-start problem when agents are introduced to new environments.

entry.title: Do We Really Need External Tools to Mitigate Hallucinations? SIRA: Shared-Prefix Internal Reconstruction of Attribution

author.name: Tian Qin, Junzhe Chen, Yuqing Shi, Tianshu Zhang, Qiang Ju, Lijie Wen

entry.summary: Proposes SIRA, a training-free contrastive decoding method for reducing hallucinations in vision-language models using internal counterfactual references. Exploits staged information flow to construct counterfactuals within the same forward pass without external image perturbation.

entry.title: Revealing Interpretable Failure Modes of VLMs

author.name: Isha Chaudhary, Vedaant V Jain, Kavya Sachdeva, Sayan Ranu, Gagandeep Singh

entry.summary: REVELIO systematically uncovers interpretable failure modes in Vision-Language Models by searching for compositions of domain-relevant concepts under which VLMs consistently fail. This is important for safety-critical deployments where understanding failure conditions is essential.

entry.title: Beyond Cooperative Simulators: Generating Realistic User Personas for Robust Evaluation of LLM Agents

author.name: Harshita Chopra, Kshitish Ghate, Aylin Caliskan, Tadayoshi Kohno, Chirag Shah, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: Introduces Persona Policies (PPol), a plug-and-play control layer that makes LLM-based user simulators exhibit realistic behavioral variation (unclear, impatient, reluctant users) while preserving task goals. Addresses the gap between cooperative simulators and real diverse users.

entry.title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yucheng Guo, Yongjian Guo, Zhong Guan, Wen Huang, Haoran Sun, Haodong Yue, Xiaolong Xiang, Shuai Di, Zhen Sun, Luqiao Wang, Junwu Xiong, Yicheng Gong

entry.summary: D-VLA introduces a high-concurrency distributed RL framework for large Vision-Language-Action models that uses 'Plane Decoupling' to physically isolate training data flow from simulation, addressing the resource conflict between physical simulation and deep learning.

entry.title: How to Interpret Agent Behavior

author.name: Jie Gao, Kaiser Sun, Jen-tse Huang, Katherine Van Koevering, Sijie Ji, Heyuan Huang, Weiyan Shi, Zhuoran Lu, Ziang Xiao, Daniel Khashabi, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: ACT*ONOMY provides a taxonomy for describing and analyzing autonomous agent behavior at runtime, developed through Grounded Theory with a three-level hierarchy of behaviors, validated on Claude Code and Codex agent traces.

entry.title: Differences in Text Generated by Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models

author.name: Zeyang Zhang, Chengwei Liang, Xingyan Chen, Meiqi Gu, Minrui Luo, Jingzhao Zhang, Tianxing He

entry.summary: Empirically characterizes differences between diffusion and autoregressive language models, finding DLMs exhibit lower n-gram entropy, higher semantic coherence, and diversity. Controlled experiments attribute these to the bidirectional context in DLM training.

entry.title: VideoSEAL: Mitigating Evidence Misalignment in Agentic Long Video Understanding by Decoupling Answer Authority

author.name: Chenhao Qiu (Mango TV), Yechao Zhang (Nanyang Technological University), Xin Luo (Mango TV), Shien Song (Mango TV), Xusheng Liu (Mango TV)

entry.summary: Identifies 'evidence misalignment' in long video understanding agents where correct answers aren't supported by retrieved evidence, and proposes VideoSEAL with decoupled answer authority to address this.

entry.title: ODRPO: Ordinal Decompositions of Discrete Rewards for Robust Policy Optimization

author.name: Nirmal Patel, Fei Wang, Inderjit Dhillon

entry.summary: Proposes ODRPO for LLM alignment that decomposes discrete multi-tier rewards into ordinal binary comparisons to be robust against stochastic auto-rater noise in RLAIF settings.

entry.title: Do Fair Models Reason Fairly? Counterfactual Explanation Consistency for Procedural Fairness in Credit Decisions

author.name: Gideon Popoola, John Sheppard

entry.summary: Shows that outcome-fair ML models can still apply different reasoning to different groups ('hidden procedural bias'), and proposes Counterfactual Explanation Consistency to detect and mitigate this.

entry.title: Discrete MeanFlow: One-Step Generation via Conditional Transition Kernels

author.name: Fairoz Nower Khan, Nabuat Zaman Nahim, Md Sajid Ahmed, Ruiquan Huang, Peizhong Ju

entry.summary: Extends MeanFlow to discrete state spaces by introducing Discrete MeanFlow with conditional transition kernels for continuous-time Markov chains, enabling one-step generation for discrete data.

entry.title: REALISTA: Realistic Latent Adversarial Attacks that Elicit LLM Hallucinations

author.name: Buyun Liang, Jinqi Luo, Liangzu Peng, Kwan Ho Ryan Chan, Darshan Thaker, Kaleab A. Kinfu, Fengrui Tian, Hamed Hassani, Ren\'e Vidal

entry.summary: Proposes REALISTA, a latent-space adversarial attack that finds semantically coherent prompts eliciting LLM hallucinations while maintaining semantic equivalence to benign prompts.

entry.title: When Should an AI Workflow Release? Always-Valid Inference for Black-Box Generate-Verify Systems

author.name: Young Hyun Cho, Will Wei Sun

entry.summary: Proposes an always-valid release wrapper for LLM generate-verify pipelines that calibrates evaluator scores against a hard-negative pool and accumulates evidence with e-processes for safe release decisions.

entry.title: Watermarking Should Be Treated as a Monitoring Primitive

author.name: Toluwani Aremu, Nils Lukas, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Argues watermarking should be treated as a monitoring primitive rather than just a detection tool. Shows that even zero-bit watermarking enables entity-level attribution under multi-key settings, and that external monitoring can emerge from persistent watermark signals.

entry.title: KVServe: Service-Aware KV Cache Compression for Communication-Efficient Disaggregated LLM Serving

author.name: Zedong Liu, Xinyang Ma, Dejun Luo, Hairui Zhao, Bing Lu, Wenjing Huang, Yida Gu, Xingchen Liu, Zheng Wei, Jinyang Liu, Dingwen Tao, Guangming Tan

entry.summary: Presents KVServe, the first service-aware adaptive KV cache compression framework for disaggregated LLM serving that dynamically adjusts compression based on workload mix, bandwidth, and SLO/quality budgets.

entry.title: Beyond Mode-Seeking RL: Trajectory-Balance Post-Training for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Saba Ahmadi, Prasanna Parthasarathi, Yufei Cui

entry.summary: Proposes TraFL, a trajectory-balance objective for post-training diffusion language models that addresses 'trajectory locking'—where reward-driven updates over-concentrate probability mass on narrow denoising paths, reducing coverage of correct solutions.

entry.title: LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling

author.name: Qi Cao, Yufan Wang, Peijia Qin, Shuhao Zhang, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: Proposes a metacognitive harness for LLMs inspired by Nelson-Narens theory, using feeling-of-knowing (FOK) and judgment-of-learning (JOL) signals to control test-time compute allocation, demonstrating that LLMs have latent metacognitive ability that improves inference when harnessed.

entry.title: PreFT: Prefill-only finetuning for efficient inference

author.name: Andrew Lanpouthakoun, Aryaman Arora, Zhengxuan Wu, Dhruv Pai, Ben Keigwin, Dan Jurafsky, Christopher Potts

entry.summary: Proposes PreFT (Prefill-only Finetuning), which applies adapters only during the prefill phase of LLM inference, eliminating the per-adapter overhead during the decode phase that bottlenecks multi-adapter serving throughput.

entry.title: TILT: Target-induced loss tilting under covariate shift

author.name: Kakei Yamamoto, Martin J. Wainwright

entry.summary: Introduces TILT for unsupervised domain adaptation under covariate shift, decomposing the source predictor as f+b and penalizing the auxiliary component b on unlabeled target data. Proves that this implicitly induces importance weighting while remaining bounded even with disjoint supports.

entry.title: Enjoy Your Layer Normalization with the Computational Efficiency of RMSNorm

author.name: Yuxin Guo, Yihao Yue, Yunhao Ni, Yizhou Ruan, Jie Luo, Wenjun Wu, Lei Huang

entry.summary: Shows that many Layer Normalization operations in DNNs can be replaced by RMSNorm without changing model behavior, by folding the centering operation into upstream linear layers. Provides a graph-based detection algorithm for identifying foldable LNs.

entry.title: Selective Safety Steering via Value-Filtered Decoding

author.name: Bat-Sheva Einbinder, Hen Davidov, Yee Whye Teh, Yarin Gal, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: Proposes value-filtered decoding for LLM safety steering that reduces unnecessary interventions on already-safe generations while improving safety of unsafe ones. Uses value-based scoring to selectively filter tokens only when needed.

entry.title: Fast Adversarial Attacks with Gradient Prediction

author.name: Kamil Ciosek, Aleksandr V. Petrov, Nicol\`o Felicioni, Konstantina Palla

entry.summary: Proposes adversarial attacks that eliminate the backward pass by predicting input gradients from forward-pass hidden states via lightweight linear regression, motivated by Neural Tangent Kernel theory. Achieves 532% throughput increase over FGSM while recovering most of its attack performance.

entry.title: InfoSFT: Learn More and Forget Less with Information-Aware Token Weighting

author.name: Mahdi Sabbaghi, George Pappas, Adel Javanmard, Hamed Hassani

entry.summary: Proposes InfoSFT, a token-weighting scheme for supervised fine-tuning that uses information-theoretic principles to balance learning novel behaviors versus preserving existing capabilities. Avoids the problem of suppressing precisely the novel behaviors models need to learn.

entry.title: Causal Foundation Models with Continuous Treatments

author.name: Christopher Stith, Medha Barath, Vahid Balazadeh, Jesse C. Cresswell, Rahul G. Krishnan

entry.summary: Presents the first causal foundation model for continuous treatment settings, meta-learning to predict causal effects across unseen tasks without fine-tuning. Designs a novel prior over data-generating processes with continuous treatments.

entry.title: Covariance-aware sampling for Diffusion Models

author.name: Andrea Schioppa, Tim Salimans

entry.summary: Presents a covariance-aware sampler for pixel-space diffusion models that explicitly models reverse-process covariance using Tweedie's formula with Fourier-space decomposition. Improves few-step sampling quality with minimal overhead (one JVP per step). Authors include Tim Salimans.

entry.title: GenCircuit-RL: Reinforcement Learning from Hierarchical Verification for Genetic Circuit Design

author.name: Noah Flynn

entry.summary: Presents GenCircuit-RL, a reinforcement learning framework for genetic circuit design through code generation, using hierarchical verification rewards and a four-stage curriculum. Introduces SynBio-Reason benchmark of 4,753 circuits spanning six canonical circuit families.

entry.title: Precise Verification of Transformers through ReLU-Catalyzed Abstraction Refinement

author.name: Hengjie Liu, Zhenya Zhang, Jianjun Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes a transformer verification approach using ReLU-catalyzed abstraction refinement to achieve precise formal verification while managing the complexity of self-attention dot products. Addresses false alarms from over-approximation in existing methods.

entry.title: Agentifying Patient Dynamics within LLMs through Interacting with Clinical World Model

author.name: Minghao Wu, Yuting Yan, Zhenyang Cai, Ke Ji, Chuangsen Fang, Ziying Sheng, Xidong Wang, Rongsheng Wang, Hejia Zhang, Shuang Li, Benyou Wang, Hongyuan Zha

entry.summary: Introduces SepsisAgent, a world model-augmented LLM agent for sepsis treatment that uses a learned Clinical World Model to simulate patient responses under candidate interventions in a propose-simulate-refine workflow.

entry.title: Your CLIP has 164 dimensions of noise: Exploring the embeddings covariance eigenspectrum of contrastively pretrained vision-language transformers

author.name: Jakub Grzywaczewski, Dawid P{\l}udowski, Przemys{\l}aw Biecek

entry.summary: Analyzes CLIP embedding spaces via spectral decomposition, identifying 164 noise dimensions that exhibit strong subgroup invariance. Shows pruning these shared noise dimensions preserves or improves downstream performance.

entry.title: When Evidence Conflicts: Uncertainty and Order Effects in Retrieval-Augmented Biomedical Question Answering

author.name: Yikun Han, Mengfei Lan, Halil Kilicoglu

entry.summary: Evaluates six open-weight LLMs on biomedical QA when retrieved evidence is conflicting, showing 11-25% of predictions flip simply by reordering contradictory documents. Introduces uncertainty quantification methods to support abstention under conflict. Highlights reliability gaps in RAG-based biomedical systems.

entry.title: Does RAG Know When Retrieval Is Wrong? Diagnosing Context Compliance under Knowledge Conflict

author.name: Yihang Chen, Pin Qian, Su Wang, Sipeng Zhang, Huan Xu, Shuhuai Lin, Xinpeng Wei

entry.summary: Introduces Context-Driven Decomposition (CDD), a belief-decomposition probe that diagnoses how retrieved context causally shapes RAG answers under knowledge conflict. Identifies three patterns of context compliance behavior and proposes intervention mechanisms for controlled retrieval conflict.

entry.title: Performance-Driven Policy Optimization for Speculative Decoding with Adaptive Windowing

author.name: Jie Jiang, Xing Sun

entry.summary: Proposes PPOW, a reinforcement learning framework for optimizing speculative decoding drafters at the window level rather than token level. Uses adaptive windowing to shift optimization from token-level imitation to window-level performance, better matching the actual objective of speculative decoding.

entry.title: SWE-Chain: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Chained Release-Level Package Upgrades

author.name: Man Ho Lam, Chaozheng Wang, Hange Liu, Jingyu Xiao, Haau-sing Li, Jen-tse Huang, Terry Yue Zhuo, Michael R. Lyu

entry.summary: Presents SWE-Chain, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents on chained release-level package upgrades where each transition builds on prior agent modifications. Uses a divide-and-conquer synthesis pipeline aligning release notes with code diffs.

entry.title: Do Composed Image Retrieval Benchmarks Require Multimodal Composition?

author.name: Matteo Attimonelli, Alessandro De Bellis, Aryo Pradipta Gema, Rohit Saxena, Monica Sekoyan, Wai-Chung Kwan, Claudio Pomo, Alessandro Suglia, Dietmar Jannach, Tommaso Di Noia, Pasquale Minervini

entry.summary: Shows that Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) benchmarks can often be solved using single-modality signals (32-83% of queries), revealing pervasive unimodal shortcuts. Evaluates 11 multimodal embedding models across four benchmarks.

entry.title: Holistic Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis of AI Agents

author.name: Netta Madvil, Gilad Dym, Alon Mecilati, Edo Dekel, Jonatan Liberman, Rotem Brazilay, Liron Schliesser, Max Svidlo, Shai Nir, Orel Shalom, Yaron Friedman, David Connack, Amos Rimon, Philip Tannor, Shir Chorev

entry.summary: Presents a holistic agent evaluation framework pairing top-down agent-level diagnosis with bottom-up span-level evaluation. Achieves SOTA on TRAIL benchmark across GAIA and SWE-Bench with significant gains over prior baselines.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Concept Omission in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Kanghyun Baek, Jaihyun Lew, Chaehun Shin, Jungbeom Lee, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Identifies and addresses concept omission in multimodal diffusion transformers (MM-DiTs) like FLUX.1 and SD3.5. Shows that text embeddings contain detectable 'omission signals' and proposes Omission Signal Intervention to amplify these signals and generate missing concepts.

entry.title: Head Forcing: Long Autoregressive Video Generation via Head Heterogeneity

author.name: Jiahao Tian, Yiwei Wang, Gang Yu, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Head Forcing for long autoregressive video generation, discovering that attention heads serve functionally distinct roles (local, anchor, memory) and proposing tailored KV cache strategies for each type with hierarchical memory for long-range consistency.

entry.title: The Velocity Deficit: Initial Energy Injection for Flow Matching

author.name: Linze Li, Zong-Wei Hong, Shen Zhang, Bo Lin, Jinglun Li, Yao Tang, Jiajun Liang

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Velocity Deficit' problem in Flow Matching where MSE objectives systematically underestimate velocity magnitude, causing generated samples to fall short of the data manifold. Proposes Initial Energy Injection via training-based and training-free methods.

entry.title: Seed3D 2.0: Advancing High-Fidelity Simulation-Ready 3D Content Generation

author.name: Diandian Gu, Jing Lin, Gaohong Liu, Jiahang Liu, Su Ma, Guang Shi, Jun Wang, Qinlong Wang, Qianyi Wu, Zhongcong Xu, Xuanyu Yi, Zihao Yu, Jianfeng Zhang, Zhuolin Zheng, Yifan Zhu, Rui Chen, Hengkai Guo, Xiaoyang Guo, Mingcong Han, Xu Han, Xiu Li, Yixun Liang, Weiqiang Lou, Junzhe Lu, Guan Luo, Minghan Qin, Shuguang Wang, Yuang Wang

entry.summary: Seed3D 2.0 presents an advanced 3D content generation system with improvements in geometry (coarse-to-fine pipeline), texture/material (unified PBR model with MoE scaling), and new capabilities including multi-object scene generation.

entry.title: 2B scoring model flags out-of-domain misalignment, suggesting specialist judges have potential for audits

author.name: burnssa

entry.summary: Demonstrates that a small 2B parameter specialist model trained on code misalignment examples can detect out-of-domain misalignment in general safety contexts, where larger frontier models (Sonnet 4.5) cannot. Suggests narrow specialist judges have potential for deployed model audits.

entry.title: Scaling Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Parallel Search and Explicit Merging

author.name: Jiabei Liu, Wenyu Mao, Junfei Tan, Chunxu Shen, Lingling Yi, Jiancan Wu, Xiang Wang

entry.summary: MultiSearch introduces an RL-based framework for retrieval-augmented reasoning that generates multiple queries from different perspectives at each step, retrieves in parallel, and explicitly merges information to improve signal-to-noise ratio.

entry.title: Learning from Language Feedback via Variational Policy Distillation

author.name: Yang Li, Erik Nijkamp, Semih Yavuz, Shafiq Rayhan Joty

entry.summary: Proposes Variational Policy Distillation (VPD) for learning from language feedback in RLVR, formalizing it as variational EM where teacher and student co-evolve. Addresses the plateau problem where fixed teachers stop improving.

entry.title: Think When Needed: Adaptive Reasoning-Driven Multimodal Embeddings with a Dual-LoRA Architecture

author.name: Longxiang Zhang, Weilong Dai, Guanghao Zhang, Hao Jiang, Pipei Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Think When Needed (TWN), a dual-LoRA architecture for multimodal embeddings that adaptively applies chain-of-thought reasoning only when beneficial. Observes that redundant reasoning can degrade performance on simple inputs, and addresses this with selective activation.

entry.title: Moltbook Moderation: Uncovering Hidden Intent Through Multi-Turn Dialogue

author.name: Ali Al-Lawati, Nafis Tripto, Abolfazl Ansari, Jason Lucas, Suhang Wang, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: BOT-MOD introduces a moderation framework for multi-agent systems that detects malicious agent intent through multi-turn dialogue exchanges guided by Gibbs-based sampling over candidate intent hypotheses, rather than relying on content-level filtering.

entry.title: Many-Shot CoT-ICL: Making In-Context Learning Truly Learn

author.name: Tsz Ting Chung, Lemao Liu, Mo Yu, Dit-Yan Yeung

entry.summary: Studies many-shot chain-of-thought in-context learning for reasoning tasks. Finds scaling behavior differs from non-reasoning tasks: CoT demonstrations help reasoning LLMs but are unstable for non-reasoning LLMs.

entry.title: To See is Not to Learn: Protecting Multimodal Data from Unauthorized Fine-Tuning of Large Vision-Language Model

author.name: Chengshuai Zhao, Zhen Tan, Dawei Li, Zhiyuan Yu, Huan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes MMGuard, a proactive defense against unauthorized fine-tuning of vision-language models by generating unlearnable examples with human-imperceptible perturbations that exploit LVLM learning dynamics. Creates optimization shortcuts that prevent meaningful parameter updates.

entry.title: Knowledge Beyond Language: Bridging the Gap in Multilingual Machine Unlearning Evaluation

author.name: Kyomin Hwang, Hyeonjin Kim, Sangyeon Cho, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: Proposes metrics (Knowledge Separability Score and Knowledge Persistence Score) for evaluating multilingual machine unlearning that capture cross-linguistic information spread. Addresses the gap where prior evaluations fail to account for how knowledge persists across languages after unlearning in one language.

entry.title: CreFlow: Corrective Reflow for Sparse-Reward Embodied Video Diffusion RL

author.name: Zhenyang Ni, Yijiang Li, Ruochen Jiao, Simon Sinong Zhan, Sipeng Chen, Zhenfei Yin, Minshuo Chen, Philip Torr, Zhaoran Wang, Qi Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces CreFlow for RL post-training of embodied video generation models using compositional constraint-based rewards formulated as Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) constraints. Addresses the gap between low-level visual metrics and compositional task verification.

entry.title: Macro-Action Based Multi-Agent Instruction Following through Value Cancellation

author.name: Wo Wei Lin, Ethan Rathbun, Enrico Marchesini Xiang Zhi Tan

entry.summary: MAVIC addresses a fundamental failure mode in multi-agent RL where Bellman updates couple value estimates across instruction contexts when natural language instructions interrupt ongoing macro-actions. The method corrects bootstrapping targets at instruction boundaries to maintain consistent values.

entry.title: State-Centric Decision Process

author.name: Sungheon Jeong, Ryozo Masukawa, Sanggeon Yun, Mahdi Imani, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: Introduces State-Centric Decision Process (SDP), a runtime framework where language agents construct MDP structure (state space, transitions, termination criteria) themselves using natural-language predicates as they act in text-based environments.

entry.title: It's not the Language Model, it's the Tool: Deterministic Mediation for Scientific Workflows

author.name: Marios Adamidis, Danae Katrisioti, Yannis Tzitzikas, Emmanuel Stratakis

entry.summary: Proposes 'typed mediation' where LLMs orchestrate deterministic, researcher-verified tools rather than generating analytical code, ensuring reproducibility in scientific workflows since regeneration doesn't change results.

entry.title: Respecting Self-Uncertainty in On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient LLM Reasoning

author.name: Junlong Ke, Zichen Wen, Weijia Li, Conghui He, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: EGRSD proposes entropy-guided reinforced self-distillation that weights the teacher's token-level signal by its confidence (entropy), down-weighting high-entropy positions during on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models.

entry.title: VERA-MH: Validation of Ethical and Responsible AI in Mental Health

author.name: Luca Belli, Kate H. Bentley, Josh Gieringer, Emily Van Ark, Nilu Zhao, Pradip Thachile, Matt Hawrilenko, Millard Brown, Adam M. Chekroud

entry.summary: VERA-MH introduces a clinically-validated evaluation for chatbot safety in mental health contexts, focusing on suicidal ideation risks. Uses persona-based conversation simulation and clinician-developed evaluation criteria.

entry.title: RealICU: Do LLM Agents Understand Long-Context ICU Data? A Benchmark Beyond Behavior Imitation

author.name: Chengzhi Shen (Cherise), Weixiang Shen (Cherise), Tobias Susetzky (Cherise), Chen (Cherise), Chen (Cherise), Jun Li, Yuyuan Liu, Xuepeng Zhang, Zhenyu Gong, Daniel Rueckert, Jiazhen Pan

entry.summary: RealICU introduces a hindsight-annotated benchmark for evaluating LLMs in ICU settings where labels are created after senior physicians review full patient trajectories, rather than treating real-time clinician actions as ground truth.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Simulate Dynamic Networks? A Case Study on Email Networks with Phishing Synthesis

author.name: Siqi Miao, Ziyang Chen, Yuhong Luo, Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, Mufei Li, Kaiqing Zhang, Pan Li

entry.summary: Evaluates whether LLM multi-agent systems can replicate realistic network dynamics, finding they excel at micro-level interactions but fail to capture macroscopic topologies. Proposes two extensions to preserve network fidelity including augmenting LLM agents with structural awareness.

entry.title: Bridging the Missing-Modality Gap: Improving Text-Only Calibration of Vision Language Models

author.name: Mingyeong Kim (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI, KAIST), Jungwon Choi (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI, KAIST), Chaeyun Jang (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI, KAIST), Juho Lee (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI, KAIST)

entry.summary: Finds that removing vision modality from VLMs causes accuracy drops and severe miscalibration on text-only inputs. Proposes Latent Imagination Module (LIM) that predicts imagined visual embeddings from text to restore calibration without generating pixels.

entry.title: SSDA: Bridging Spectral and Structural Gaps via Dual Adaptation for Vision-Based Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Mingrui Zhang, Hanchen Yang, Wengen Li, Xudong Jiang, Yichao Zhang, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies spectral and structural gaps between rendered time series images and natural images that limit vision model transfer to forecasting, and proposes SSDA to bridge these gaps through dual adaptation.

entry.title: Learning to Decide with AI Assistance under Human-Alignment

author.name: Nina Corvelo Benz, Eleni Straitouri, Manuel Gomez-Rodriguez

entry.summary: Studies how alignment between AI confidence and human decision-makers' confidence affects the complexity of learning to make optimal AI-assisted decisions, providing theoretical and empirical evidence.

entry.title: Inline Critic Steers Image Editing

author.name: Weitai Kang, Xiaohang Zhan, Yizhou Wang, Mang Tik Chiu, Jason Kuen, Kangning Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Introduces Inline Critic, a learnable token that critiques a frozen image-editing model's predictions mid-forward-pass, enabling refinement within a single pass rather than after full generation.

entry.title: Simulating Students or Sycophantic Problem Solving? On Misconception Faithfulness of LLM Simulators

author.name: Heejin Do, Shashank Sonkar, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for evaluating whether LLM student simulators maintain coherent misconceptions during interaction, revealing they often exhibit sycophantic rather than misconception-faithful behavior.

entry.title: Correcting Influence: Unboxing LLM Outputs with Orthogonal Latent Spaces

author.name: Shixing Yu, Promit Ghosal, Kyra Gan

entry.summary: Introduces a framework using sparse autoencoders to infer token-level influence of training data on LLM predictions through latent mediation, addressing limitations of existing influence function approaches.

entry.title: ChipMATE: Multi-Agent Training via Reinforcement Learning for Enhanced RTL Generation

author.name: Zhongkai Yu, Yichen Lin, Chenyang Zhou, Yuwei Zhang, Kun Zhou, Junxia Cui, Haotian Ye, Zhengding Hu, Zaifeng Pan, Ruiyi Wang, Yujie Zhao, Hejia Zhang, Jingbo Shang, Jishen Zhao, Yufei Ding

entry.summary: Presents ChipMATE, the first self-trained multi-agent framework for RTL code generation using RL, addressing industrial requirements of air-gapped deployment and verification-integrated workflows.

entry.title: The Expressivity Boundary of Probabilistic Circuits: A Comparison with Large Language Models

author.name: Zhiyu Zhao, Xuejie Liu, Muhan Zhang, Anji Liu

entry.summary: Compares probabilistic circuits and LLMs under a unified autoregressive formulation, identifying output and context-encoding bottlenecks in PCs and proposing solutions to narrow the gap.

entry.title: Towards Long-horizon Embodied Agents with Tool-Aligned Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zixing Lei, Changxing Liu, Yichen Xiong, Minhao Xiong, Yuanzhuo Ding, Zhipeng Zhang, Weixin Li, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: Proposes VLAs-as-Tools, distributing long-horizon robot task execution across a high-level VLM agent for planning and specialized VLA tools for local physical operations. Introduces a VLA tool-family interface with progress feedback.

entry.title: Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization for LLM Distillation

author.name: Xinyu Liu, Kechen Jiao, Chunyang Xiao, Runsong Zhao, Junhao Ruan, Bei Li, Jiahao Liu, Qifan Wang, Xin Chen, Jingang Wang, Tong Xiao, JingBo Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes Teacher-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO) for LLM distillation that provides dense directional guidance by leveraging teacher predictions conditioned on student rollouts. Addresses the failure of standard Reverse KL when student-teacher distributions diverge significantly.

entry.title: CANTANTE: Optimizing Agentic Systems via Contrastive Credit Attribution

author.name: Tom Zehle

entry.summary: Introduces CANTANTE, a framework that decomposes system-level rewards into per-agent update signals for multi-agent LLM systems using contrastive rollouts. Instantiated for prompt optimization of agent systems.

entry.title: Query-Conditioned Test-Time Self-Training for Large Language Models

author.name: Chaehee Song, Minseok Seo, Yeeun Seong, Doyi Kim, Changick Kim

entry.summary: Proposes QueST, a test-time self-training framework that adapts LLM parameters during inference using supervision derived from the input query itself. Enables query-specific parameter updates without external data.

entry.title: Temper and Tilt Lead to SLOP: Reward Hacking Mitigation with Inference-Time Alignment

author.name: Ye Wang, Jing Liu, Toshiaki Koike-Akino

entry.summary: Introduces SLOP (Sharpened Logarithmic Opinion Pool) for inference-time alignment, combining reference-model temperature adjustment with ensembles of generative reward models. Proposes calibration to mitigate reward hacking.

entry.title: Beyond Perplexity: A Geometric and Spectral Study of Low-Rank Pre-Training

author.name: Namrata Shivagunde, Vijeta Deshpande, Sherin Muckatira, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Goes beyond perplexity to characterize low-rank pre-trained LLMs using geometric and spectral analysis, revealing that models matching on perplexity can converge to fundamentally different loss landscape regions and internal representations.

entry.title: AnyFlow: Any-Step Video Diffusion Model with On-Policy Flow Map Distillation

author.name: Yuchao Gu, Guian Fang, Yuxin Jiang, Weijia Mao, Song Han, Han Cai, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Introduces AnyFlow, the first any-step video diffusion distillation framework based on flow maps that optimizes the full ODE sampling trajectory, overcoming the performance degradation of consistency distillation when more sampling steps are used.

entry.title: High-Rate Quantized Matrix Multiplication II

author.name: Or Ordentlich, Yury Polyanskiy

entry.summary: Investigates quantized matrix multiplication with available covariance information, showing how classical waterfilling from rate-distortion theory can improve practical LLM weight-only quantization algorithms like GPTQ by allocating rate non-uniformly across coordinates.

entry.title: Collider-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents with Particle Physics Analysis Reproduction

author.name: Darius A. Faroughy, Sofia Palacios Schweitzer, Ian Pang, Siddharth Mishra-Sharma, David Shih

entry.summary: Introduces Collider-Bench, a benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents can reproduce experimental particle physics analyses from the LHC using only published papers and open software, testing physical reasoning and domain expertise.

entry.title: Diagnosing Training Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tianle Zhong, Neiwen Ling, Yifan Pi, Zijun Wei, Tianshu Yu, Geoffrey Fox, Peng Wu, Xiao Yu

entry.summary: Identifies and diagnoses Training-Inference Mismatch (TIM) in LLM RL systems where rollout generation and policy optimization produce different token probabilities for the same weights, showing small numerical disagreements can cause training collapse.

entry.title: Minimal-Intervention KV Retention: A Design-Space Study and a Diversity-Penalty Survivor

author.name: Libo Sun, Po-wei Harn, Peixiong He, Xiao Qin

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic design-space study of KV-cache compression for long-form mathematical reasoning, testing seven mechanisms across two distilled-reasoning models. Proposes α, a diversity-penalty retention scorer that improves upon existing methods at very small budgets.

entry.title: Guided Diffusion Sampling for Precipitation Forecast Interventions

author.name: Ayumu Ueyama, Kazuhiko Kawamoto, Hiroshi Kera

entry.summary: Proposes using guided diffusion sampling in weather forecasting models for precipitation-reduction interventions, steering diffusion trajectories toward physically plausible states with reduced extreme precipitation rather than applying adversarial perturbations.

entry.title: What if Tomorrow is the World Cup Final? Counterfactual Time Series Forecasting with Textual Conditions

author.name: Shuqi Gu, Yongxiang Zhao, Baoyu Jing, Kan Ren

entry.summary: Introduces counterfactual time series forecasting with textual conditions—predicting how time series would change under hypothetical future events described in natural language. A novel task formulation combining causal reasoning with language-conditioned forecasting.

entry.title: When Answers Stray from Questions: Hallucination Detection via Question-Answer Orthogonal Decomposition

author.name: Siyang Yao, Erhu Feng, Yubin Xia

entry.summary: Proposes QAOD for hallucination detection by projecting away the question-aligned direction from answer representations, obtaining a question-orthogonal component that suppresses domain-conditioned variation. Achieves robust single-pass detection under domain shift.

entry.title: Discovering Physical Directions in Weight Space: Composing Neural PDE Experts

author.name: Pengkai Wang, Pengwei Liu, Yuanyi Wang, Guanyu Chen, Xingyu Ren, Xiaolong Li, Zhongkai Hao, Yuting Kong, Qixin Zhang, Dong Ni

entry.summary: Discovers physical directions in neural PDE operator weight space—showing that fine-tuned regime experts can be separated into family-shared adaptation and a direction aligned with the underlying physical parameter. Enables interpolation to intermediate regimes.

entry.title: Fast Rates for Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Andreas Schlaginhaufen, Maryam Kamgarpour

entry.summary: Establishes fast O(n^{-1}) convergence rates for entropy-regularized min-max inverse RL, proving equivalence between MLE and Min-Max-IRL at population level. Results apply under misspecification without exploration assumptions.

entry.title: NeuroAtlas: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Clinical EEG and Brain-Computer Interfaces

author.name: Konstantinos Kontras, Trui Osselaer, Stylianos G. Mouslech, Angeliki-Ilektra Karaiskou, Guido Gagliardi, Thomas Strypsteen, Mohammad Hossein Badiei, Anku Rani, Maarten Vanmarcke, Miguel Bhagubai, Chanakya Ekbote, Jaedong Hwang, Christos Chatzichristos, Paul Pu Liang, Maarten De Vos

entry.summary: Introduces NeuroAtlas, the largest EEG benchmark (42 datasets, 260K hours) covering clinical EEG and brain-computer interfaces. Evaluates EEG foundation models with clinically relevant metrics.

entry.title: Crys-JEPA: Accelerating Crystal Discovery via Embedding Screening and Generative Refinement

author.name: Nian Liu, Nikita Kazeev, Stephen Gregory Dale, Artem Maevskiy, Yuwei Zeng, Ryoji Kubo, Pengru Huang, Thomas Laurent, Yann LeCun, Kostya S. Novoselov, Xavier Bresson

entry.summary: Introduces Crys-JEPA for crystal discovery, combining JEPA-based embedding screening with generative refinement to navigate the stability-novelty tradeoff in de novo crystal generation. Shows current generative models are caught in this tradeoff.

entry.title: GPart: End-to-End Isometric Fine-Tuning via Global Parameter Partitioning

author.name: Paolo Mandica, Micha{\l} Brzozowski, Zuzanna Dubanowska, Neo Christopher Chung

entry.summary: Proposes GPart, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that replaces LoRA's bilinear low-rank structure with a single isometric mapping from trainable parameters to weight updates, preserving distances in the optimization landscape. Claims to remove the distortion problem inherent in LoRA-based approaches.

entry.title: Boosting Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Randomly Selected Few-Shot Guidance

author.name: Kai Yan, Alexander G. Schwing, Yu-Xiong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes FEST, a few-shot demonstration-guided RLVR algorithm that achieves strong results with only 128 randomly selected demonstrations. Identifies three key components for effective few-shot guidance in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

entry.title: Training ML Models with Predictable Failures

author.name: Will Schwarzer, Scott Niekum

entry.summary: Analyzes finite-sample properties of deployment-scale failure rate estimators, showing built-in safety-favorable bias. Proposes a fine-tuning objective that makes models fail more predictably, improving pre-deployment safety assessment.

entry.title: Mistletoe: Stealthy Acceleration-Collapse Attacks on Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shuoyang Sun, Chang Da, Hao Fang, Kuofeng Gao, Xinhao Zhong, Yi Sun, Fan Mo, Shu-Tao Xia, Bin Chen

entry.summary: Identifies a new attack surface in speculative decoding (Mistletoe attack) where small perturbations preserve visible model behavior while substantially reducing draft token acceptance rates, stealthily degrading inference speed.

entry.title: MathAtlas: A Benchmark for Autoformalization in the Wild

author.name: Nilay Patel, Noah Arias, Davit Babayan, Victoria Cochran, Timothy Libman, Hafsah Mahmood, Liam McCarty, Soli Munoz, Laurel Willey, Jeffrey Flanigan

entry.summary: Introduces MathAtlas, a large-scale autoformalization benchmark of ~52K graduate-level mathematics items from 103 textbooks, with ~178K dependency relations. Shows current models struggle significantly with graduate-level formalization.

entry.title: To discretize continually: Mean shift interacting particle systems for Bayesian inference

author.name: Ayoub Belhadji, Daniel Sharp, Youssef M. Marzouk

entry.summary: Introduces interacting particle methods for Bayesian inference that extend the mean shift algorithm to minimize maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to target distributions. Methods are invariant to unknown normalizing constants and support both gradient-free and gradient-informed implementations.

entry.title: ICED: Concept-level Machine Unlearning via Interpretable Concept Decomposition

author.name: Shen Lin, Jing Lin, Junhao Dong, Piotr Koniusz, Li Xu

entry.summary: Introduces ICED, a concept-level machine unlearning framework for vision-language models that constructs a concept vocabulary from the forgetting set and decomposes visual representations into sparse, nonnegative concept combinations for targeted removal.

entry.title: Nexus : An Agentic Framework for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Sarkar Snigdha Sarathi Das, Palash Goyal, Mihir Parmar, Nanyun Peng, Vishy Tirumalashetty, Chun-Liang Li, Rui Zhang, Jinsung Yoon, Tomas Pfister

entry.summary: Introduces Nexus, a multi-agent forecasting framework that decomposes time series prediction into specialized stages for macro/micro temporal fluctuations and contextual information integration. Bridges TSFMs and LLMs for context-aware forecasting.

entry.title: Prompting Policies for Multi-step Reasoning and Tool-Use in Black-box LLMs with Iterative Distillation of Experience

author.name: Krishna Sayana, Ketan Todi, Ambarish Jash

entry.summary: Proposes an RL framework for training a lightweight prompter model to optimize prompts for a frozen black-box LLM, using a contrastive experience buffer with scalar rewards and textual critiques. Evaluated on Big Bench Extra Hard and Tau-bench.

entry.title: Let Robots Feel Your Touch: Visuo-Tactile Cortical Alignment for Embodied Mirror Resonance

author.name: Tianfang Zhu, Ning An, Rui Wang, Jiasi Gao, Qingming Luo, Anan Li, Guyue Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Mirror Touch Net, which operationalizes visuo-tactile cortical correspondence in robots by aligning visual and tactile representations through multi-level constraints. Predicts millimeter-scale tactile signals across 1,140 taxels from visual observation alone.

entry.title: From Sycophantic Consensus to Pluralistic Repair: Why AI Alignment Must Surface Disagreement

author.name: Varad Vishwarupe, Nigel Shadbolt, Marina Jirotka

entry.summary: Argues that pluralistic AI alignment must surface disagreement rather than achieve sycophantic consensus. Critiques current RLHF-trained assistants for collapsing disagreement and proposes 'pluralistic repair' as an alternative.

entry.title: ROK-FORTRESS: Measuring the Effect of Geopolitical Transcreation for National Security and Public Safety

author.name: Michael S. Lee, Yash Maurya, Drew Rein, Bert Herring, Jonathan Nguyen, Kyungho Song, Udari Madhushani Sehwag, Jiyeon Cho, Kaustubh Deshpande, Yeongkyun Jang, Jiyeon Joo, Minn Seok Choi, Evi Fuelle, Christina Q Knight, Joseph Brandifino, Max Fenkell

entry.summary: Introduces ROK-FORTRESS, a bilingual benchmark separating language effects from geopolitical context effects on LLM safety using English-Korean pairs and U.S.-ROK geopolitical axis. Uses a transcreation matrix to distinguish cultural grounding from mere translation. Addresses gaps in multilingual safety evaluation.

entry.title: Agentic Recommender System with Hierarchical Belief-State Memory

author.name: Xiang Shen, Yuhang Zhou, Yifan Wu, Zhuokai Zhao, Siyu Lin, Lei Huang, Qianqian Zhong, Lizhu Zhang, Benyu Zhang, Xiangjun Fan, Hong Yan

entry.summary: Proposes MARS, a recommender system treating recommendation as a partially observable problem with hierarchical belief-state memory organized in three tiers: event memory, preference memory, and profile memory. Provides a complete lifecycle for how memory should evolve, addressing limitations of flat memory representations.

entry.title: GroupMemBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent Memory in Multi-Party Conversations

author.name: Jingbo Yang, Kwei-Herng Lai, Xiaowen Wang, Shiyu Chang, Yaar Harari, Evgeniy Gabrilovich

entry.summary: Introduces GroupMemBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agent memory in multi-party conversations, measuring group dynamics, speaker-grounded belief tracking, and audience-adapted language. Addresses the gap between single-user memory evaluation and real multi-user deployment scenarios.

entry.title: The Scientific Contribution Graph: Automated Literature-based Technological Roadmapping at Scale

author.name: Peter A. Jansen

entry.summary: Presents the Scientific Contribution Graph, a large-scale resource with 2 million contributions from 230k papers connected by 12.5 million prerequisite edges. Introduces scientific prerequisite prediction as a discovery task, showing models reaching 0.48 MAP.

entry.title: Know When To Fold 'Em: Token-Efficient LLM Synthetic Data Generation via Multi-Stage In-Flight Rejection

author.name: Anjir Ahmed Chowdhury, Syed Zawad, Feng Yan

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-Stage In-Flight Rejection (MSIFR) for synthetic data generation, detecting and terminating low-quality generation trajectories at intermediate checkpoints. Uses rule-based validators to identify arithmetic inconsistencies, hallucinations, and formatting violations early. Training-free and reduces token waste.

entry.title: IntentVLA: Short-Horizon Intent Modeling for Aliased Robot Manipulation

author.name: Shijie Lian, Bin Yu, Xiaopeng Lin, Zhaolong Shen, Laurence Tianruo Yang, Yurun Jin, Haishan Liu, Changti Wu, Hang Yuan, Cong Huang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Introduces IntentVLA, a history-conditioned vision-language-action framework that encodes recent visual observations into short-horizon intent representations for robot manipulation. Addresses multi-modality in imitation data where similar observations lead to different actions. Introduces AliasBench for ambiguity-aware evaluation.

entry.title: Venus-DeFakerOne: Unified Fake Image Detection & Localization

author.name: GuangJian Team

entry.summary: Presents Venus-DeFakerOne, a unified foundation model for fake image detection and localization across multiple forgery domains (document editing, deepfakes, AIGC synthesis). Addresses the mismatch between unified forgery generation and fragmented detection approaches.

entry.title: TeDiO: Temporal Diagonal Optimization for Training-Free Coherent Video Diffusion

author.name: Nurislam Tursynbek, Zhiqiang Lao, Heather Yu, Gedas Bertasius, Marc Niethammer

entry.summary: Introduces TeDiO, a training-free inference-time method for improving temporal coherence in video diffusion by regularizing self-attention patterns. Shows that temporal coherence failures correspond to irregular patterns in attention maps, and smooth diagonal patterns indicate stable motion.

entry.title: KVPO: ODE-Native GRPO for Autoregressive Video Alignment via KV Semantic Exploration

author.name: Ruicheng Zhang, Kaixi Cong, Jun Zhou, Zhizhou Zhong, Zunnan Xu, Shuiyang Mao, Wei Liu, Xiu Li

entry.summary: Presents KVPO, an ODE-native online GRPO framework for aligning streaming autoregressive video generators with human preferences. Introduces causal-semantic exploration through KV cache perturbation rather than noise-based exploration.

entry.title: InsightTok: Improving Text and Face Fidelity in Discrete Tokenization for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Yang Yue, Fangyun Wei, Tianyu He, Jinjing Zhao, Zanlin Ni, Zeyu Liu, Jiayi Guo, Lei Shi, Yue Dong, Li Chen, Ji Li, Gao Huang, Dong Chen

entry.summary: Introduces InsightTok, a discrete visual tokenization framework that enhances text and face fidelity in autoregressive image generation by aligning tokenizer objectives with text legibility and facial fidelity rather than generic reconstruction.

entry.title: Real2Sim in HOI: Toward Physically Plausible HOI Reconstruction from Monocular Videos

author.name: Yubo Zhao, Yujin Chai, Yunao Dong, Chengfeng Zhao, Zijiao Zeng, Yuan Liu, Chi-Keung Tang

entry.summary: Introduces HA-HOI for reconstructing physically plausible 4D human-object interaction from monocular video, bridging the gap between visual reconstruction and physics-based simulation for humanoid-object interaction.

entry.title: Video-Zero: Self-Evolution Video Understanding

author.name: Ruixu Zhang, Deyi Ji, Lanyun Zhu, Xuanyi Liu, Yuxin Meng, Ruihang Chu, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Video-Zero, an annotation-free self-evolution framework for video understanding where a Questioner-Solver co-evolves with emphasis on grounding rather than difficulty alone, ensuring questions target temporally localized evidence.

entry.title: Unlocking Complex Visual Generation via Closed-Loop Verified Reasoning

author.name: Hanbo Cheng, Limin Lin, Ruo Zhang, Yicheng Pan, Jun Du

entry.summary: CLVR proposes a closed-loop visual reasoning framework for text-to-image generation that couples visual-language planning with pixel-level diffusion, including step-level visual verification to overcome hallucinated plans and monolithic reflection limitations.

entry.title: Causal Forcing++: Scalable Few-Step Autoregressive Diffusion Distillation for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation

author.name: Min Zhao, Hongzhou Zhu, Kaiwen Zheng, Zihan Zhou, Bokai Yan, Xinyuan Li, Xiao Yang, Chongxuan Li, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: Causal Forcing++ advances real-time interactive video generation to frame-wise autoregression with 1-2 sampling steps, identifying student initialization as the key bottleneck and proposing a principled, scalable solution.

entry.title: Articraft: An Agentic System for Scalable Articulated 3D Asset Generation

author.name: Matt Zhou, Ruining Li, Xiaoyang Lyu, Zhaomou Song, Zhening Huang, Chuanxia Zheng, Christian Rupprecht, Andrea Vedaldi, Shangzhe Wu

entry.summary: Articraft leverages LLMs as agentic systems to generate articulated 3D assets at scale by writing programs against a domain-specific SDK, with validation tests to ensure asset quality. Addresses the bottleneck of scarce articulated 3D datasets.

entry.title: Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking? Rewarding Perception for Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Haozhe Wang, Qixin Xu, Changpeng Wang, Taofeng Xue, Chong Peng, Wenhu Chen, Fangzhen Lin

entry.summary: Argues that the perception-reasoning trade-off in VLMs stems from ambiguous modality credit assignment ('bad seeing' vs 'bad thinking'), and proposes rewarding perception directly to address this fundamental bottleneck.

entry.title: MAPLE: Latent Multi-Agent Play for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Rajeev Yasarla, Deepti Hegde, Hsin-Pai Cheng, Shizhong Han, Yunxiao Shi, Meysam Sadeghigooghari, Hanno Ackermann, Litian Liu, Pranav Desai, Fatih Porikli, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Hong Cai

entry.summary: MAPLE introduces latent multi-agent play for end-to-end autonomous driving, enabling reactive multi-agent rollout in the VLA model's latent space for closed-loop training without traditional simulation.

entry.title: GEAR: Genetic AutoResearch for Agentic Code Evolution

author.name: Ahmadreza Jeddi, Minh Ngoc Le, Hakki C. Karaimer, Konstantinos G. Derpanis, Babak Taati

entry.summary: GEAR introduces a genetic/population-based search approach for autonomous research agents, maintaining multiple candidate solutions and using mutation/crossover instead of single-path optimization. Overcomes limitation of discarding useful partial ideas.

entry.title: DSSP: Diffusion State Space Policy with Full-History Encoding

author.name: Zhiyuan Guan, Jianshu Hu, Han Fang, Yunpeng Jiang, Yize Huang, Shujia Li, Xiao Li, Yutong Ban

entry.summary: Introduces DSSP, a history-conditioned diffusion policy using State Space Models (SSMs) to efficiently compress full observation histories for robot manipulation. Addresses the limitation of existing diffusion policies that only condition on short observation windows.

entry.title: CoRDS: Coreset-based Representative and Diverse Selection for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Ailar Mahdizadeh, Puria Azadi, Muchen Li, Xiangteng He, Leonid Sigal

entry.summary: Proposes CoRDS, viewing KV-cache compression in streaming video VLMs as a coreset selection problem. Selects a representative subset that covers the geometry of accumulated visual cache rather than using local token-wise heuristics.

entry.title: Mitigating Mask Prior Drift and Positional Attention Collapse in Large Diffusion Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sujung Hong, Chanyong Yoon, Seongjae Hwang

entry.summary: Identifies two problems in large diffusion vision-language models (LDVLMs) for long-form generation: mask token prior drift causing repetition, and positional attention misalignment degrading visual grounding. Proposes solutions for both.

entry.title: EponaV2: Driving World Model with Comprehensive Future Reasoning

author.name: Jiawei Xu, Zhizhou Zhong, Zhijian Shu, Mingkai Jia, Mingxiao Li, Jia-Wang Bian, Qian Zhang, Kaicheng Zhang, Jin Xie, Jian Yang, Wei Yin

entry.summary: Proposes EponaV2, a driving world model paradigm that achieves high-quality planning through comprehensive future reasoning beyond just next-frame prediction, without requiring expensive manual annotations for trajectory supervision.

entry.title: Language-Induced Priors for Domain Adaptation

author.name: Qiyuan Chen, Jiayu Zhou, Raed Al Kontar

entry.summary: Proposes Language-Induced Priors (LIP) for domain adaptation in cold-start settings, using expert textual descriptions and LLM preferences to identify relevant source domains when target data is scarce. Integrates into an EM algorithm for source relevance identification.

entry.title: AIS: Adaptive Importance Sampling for Quantized RL

author.name: Jiajun Zhou, Wei Shao, Lingchao Zheng, Yuwei Fan, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Importance Sampling (AIS) for quantized RL with LLMs, addressing the rollout-training mismatch when using FP8 rollouts with BF16 training. Shows the mismatch provides early exploration bonus but later destabilizes training.

entry.title: Rethinking the Good Enough Embedding for Easy Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Michael Karnes, Alper Yilmaz

entry.summary: Demonstrates that off-the-shelf frozen DINOv2 embeddings with k-NN classification are sufficient for few-shot learning tasks, arguing that universal representations have converged enough to make task-specific fine-tuning unnecessary. Connects to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.

entry.title: SceneForge: Structured World Supervision from 3D Interventions

author.name: Jizhizi Li, Jiayang Ao, Danny Wicks, Petru-Daniel Tudosiu

entry.summary: Presents SceneForge, an intervention-driven framework generating structured supervision from editable 3D world states. Applies explicit interventions (object removal, camera variation) and propagates effects through scene dependencies for consistent multi-view supervision.

entry.title: SceneFunRI: Reasoning the Invisible for Task-Driven Functional Object Localization

author.name: Posheng Chen, Powen Cheng, Gueter Josmy Faure, Hung-Ting Su, Winston H. Hsu

entry.summary: Introduces SceneFunRI benchmark for reasoning about invisible (occluded) functional objects in 3D scenes from task instructions and commonsense knowledge. Best baseline achieves only 15.20% accuracy, revealing a major capability gap.

entry.title: Think Twice, Act Once: Verifier-Guided Action Selection For Embodied Agents

author.name: Nishad Singhi, Christian Bialas, Snehal Jauhri, Vignesh Prasad, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Marcus Rohrbach, Anna Rohrbach

entry.summary: VegAS proposes a test-time framework that improves robustness of MLLM-based embodied agents by sampling candidate actions and using a generative verifier to select the best one, rather than committing to a single decoded action. This addresses brittleness in out-of-distribution scenarios for embodied AI.

entry.title: Hierarchical Attacks for Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Hao Zhou, Tiru Wu, Yan Jiang, Wanqi Zhou, Junxing Hu, Ai Han

entry.summary: HAM³ introduces a hierarchical attack framework for multi-modal multi-agent systems decomposed into perception, reasoning, and communication layers. Addresses the largely unexplored vulnerability space of MM-MAS.

entry.title: Differentiable Learning of Lifted Action Schemas for Classical Planning

author.name: Jonas Reiter, Jakob Elias Gebler, Hector Geffner

entry.summary: Develops a differentiable neural network architecture for learning lifted action schemas from traces where states are fully observed but action arguments are unknown, enabling classical planning with learned domain models.

entry.title: Ego2World: Compiling Egocentric Cooking Videos into Executable Worlds for Belief-State Planning

author.name: Qinchuan Cheng, Zhantao Gong, Pengzhan Sun, Angela Yao, Xulei Yang, Shijie Li

entry.summary: Ego2World turns egocentric cooking videos into executable symbolic worlds with graph-transition rules, creating a benchmark that bridges passive egocentric video datasets with interactive simulators for testing embodied agents under partial observation.

entry.title: ToolWeave: Structured Synthesis of Complex Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Dialogues

author.name: Dinesh Khandelwal, Gnana Prakash Punnavajhala, GPS Bhargav, Gaurav Pandey, Sachin Joshi, Hima Karanam, Dinesh Raghu

entry.summary: ToolWeave addresses the challenge of synthesizing realistic multi-turn tool-calling training dialogues by ensuring tools are chained based on meaningful user tasks rather than superficial compatibility, preventing argument hallucination.

entry.title: Information as Maximum-Caliber Deviation: A bridge between Integrated Information Theory and the Free Energy Principle

author.name: Alexander Kearney

entry.summary: Proposes a mathematical bridge between Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and the Free Energy Principle (FEP) by defining information as deviation from maximum-caliber path ensembles, showing IIT's cause/effect repertoires emerge from MaxCal variational inference.

entry.title: DistractMIA: Black-Box Membership Inference on Vision-Language Models via Semantic Distraction

author.name: Hongyi Tang, Zhihao Zhu, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Introduces DistractMIA, a black-box membership inference attack on VLMs using semantic distraction rather than mask-based approaches, working with only textual output observations.

entry.title: Bayesian Model Merging

author.name: Kaiyang Li, Shaobo Han, Qing Su, Shihao Ji

entry.summary: Introduces Bayesian Model Merging (BMM), a plug-and-play bi-level optimization framework that leverages anchor model priors and activation-based Bayesian regression for merging task-specific models.

entry.title: Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks Using Survival Analysis

author.name: Zvi Topol

entry.summary: Applies survival analysis to model time-to-jailbreak of LLMs under persistent adversarial pressure, enabling estimation of hazard functions and risk factors rather than binary success/failure metrics.

entry.title: Embodied Multi-Agent Coordination by Aligning World Models Through Dialogue

author.name: Vardhan Dongre, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: Extends the PARTNR benchmark with natural-language dialogue for embodied multi-agent coordination, examining whether LLM-based agents can effectively communicate to align world models under partial observability.

entry.title: FeatCal: Feature Calibration for Post-Merging Models

author.name: Yanggan Gu, Shuo Cai, Zihao Wang, Wenjun Wang, Yuanyi Wang, Pengkai Wang, Sirui Huang, Su Lu, Jianmin Wu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: Proposes FeatCal for calibrating merged model weights layer by layer to reduce feature drift between merged and expert models. Provides theoretical decomposition of drift into upstream propagation and local mismatch components.

entry.title: AcquisitionSynthesis: Targeted Data Generation using Acquisition Functions

author.name: Ishika Agarwal, Sofia Stoica, Emre Can Acikgoz, Pradeep Natarajan, Mahdi Namazifar, Jiaqi Ma, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: Uses acquisition functions from active learning to guide targeted synthetic data generation for LLM training. Proposes quantitative measurement of how generated samples impact the downstream learner, addressing a gap in current data synthesis approaches.

entry.title: Discovery of Hidden Miscalibration Regimes

author.name: Katarzyna Kobalczyk, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: Formulates the problem of discovering hidden miscalibration regimes in ML models without predefined data slices. Proposes a diagnostic framework that learns calibration-aware input representations and estimates signed local miscalibration.

entry.title: Self-Supervised On-Policy Reinforcement Learning via Contrastive Proximal Policy Optimisation

author.name: Asim Osman, Sasha Abramowitz, Mark Bergh, Ulrich Armel Mbou Sob, Ruan John de Kock, Omayma Mahjoub, Oussama Hidaoui, Noah De Nicola, Arnol Manuel Fokam, Felix Chalumeau, Daniel Rajaonarivonivelomanantsoa, Siddarth Singh, Refiloe Shabe, Juan Claude Formanek, Simon Verster Du Toit, Arnu Pretorius

entry.summary: Introduces Contrastive Proximal Policy Optimization (CPPO), bringing contrastive RL to on-policy training for the first time. Enables self-supervised goal-conditioned RL without hand-crafted rewards in both continuous and discrete action spaces.

entry.title: Identifying AI Web Scrapers Using Canary Tokens

author.name: Steven Seiden, Triss Ren, Caroline Zhang, Taein Kim, Enze Liu, Emily Wenger

entry.summary: Develops a canary token system to identify AI web scrapers—embedding hidden markers in web content that can be detected when they appear in LLM outputs, helping website owners identify which companies are scraping their data.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of EEG Foundation Models via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: William Lehn-Schi{\o}ler, Magnus Ruud Kj{\ae}r, Rahul Thapa, Magnus Guldberg Pedersen, Anton Storgaard Mosquera, Nick Williams, Radu Gatej, Tue Lehn-Schi{\o}ler, S\'andor Beniczky, Sadasivan Puthusserypady, James Zou, Lars Kai Hansen

entry.summary: Applies sparse autoencoders to three architecturally distinct EEG foundation models (SleepFM, REVE, LaBraM) to extract interpretable feature dictionaries, benchmarking monosemanticity and enabling concept steering across clinical categories.

entry.title: A Unified Geometric Framework for Weighted Contrastive Learning

author.name: Raphael Vock, Edouard Duchesnay, Benoit Dufumier

entry.summary: Provides a unified geometric framework showing that weighted InfoNCE objectives can be interpreted as Distance Geometry Problems, yielding exact characterizations of optimal embeddings for supervised and weakly supervised contrastive learning.

entry.title: Towards Resource-Efficient LLMs: End-to-End Energy Accounting of Distillation Pipelines

author.name: Katherine Lambert, Sasha Luccioni

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive energy accounting framework measuring the full end-to-end computational cost of LLM distillation pipelines, including teacher-side costs like data generation, logit caching, and evaluation that are typically overlooked.

entry.title: EnergyLens: Predictive Energy-Aware Exploration for Multi-GPU LLM Inference Optimization

author.name: Zhiye Song, Kyungmi Lee, Eun Kyung Lee, Xin Zhang, Tamar Eilam, Anantha P. Chandrakasan

entry.summary: Presents EnergyLens, an end-to-end framework for predicting and optimizing energy consumption during multi-GPU LLM inference. Uses an einsum-based interface to capture model specifications and predict energy without expensive profiling.

entry.title: Beyond Binary: Reframing GUI Critique as Continuous Semantic Alignment

author.name: Yuchen Sun, Pei Fu, Shaojie Zhang, Anan Du, Xiuwen Xi, Ruoceng Zhang, Zhenbo Luo, Jian Luan, Chongyang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes BBCritic, moving beyond binary classification for GUI agent critique models to continuous semantic alignment. Addresses affordance collapse and noise sensitivity issues in existing binary critics used for test-time scaling of GUI agents.

entry.title: NodeSynth: Socially Aligned Synthetic Data for AI Evaluation

author.name: Qazi Mamunur Rashid, Xuan Yang, Zhengzhe Yang, Yanzhou Pan, Erin van Liemt, Darlene Neal, Kshitij Pancholi, Jamila Smith-Loud

entry.summary: Introduces NodeSynth, a methodology for generating socially relevant synthetic queries for AI evaluation using a fine-tuned taxonomy generator grounded in real-world evidence. Achieves failure rates up to 5x higher than human-authored benchmarks against major LLMs.

entry.title: RxEval: A Prescription-Level Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Medication Recommendation

author.name: Shuhao Chen, Weisen Jiang, Changmiao Wang, Xiaoqing Wu, Xuanren Shi, Yu Zhang, James T. Kwok

entry.summary: Introduces RxEval, a prescription-level benchmark evaluating LLM prescribing capability through multiple-choice questions based on real patient profiles and clinical trajectories. Uses reasoning-chain perturbation for generating patient-specific distractors.

entry.title: XFP: Quality-Targeted Adaptive Codebook Quantization with Sparse Outlier Separation for LLM Inference

author.name: Thomas Witt

entry.summary: Introduces XFP, a dynamic weight quantizer for LLM inference that lets users specify quality floors (cosine similarity) and automatically determines codebook size, outlier budget, and packing. Tested on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, eliminating need for Hessian computation or calibration data.

entry.title: Separating Intrinsic Ambiguity from Estimation Uncertainty in Deep Generative Models for Linear Inverse Problems

author.name: Yuxin Guo, Dongrui Deng, Pulkit Grover

entry.summary: Introduces a structural decomposition of posterior uncertainty in deep generative models for inverse problems, separating intrinsic ambiguity (from the forward operator) from estimation uncertainty (from inference). Enables calibration diagnostics revealing hidden failure modes.

entry.title: When Are Two Networks the Same? Tensor Similarity for Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: ML Nissen Gonzalez, Melwina Albuquerque, Laurence Wroe, Jacob Meyer Cohen, Logan Riggs Smith, Thomas Dooms

entry.summary: Introduces tensor similarity, a weight-based metric for comparing neural networks that is invariant to weight-space symmetries, capturing functional equivalence. Tracks training dynamics like grokking and backdoor insertion.

entry.title: Hidden State Poisoning Attacks against Mamba-based Language Models

author.name: Alexandre Le Mercier, Chris Develder, Thomas Demeester

entry.summary: Studies Hidden State Poisoning Attacks (HiSPA) against Mamba and SSM-based language models, showing that short input phrases can cause partial amnesia by irreversibly overwriting hidden states. Even Jamba-1.7-Mini hybrid model is vulnerable.

entry.title: ProtoMedAgent: Multimodal Clinical Interpretability via Privacy-Aware Agentic Workflows

author.name: Alvaro Lopez Pellicer, Plamen Angelov, Marwan Bukhari, Yi Li, Eduardo Soares, Jemma Kerns

entry.summary: Introduces ProtoMedAgent, a framework for clinical reporting that addresses 'retrieval sycophancy' in RAG by formalizing multimodal clinical reporting as iterative test-time optimization over a neuro-symbolic bottleneck. Operates on frozen prototype backbone with discrete semantic memory.

entry.title: Training-Free Generative Sampling via Moment-Matched Score Smoothing

author.name: Zhenyu Yao, Daniel Paulin

entry.summary: Proposes MM-SOLD, a training-free particle sampler for generative modeling that enforces target moments throughout sampling. Proves convergence in the large-particle limit to a Gibbs-Boltzmann density, offering an alternative to trained diffusion models.

entry.title: Large Dimensional Kernel Ridge Regression: Extending to Product Kernels

author.name: Yang Zhou, Yicheng Li, Yuqian Cheng, Qian Lin

entry.summary: Extends kernel ridge regression theory to product kernels in large dimensions, recovering saturation effects and multiple descent behavior previously known only for inner product kernels on spheres. Establishes convergence rates for a broader kernel family.

entry.title: SpeakerLLM: A Speaker-Specialized Audio-LLM for Speaker Understanding and Verification Reasoning

author.name: KiHyun Nam, Jungwoo Heo, Siu Bae, Ha-Jin Yu, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: Presents SpeakerLLM, a speaker-specialized audio-LLM that unifies speaker verification, profiling, and reasoning. Aims to provide linguistic evidence alongside verification scores for user authorization and personalization in audio-first agents.

entry.title: Logging Policy Design for Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Connor Douglas, Joel Persson, Foster Provost

entry.summary: Studies logging policy design for off-policy evaluation, characterizing a reward-coverage tradeoff and proposing optimal policies in canonical informational regimes. Provides a unifying framework for minimizing OPE error.

entry.title: RefDecoder: Enhancing Visual Generation with Conditional Video Decoding

author.name: Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Bohan Fang, Zhongzheng Ren, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Introduces RefDecoder, a reference-conditioned video VAE decoder that injects high-fidelity reference image signals via reference attention to preserve detail and consistency in video generation, addressing the asymmetry between heavily conditioned denoisers and unconditional decoders.

entry.title: Mechanical Enforcement for LLM Governance:Evidence of Governance-Task Decoupling in Financial Decision Systems

author.name: Jos\'e Manuel de la Chica Rodr\'iguez, Carlos Mart\'i-Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: Introduces governance metrics for LLM compliance in financial systems, comparing text-only governance against mechanical enforcement primitives operating outside the model's interpretive loop. Finds 27% of deferrals under text-only governance carry no decision-relevant information, while mechanical enforcement achieves better compliance.

entry.title: From Scenes to Elements: Multi-Granularity Evidence Retrieval for Verifiable Multimodal RAG

author.name: Guanhua Chen, Chuyue Huang, Yutong Yao, Shudong Liu, Xueqing Song, Lidia S. Chao, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: Introduces GranuVistaVQA benchmark and GranuRAG framework for multi-granularity evidence retrieval in multimodal RAG, treating visual elements as first-class retrieval units. Addresses the mismatch between coarse retrieval granularity and fine-grained queries.

entry.title: GraphBit: A Graph-based Agentic Framework for Non-Linear Agent Orchestration

author.name: Yeahia Sarker, Md Rahmat Ullah, Musa Molla, Shafiq Joty

entry.summary: Introduces GraphBit, an engine-orchestrated agentic framework using DAGs for deterministic workflow execution, contrasting with prompted orchestration. Uses a Rust-based engine for routing, state transitions, and tool invocation with a three-tier memory architecture.

entry.title: MemEye: A Visual-Centric Evaluation Framework for Multimodal Agent Memory

author.name: Minghao Guo, Qingyue Jiao, Zeru Shi, Yihao Quan, Boxuan Zhang, Danrui Li, Liwei Che, Wujiang Xu, Shilong Liu, Zirui Liu, Mubbasir Kapadia, Vladimir Pavlovic, Jiang Liu, Mengdi Wang, Yiyu Shi, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Ruixiang Tang

entry.summary: Introduces MemEye, a framework evaluating multimodal agent memory along two dimensions: granularity of visual evidence (scene to pixel level) and how evidence must be used (single to evolutionary synthesis). Addresses the gap where text-based traces suffice for current benchmarks.

entry.title: SToRe3D: Sparse Token Relevance in ViTs for Efficient Multi-View 3D Object Detection

author.name: Sandro Papais, Lezhou Feng, Charles Cossette, Lingting Ge

entry.summary: Introduces SToRe3D, a relevance-aligned sparsity framework for multi-view 3D object detection that jointly selects 2D image tokens and 3D object queries while preserving filtered features for reactivation. Achieves up to 3x faster inference with marginal accuracy loss on nuScenes.

entry.title: CoReDiT: Spatial Coherence-Guided Token Pruning and Reconstruction for Efficient Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Zhuojin Li, Hsin-Pai Cheng, Hong Cai, Shizhong Han, Fatih Porikli

entry.summary: Introduces CoReDiT, a structured token pruning framework for Diffusion Transformers that uses spatial coherence scores to identify redundant tokens and reconstructs them via coherence-guided aggregation. Features progressive, block-adaptive pruning schedules.

entry.title: A Picture is Worth a Thousand Words? An Empirical Study of Aggregation Strategies for Visual Financial Document Retrieval

author.name: Ho Hung Lim, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Studies single-vector aggregation of vision patch tokens for financial document retrieval in Visual RAG, finding that aggregation collapses different documents into nearly identical vectors when single-digit changes cause semantic shifts.

entry.title: ViMU: Benchmarking Video Metaphorical Understanding

author.name: Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces ViMU benchmark for video metaphorical understanding, evaluating whether models can grasp implicit meanings, emotions, and social messages conveyed through video beyond surface-level content.

entry.title: Beyond Instance-Level Self-Supervision in 3D Multi-Modal Medical Imaging

author.name: Tan Pan, Shuhao Mei, Yixuan Sun, Kaiyu Guo, Chen Jiang, Zhaorui Tan, Mengzhu Li, Limei Han, Xiang Zou, Yuan Cheng, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh

entry.summary: Proposes leveraging cross-instance topological consistency of anatomical structures as a supervisory signal for self-supervised pretraining in 3D multi-modal medical imaging, going beyond instance-level objectives.

entry.title: Probing into Camera Control of Video Models

author.name: Chen Hou, Christian Rupprecht

entry.summary: This paper reframes camera control in video generation models from an implicit mapping problem to geometric guidance that induces displacement fields, showing that strong video priors already encode camera-responsive behavior without requiring large paired camera-video datasets.

entry.title: MemLens: Benchmarking Multimodal Long-Term Memory in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xiyu Ren, Zhaowei Wang, Yiming Du, Zhongwei Xie, Chi Liu, Xinlin Yang, Haoyue Feng, Wenjun Pan, Tianshi Zheng, Baixuan Xu, Zhengnan Li, Yangqiu Song, Ginny Wong, Simon See

entry.summary: MEMLENS introduces a comprehensive benchmark for multimodal long-term memory in vision-language models, comparing long-context LVLMs vs. memory-augmented agents across 789 questions spanning five memory abilities at four context lengths.

entry.title: RAVEN: Real-time Autoregressive Video Extrapolation with Consistency-model GRPO

author.name: Yanzuo Lu, Ronglai Zuo, Jiankang Deng

entry.summary: RAVEN introduces a training-time test framework for real-time autoregressive video extrapolation that addresses the history distribution mismatch between training and inference through interleaved rollout repacking and consistency-model GRPO.

entry.title: Meschers: Geometry Processing of Impossible Objects

author.name: Ana Dodik, Isabella Yu, Kartik Chandra, Jonathan Ragan-Kelley, Joshua Tenenbaum, Vincent Sitzmann, Justin Solomon

entry.summary: Meschers introduces a mesh representation for impossible objects (like Escher drawings) that avoids cutting or bending, enabling standard geometry processing operations on these paradoxical constructions.

entry.title: Darwin Family: MRI-Trust-Weighted Evolutionary Merging for Training-Free Scaling of Language-Model Reasoning

author.name: Taebong Kim, Youngsik Hong, Minsik Kim, Sunyoung Choi, Jaewon Jang, Junghoon Shin, Minseo Kim

entry.summary: Darwin Family proposes training-free evolutionary merging of LLMs through gradient-free weight-space recombination, introducing a 14-dimensional merge genome, MRI-Trust Fusion, and cross-architecture breeding to improve reasoning without additional training.

entry.title: Safety-Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Post-Training Reachability Verification for Robot Navigation

author.name: Qisong He, Xinmiao Huang, Jinwei Hu, Zhuoyun Li, Yi Dong, Changshun Wu, Xiaowei Huang

entry.summary: Proposes a safe RL framework combining CVaR-constrained policy optimization on TD3 with post-training neural network reachability verification for robot navigation. Addresses the limitation of average-cost safety metrics that can mask dangerous tail-risk behaviors.

entry.title: SR-Platform: An Agentic Pipeline for Natural Language-Driven Robot Simulation Environment Synthesis

author.name: Ben Wei Lim, Minh Duc Le, Thang Truong, Thanh Nguyen Canh

entry.summary: Presents SR-Platform, an LLM-based agentic system that converts natural language descriptions into physically valid MuJoCo simulation environments. Decomposes scene synthesis into orchestration, asset generation, layout, and verification stages.

entry.title: Models finding software vulnerabilities is not the primary source of cybersecurity risk

author.name: lc

entry.summary: Argues that AI's primary cybersecurity risk is not finding new vulnerabilities but rather automating exploitation at scale—weaponizing recently patched exploits, automating social engineering, and enabling mass-scale attacks that were previously bottlenecked by human labor.

entry.title: MAP: A Map-then-Act Paradigm for Long-Horizon Interactive Agent Reasoning

author.name: Yuxin Liu, Ziang Ye, Yueqing Sun, Mingye Zhu, Jinwei Xiao, Zhuowen Han, Qi GU, Xunliang Cai, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: MAP proposes a Map-then-Act paradigm for LLM agents that shifts environment understanding before execution through global exploration and task-specific cognitive mapping, inspired by human affordance perception.

entry.title: Improving Code Translation with Syntax-Guided and Semantic-aware Preference Optimization

author.name: Yuhan Wu, Huan Zhang, Wei Cheng, Chen Shen, Jingyue Yang, Wei Hu

entry.summary: CTO improves code translation by training a cross-lingual semantic model through contrastive learning to assess functional equivalence between source and translated code, combined with syntax-guided preference optimization.

entry.title: Assessing the Creativity of Large Language Models: Testing, Limits, and New Frontiers

author.name: Samuel Schapiro, Alexi Gladstone, Jonah Black, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Conducts the first large-scale systematic study assessing whether human creativity tests validly measure LLM creative capabilities across divergent thinking, convergent thinking, and creative writing, finding limitations in test validity.

entry.title: MMSkills: Towards Multimodal Skills for General Visual Agents

author.name: Kangning Zhang, Shuai Shao, Qingyao Li, Jianghao Lin, Lingyue Fu, Shijian Wang, Wenxiang Jiao, Yuan Lu, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu

entry.summary: MMSkills formalizes multimodal procedural knowledge for visual agents, defining what a multimodal skill package should contain, how to derive them from public interaction data, and how agents can consult multimodal evidence during execution.

entry.title: Beyond Individual Mimicry: Constructing Human-Like Social network with Graph-Augmented LLM Agents

author.name: Haoran Bu, Litian Zhang, Chuxuan Zhang, Zhanyuan Liu, Hui Pang, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: GraphMind equips LLM-driven social bots with graph-awareness to fit human-like social network structures, making botnets more resistant to GNN-based detection. Evaluates as a red-teaming tool for bot detection research.

entry.title: Visual Aesthetic Benchmark: Can Frontier Models Judge Beauty?
