entry.summary: Identifies two training timescales in generative models: τ_rule (when generations become rule-valid) and τ_mem (when models memorize training samples). Characterizes how dataset size, model capacity, and rule complexity affect the 'innovation window' between them.

entry.title: PowerStep: Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimization via $\ell_p$-Norm Steepest Descent

author.name: Yao Lu, Dengdong Fan, Shixun Zhang, Yonghong Tian

entry.summary: Introduces PowerStep, a memory-efficient optimizer achieving coordinate-wise adaptivity without second-moment statistics, motivated by steepest descent under ℓp-norm geometry. Tested on models up to 235B parameters with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: bViT: Investigating Single-Block Recurrence in Vision Transformers for Image Recognition

author.name: Michal Byra, Pawel Olszowiec, Grzegorz Stefanski, Grzegorz Gruszczynski, Alberto Presta

entry.summary: Proposes bViT, a single-block recurrent Vision Transformer that applies one transformer block repeatedly, achieving comparable accuracy to standard ViT-B on ImageNet-1K with an order of magnitude fewer parameters. Demonstrates that much of ViT depth can be replaced by recurrent computation.

entry.title: SWE Atlas: Benchmarking Coding Agents Beyond Issue Resolution

author.name: Mohit Raghavendra, Soham Dan, Miguel Romero Calvo, Yannis Yiming He, Johannes Baptist Mols, Gautam Anand, Cole McCollum, Edgar Arakelyan, Vijay Bharadwaj, Andrew Park, Jeff Da, MohammadHossein Rezaei, Bing Liu, Brad Kenstler, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: Introduces SWE Atlas, a benchmark for coding agents spanning three professional workflows: Codebase Q&A, Test Writing, and Refactoring. Goes beyond issue resolution to evaluate software engineering quality including maintainability and reusable abstractions.

entry.title: Can Revealed Preferences Clarify LLM Alignment and Steering?

author.name: Khurram Yamin, Jingjing Tang, Eric Horvitz, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: Presents an empirical pipeline for estimating LLM implied preferences through revealed-preference analysis, fitting discrete choice models to recover cost functions that rationalize model decisions.

entry.title: Muon Does Not Converge on Convex Lipschitz Functions

author.name: Tetiana Parshakova, Ahmed Khaled, Michael Crawshaw, Guillaume Garrigos, Robert M. Gower

entry.summary: Proves that the Muon optimizer does not converge on the class of convex Lipschitz functions regardless of learning rate schedule, and shows that error feedback restores convergence. This challenges using classical convex analysis to understand Muon.

entry.title: CALYREX: Cross-Attention LaYeR EXtended Transformers for System Prompt Anchoring

author.name: Li Lixing

entry.summary: Proposes CALYREX, a cross-attention mechanism that structurally isolates system prompts from user content in LLMs to resist prompt injection and instruction erosion. Placement ablation identifies optimal insertion at the final eighth of layers.

entry.title: What should post-training optimize? A test-time scaling law perspective

author.name: Muheng Li, Jian Qian, Wenlong Mou

entry.summary: Studies how post-training objectives should be designed when models are deployed with best-of-N test-time strategies, revealing a mismatch between standard mean-reward training and deployment that requires upper-tail optimization. Provides scaling laws for the budget-mismatch regime where training rollouts m << N deployment samples.

entry.title: Kinetic theory for Transformers and the lost-in-the-middle phenomenon

author.name: Mitia Duerinckx, Borjan Geshkovski, Stefano Rossi

entry.summary: Provides rigorous mathematical explanation of the 'lost-in-the-middle' phenomenon in Transformers through kinetic theory, proving the U-shaped token retrieval profile emerges from causal self-attention dynamics.

entry.title: When Routine Chats Turn Toxic: Unintended Long-Term State Poisoning in Personalized Agents

author.name: Xiaoyu Xu, Minxin Du, Qipeng Xie, Haobin Ke, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: Formalizes 'unintended long-term state poisoning' where routine user-agent interactions gradually reshape an agent's persistent state, weakening confirmation boundaries and expanding autonomous behavior. Introduces ULSPB benchmark with 350 settings.

entry.title: When Are Experts Misrouted? Counterfactual Routing Analysis in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Youngsik Yoon, Siwei Wang, Wei Chen, Jungseul Ok

entry.summary: Analyzes MoE routing quality by comparing standard routes against sampled alternatives, finding routers work well on confident tokens but are uninformative on fragile reasoning tokens where better routes consistently exist.

entry.title: Belief or Circuitry? Causal Evidence for In-Context Graph Learning

author.name: Katharine Kowalyshyn, Timothy Duggan, Daniel Little, Michael C Hughes

entry.summary: Uses causal interventions on transformer internals to investigate whether LLMs perform in-context learning via pattern matching or latent structure inference on graph random walks. Finds evidence that both mechanisms coexist in orthogonal subspaces.

entry.title: How You Begin is How You Reason: Driving Exploration in RLVR via Prefix-Tuned Priors

author.name: Yifan Xu, Junren Chen, Yifan Chen

entry.summary: Proposes IMAX framework to address entropy collapse in RLVR by training soft prefixes that reshape the base model's prior over reasoning trajectories, enabling more diverse exploration without degrading generation quality.

entry.title: EnactToM: An Evolving Benchmark for Functional Theory of Mind in Embodied Agents

author.name: Gurusha Juneja, Dylan Lu, Saaket Agashe, Parth Diwane, Edward Gunn, Jayanth Srinivasa, Gaowen Liu, William Yang Wang, Yali Du, Xin Eric Wang

entry.summary: Introduces EnactToM, an evolving benchmark of 300 embodied multi-agent tasks testing functional Theory of Mind - acting optimally on implicit beliefs rather than just answering belief questions. All 7 frontier models score below 50% on hard split.

entry.title: Sanity Checks for Long-Form Hallucination Detection

author.name: Geigh Zollicoffer, Minh Vu, Hongli Zhan, Raymond Li, Manish Bhattarai

entry.summary: Introduces controlled-invariance tests (FORCE and REMOVE) for hallucination detection methods, revealing that many methods exploit answer-level artifacts rather than evaluating reasoning quality in chain-of-thought traces.

entry.title: BubbleSpec: Turning Long-Tail Bubbles into Speculative Rollout Drafts for Synchronous Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuhang Xu, Kaibin Tian, Yang Tian, Zhice Yang, Yifeng Yu, Yan Li, Shengzhong Liu, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: BubbleSpec exploits idle GPU time (long-tail bubbles) in synchronous RL rollouts for LLM training by using faster GPUs for speculative rollout drafts during wait times, maintaining mathematical exactness of synchronous RL while improving efficiency.

entry.title: Break the Brake, Not the Wheel: Untargeted Jailbreak via Entropy Maximization

author.name: Mengqi He, Xinyu Tian, Xin Shen, Shu Zou, Jinhong Ni, Zhaoyuan Yang, Weikang Li, Xuesong Li, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes UJEM-KL, a lightweight jailbreak attack on vision-language models that maximizes entropy at decision tokens to flip refusal behavior. Demonstrates cross-model transferability that was previously thought infeasible.

entry.title: RubiConv -- Efficient Boundary-Respecting Convolutions

author.name: Linda Friso, Annie Marsden, Xinyi Chen, Arushi Gupta, Peter Bartlett, Mark Braverman, Elad Hazan

entry.summary: Introduces RubiConv, efficient boundary-respecting convolutions that work with document packing in large-scale training pipelines. Closes the gap between theoretical FFT efficiency and practical convolutional architecture performance.

entry.title: Why Retrying Fails: Context Contamination in LLM Agent Pipelines

author.name: Zhanfu Yang

entry.summary: Formalizes the 'context contamination' problem where failed LLM agent attempts remaining in context elevate error rates in subsequent retries. Derives closed-form formulas for success probability and optimal retry strategies under contamination.

entry.title: Reasoning Compression with Mixed-Policy Distillation

author.name: Han Yang, Mingyan Wu, Bailan He, Zeyu Cao, Sikuan Yan, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Zifeng Ding

entry.summary: Proposes Mixed-Policy Distillation to compress reasoning traces from large models into smaller ones, observing that larger models produce more concise reasoning and transferring this compression ability rather than enforcing length constraints.

entry.title: Agentic AI Scientists Are Not Built For Autonomous Scientific Discovery

author.name: Harshit Bisht, Vinay Kumar, Kevin Maik Jablonka, Mausam, N. M. Anoop Krishnan

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that agentic AI scientists are not built for autonomous scientific discovery due to four challenges: McNamara fallacy in problem selection, missing tacit knowledge, preference optimization compressing diversity, and inadequate benchmarks.

entry.title: Workspace Optimization: How to Train Your Agent

author.name: Elad Sarafian, Gal Kaplun, Ron Banner, Daniel Soudry, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: Proposes 'workspace optimization' - evolving an agent's structured external substrate (artifacts, evidence, counterexamples, feedback) as the trainable component when model weights are frozen. Instantiates in DreamTeam, a multi-agent system.

entry.title: Memorize Theorems, Not Instances: Probing SFT Generalization through Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Ruiying Peng, Mengyu Yang, Jing Lei, Xiaohui Li, Xueyu Wu, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Theorem-SFT, which reorients supervised fine-tuning supervision toward explicit theorem application rather than problem-solution pairs. Achieves +8.8% on MATH and +20.27% on GeoQA by teaching models how rules are invoked rather than what answers look like.

entry.title: OTora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework for Reasoning-Level Denial-of-Service in LLM Agents

author.name: Xinyu Li, Ronghui Mu, Lin Li, Tianjin Huang, Gaojie Jin

entry.summary: Introduces OTora, the first unified red-teaming framework for Reasoning-Level Denial-of-Service attacks against LLM agents, where attackers preserve task correctness but inflate reasoning depth and tool-use budget.

entry.title: Beyond Language: Format-Agnostic Reasoning Subspaces in Large Language Models

author.name: Aojie Yuan, Zhiyuan Su

entry.summary: Discovers Format-Agnostic Reasoning Subspaces (FARS) in LLMs - a shared 10-dimensional internal representation that encodes reasoning concepts identically regardless of whether expressed as English, code, or math notation.

entry.title: Embeddings for Preferences, Not Semantics

author.name: Carter Blair, Ariel D. Procaccia, Milind Tambe

entry.summary: Proposes 'preferential embeddings' distinct from semantic embeddings for collective decision-making, where distance measures agreement rather than topical similarity. Bridges text embedding with facility location and fair clustering literature for democratic deliberation applications.

entry.title: Mid-Training with Self-Generated Data Improves Reinforcement Learning in Language Models

author.name: Aswin RRV, Jacob Dineen, Divij Handa, Mihir Parmar, Ben Zhou, Swaroop Mishra, Chitta Baral

entry.summary: Shows that mid-training with diverse self-generated data (using Polya's problem-solving approaches) before RL significantly improves reasoning performance. Demonstrates that exposure to diverse solution strategies enhances subsequent RL training.

entry.title: Can We Formally Verify Neural PDE Surrogates? SMT Compilation of Small Fourier Neural Operators

author.name: Ali Baheri, David Millard, Ignacio Laguna Peralta

entry.summary: Shows that Fourier Neural Operators are piecewise-linear (once weights are fixed) and can be exactly compiled into Z3 SMT solver for formal verification. Demonstrates property checking on small FNOs for advection-diffusion-reaction.

entry.title: Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue? Investigating Reasoning through the Lens of Personas

author.name: Nils A. Herrmann, Leander Girrbach, Kirill Bykov, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs experience an 'internal polylogue' - time series of alignments between persona vectors and hidden activations during generation. Shows these dynamic persona signals predict correctness on MMLU-Pro and enable interpretable interventions.

entry.title: SciIntegrity-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Academic Integrity in AI Scientist Systems

author.name: Zonglin Yang, Xingtong Liu, Xinyan Xu

entry.summary: Introduces SciIntegrity-Bench, the first benchmark evaluating academic integrity of AI scientist systems. Uses dilemmatic scenarios where honest acknowledgment of failure is the only correct response. Finds 34.2% integrity problem rate across 7 SOTA LLMs.

entry.title: Verifiable Process Rewards for Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Huining Yuan, Zelai Xu, Huaijie Wang, Xiangmin Yi, Jiaxuan Gao, Xiao-Ping Zhang, Yu Wang, Chao Yu, Yi Wu

entry.summary: Proposes Verifiable Process Rewards (VPR), a framework that converts symbolic/algorithmic oracles into dense turn-level supervision for RL in agentic reasoning. Addresses sparse credit assignment in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Playing Games with My Heart: An Evaluation of AI Companion Apps

author.name: Maribeth Rauh, Dick A. H. Blankvoort, Matias Duran, Caoilfhionn N\'i Dheor\'ain, Harshvardhan J. Pandit, Siddharth D. Jaiswal, Anthony Ventresque, Abeba Birhane

entry.summary: Evaluates the five most popular AI companion mobile apps in EU/UK markets for dark patterns, anthropomorphism, and manipulation tactics that encourage parasocial interaction. Systematically records and quantifies design features that may cause psychological harm.

entry.title: In-Context Fixation: When Demonstrated Labels Override Semantics in Few-Shot Classification

author.name: Ming Liu

entry.summary: Demonstrates 'in-context fixation': when few-shot demonstrations have homogeneous labels, LLMs collapse accuracy to ≤12% because models treat tokens in label positions as exhaustive answer vocabularies. Challenges Bayesian accounts of ICL.

entry.title: Defense effectiveness across architectural layers: a mechanistic evaluation of persistent memory attacks on stateful LLM agents

author.name: Jun Wen Leong

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates six defenses across four architectural layers against persistent memory attacks on LLM agents, finding that most defenses fail (88-89% ASR) while only system-prompt instructions show effectiveness.

entry.title: Uncovering Intra-expert Activation Sparsity for Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Model Execution

author.name: Jongseok Park, Sunga Kim, Zhenyu Gu, Ion Stoica, Alvin Cheung

entry.summary: Discovers and exploits intra-expert activation sparsity in pre-trained MoE models, finding up to 90% sparsity within each expert without architecture or training modifications, enabling additional inference speedups.

entry.title: AgentForesight: Online Auditing for Early Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Boxuan Zhang, Jianing Zhu, Zeru Shi, Dongfang Liu, Ruixiang Tang

entry.summary: AgentForesight reframes multi-agent failure detection as online auditing, where an auditor observes trajectory prefixes in real-time and must alarm at the earliest decisive error before failure cascades. Introduces AFTra dataset for this purpose.

entry.title: The Grounding Gap: How LLMs Anchor the Meaning of Abstract Concepts Differently from Humans

author.name: Odysseas S. Chlapanis, Orfeas Menis Mastromichalakis, Christos H. Papadimitriou

entry.summary: Studies how LLMs ground abstract concepts compared to humans by replicating cognitive science property-generation experiments. Finds LLMs over-rely on word associations and under-produce emotion/internal-state properties, with a large 'grounding gap' (max r=0.37 vs human ceiling >0.9).

entry.title: The Art of the Jailbreak: Formulating Jailbreak Attacks for LLM Security Beyond Binary Scoring

author.name: Ismail Hossain, Tanzim Ahad, Md Jahangir Alam, Sai Puppala, Syed Bahauddin Alam, Sajedul Talukder

entry.summary: Presents a large-scale jailbreak evaluation infrastructure with 114,000 adversarial prompts created by applying 912 composing strategies to 125 harmful seed prompts. Introduces a continuous scoring rubric beyond binary pass/fail and maps attacks to 14 cybersecurity categories.

entry.title: The Geometric Wall: Manifold Structure Predicts Layerwise Sparse Autoencoder Scaling Laws

author.name: Eslam Zaher, Maciej Trzaskowski, Quan Nguyen, Fred Roosta

entry.summary: Shows that sparse autoencoder reconstruction error varies sharply across layers due to geometric mismatch between activation manifold curvature and linear dictionaries. Derives layer-dependent scaling laws predicted by intrinsic dimension and curvature.

entry.title: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents

author.name: Seth Karten, Joel Zhang, Tersoo Upaa Jr, Ruirong Feng, Wenzhe Li, Chengshuai Shi, Chi Jin, Kiran Vodrahalli

entry.summary: Reports first AI system to complete Pokemon Blue, Yellow Legacy (hard mode), and Crystal without a lost battle using Gemini with iterative harness refinement. Proposes Continual Harness for reset-free self-improving embodied agents.

entry.title: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs

author.name: Krishak Aneja, Manas Mittal, Anmol Goel, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru, Vamshi Krishna Bonagiri

entry.summary: Maps latent personality space of LLMs through psychometric profiles and shows that emergent misalignment from fine-tuning can be understood and mitigated through semantic valence vectors in activation space.

entry.title: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions

author.name: Diancheng Kang, Zheyuan Liu, Ningshan Ma, Yue Huang, Zhaoxuan Tan, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: Identifies KV-cache contamination as a failure mode in activation steering for dialogue and proposes GCAD, which extracts steering signals from system-prompt contributions to self-attention with token-level gating. Substantially improves long-horizon coherence in persona-steering tasks.

entry.title: Unmasking On-Policy Distillation: Where It Helps, Where It Hurts, and Why

author.name: Mohammadreza Armandpour, Fatih Ilhan, David Harrison, Ajay Jaiswal, Duc N. M Hoang, Fartash Faghri, Yizhe Zhang, Minsik Cho, Mehrdad Farajtabar

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free diagnostic framework for understanding when on-policy distillation helps or hurts reasoning models, operating at per-token, per-question, and per-teacher resolution to identify optimal teaching signals.

entry.title: The Cancellation Hypothesis in Critic-Free RL: From Outcome Rewards to Token Credits

author.name: Tianhao Cheng, Zeyu Huang, Zihan Qiu, Yu Cheng, Edoardo Ponti, Yinghui Xu, Ivan Titov, Zenglin Xu

entry.summary: Reveals a 'token-flipping' phenomenon in critic-free RL: positive and negative rollouts show similar proportions of tokens boosted/suppressed. Explains this through coupled gradient interactions between identical tokens.

entry.title: From Mechanistic to Compositional Interpretability

author.name: Ward Gauderis, Thomas Dooms, Steven T. Holmer, Kola Ayonrinde, Geraint A. Wiggins

entry.summary: Introduces compositional interpretability, a category-theoretic framework for mechanistic interpretability that formalizes explanation quality into faithfulness and complexity measures, casting interpretability as constrained optimization.

entry.title: Predicting Large Model Test Losses with a Noisy Quadratic System

author.name: Chuning Li, Chris J. Maddison

entry.summary: Introduces a loss prediction model for LLM pre-training that handles variable batch sizes, outperforming Chinchilla's model for compute extrapolation up to 1000x. Can find optimal N, B, K configurations under compound resource constraints.

entry.title: Nectar: Neural Estimation of Cached-Token Attention via Regression

author.name: Jo\~ao Monteiro, Michal Klein, Pierre Ablin, Marco Cuturi

entry.summary: Proposes Nectar, which replaces O(n) KV-cache attention with a compact neural network that learns to predict attention outputs for a fixed long context. Fits per-layer networks whose cost is independent of context length.

entry.title: Self-Attention as a Covariance Readout: A Unified View of In-Context Learning and Repetition

author.name: Haoren Xu, Guanhua Fang

entry.summary: Proves that under stationary, ergodic, elliptical inputs, softmax attention converges to a linear readout of input covariance, unifying in-context learning and repetitive generation as consequences of this covariance readout behavior.

entry.title: Neural Weight Norm = Kolmogorov Complexity

author.name: Tiberiu Musat

entry.summary: Proves that in fixed-precision regimes, the smallest weight norm of a looped neural network outputting a binary string equals Kolmogorov complexity up to logarithmic factors. This implies weight decay induces a prior matching Solomonoff's universal prior.

entry.title: Repeated-Token Counting Reveals a Dissociation Between Representations and Outputs

author.name: Sohan Venkatesh

entry.summary: Reveals that LLMs internally encode correct counts of repeated tokens (shown by linear probes) but an MLP block overwrites this with incorrect outputs, demonstrating a dissociation between internal representations and model outputs.

entry.title: Beyond Reasoning: Reinforcement Learning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs

author.name: Wanli Yang, Hongyu Zang, Junwei Zhang, Wenjie Shi, Du Su, Jingang Wang, Xueqi Cheng, Fei Sun

entry.summary: Shows that RL training improves LLMs' direct factual recall (not just reasoning) by ~27% average relative gains in zero-shot closed-book QA. Mechanistically, RL redistributes probability mass over existing knowledge rather than acquiring new facts.

entry.title: Teaching Language Models to Think in Code

author.name: Hyeon Hwang, Jiwoo Lee, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: Proposes ThinC (Thinking in Code), a framework where code itself serves as the reasoner rather than being a tool invoked by natural language. After a brief NL planning step, all reasoning unfolds through code blocks, addressing limitations of interleaved NL/code approaches.

entry.title: Tool Calling is Linearly Readable and Steerable in Language Models

author.name: Zekun Wu (University College London), Ze Wang (University College London), Seonglae Cho (Holistic AI), Yufei Yang (Imperial College London), Adriano Koshiyama (University College London), Sahan Bulathwela (University College London), Maria Perez-Ortiz (University College London)

entry.summary: Finds that tool calling decisions in language models are linearly readable and steerable in internal activations across 12 models. Adding mean-difference vectors between tool activations switches tool selection at 77-100% accuracy, with arguments auto-conforming.

entry.title: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Tong Zheng, Haolin Liu, Chengsong Huang, Huiwen Bao, Sheng Zhang, Rui Liu, Runpeng Dai, Ruibo Chen, Chenxi Liu, Tianyi Xiong, Xidong Wu, Hongming Zhang, Heng Huang

entry.summary: Proposes AutoTTS, a framework where LLMs automatically discover test-time scaling strategies rather than having researchers manually design them. Constructs environments where TTS strategies can be discovered through search with cheap feedback.

entry.title: Experience Sharing in Mutual Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Language Models

author.name: Xiaoze Liu, Dhananjay Ram, Yuting Zhang, Zhaoyang Zhang, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto

entry.summary: Introduces Mutual Reinforcement Learning where heterogeneous LLM policies exchange typed experience while maintaining separate parameters and tokenizers. Implements experience sharing across incompatible model families through a Tokenizer Heterogeneity Layer.

entry.title: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Must Disclose Identification Assumptions for Causal Claims

author.name: Zezheng Lin, Fengming Liu

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that mechanistic interpretability must explicitly disclose causal identification assumptions. Audits 10 papers finding no dedicated identification sections and common validation-metric substitution for causal claims.

entry.title: A Breast Vision Pathology Foundation Model for Real-world Clinical Utility

author.name: Yingxue Xu, Zhengyu Zhang, Xiuming Zhang, Mengwei Xu, Fengtao Zhou, Yihui Wang, Jiabo Ma, Yi Xin, Danyi Li, Chengyu Lu, Zhijian Cen, Ying Tan, Qingbing Yao, Qi Wang, Zizhao Gao, Yong Zhang, Jingjing Chen, Feifei Liu, Qian Xu, Yi Dai, Hongxuan Tan, Cheng Jin, Huajun Zhou, Zhengrui Guo, Ling Liang, Hongyi Wang, Yingcong Chen, Xi Wang, Zhenhui Li, Ronald Cheong Kin Chan, Ning Mao, Muyan Cai, Zhe Wang, Li Liang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Presents BRAVE, a breast-adaptive pathology foundation model trained on 101,638 whole-slide images from 32 sources, evaluated across 34 tasks in 82 cohorts spanning pre/intra/post-operative stages.

entry.title: Playing games with knowledge: AI-Induced delusions need game theoretic interventions

author.name: Will Beaumaster, Paul Schrater

entry.summary: Formalizes sycophancy in AI chatbots as a Crawford-Sobel cheap talk game, showing that costless user signals induce pooling equilibria that reinforce epistemic entrenchment regardless of user type. Proposes game-theoretic interventions.

entry.title: CauSim: Scaling Causal Reasoning with Increasingly Complex Causal Simulators

author.name: Nicol\'as Astorga, Anita Kriz, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: Introduces CauSim, a framework that converts causal reasoning from a scarce-label problem into a scalable supervised one by constructing increasingly complex executable structural causal models as training data generators.

entry.title: Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget? Capability Degradation and Preservation in Lifelong LLM Agent Adaptation

author.name: Ye Yu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Haibo Jin, Heming Liu, Yaoning Yu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Identifies 'capability erosion under self-evolution' - where LLM agents adapting to new tasks degrade previously acquired capabilities across workflow, skill, model, and memory evolution channels. Proposes Capability-Preserving Evolution (CPE) to mitigate.

entry.title: RDKV: Rate-Distortion Bit Allocation for Joint Eviction and Quantization of the KV Cache

author.name: Junkai Zhang, Hang Guo, Luca Benini, Yawei Li

entry.summary: Frames KV cache compression as a rate-distortion optimization problem, unifying eviction and quantization as endpoints of the same bit allocation scheme. The joint optimization (RDKV) outperforms treating them in isolation.

entry.title: Cornerstones or Stumbling Blocks? Deciphering the Rock Tokens in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Runchao Li, Shubhashis Roy Dipta, Dawei Li, Zhao Yang

entry.summary: Identifies 'Rock Tokens' in on-policy distillation - tokens with persistently high loss that don't diminish even after training saturation. These account for up to 18% of tokens and represent fundamental student-teacher mismatches rather than convergence artifacts.

entry.title: Engineering Robustness into Personal Agents with the AI Workflow Store

author.name: Roxana Geambasu (Google, Columbia University), Mariana Raykova (Google), Pierre Tholoniat (Google), Trishita Tiwari (Google), Lillian Tsai (Google), Wen Zhang (Google)

entry.summary: Argues that the on-the-fly synthesis paradigm for AI agents short-circuits disciplined software engineering processes, proposing the AI Workflow Store pattern to integrate iterative design, testing, and staged deployment into agentic systems.

entry.title: Bilinear autoencoders find interpretable manifolds

author.name: Thomas Dooms, Ward Gauderis, Geraint Wiggins, Jose Oramas

entry.summary: Introduces bilinear autoencoders with quadratic latents that can capture multi-dimensional manifold concepts, challenging the linear representation hypothesis. Shows composite latents systematically outperform linear ones.

entry.title: Exploration-Driven Optimization for Test-Time Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Changhao Li, Yuchen Zhuang, Chenxiao Gao, Haotian Sun, Rushi Qiang, Chao Zhang, Bo Dai

entry.summary: Proposes Exploration-Driven Optimization (EDO) to address the tension between RL post-training (which sharpens distributions) and inference-time scaling (which benefits from diverse sampling). Integrates exploration objectives into iterative RL training.

entry.title: Reinforce Adjoint Matching: Scaling RL Post-Training of Diffusion and Flow-Matching Models

author.name: Andreas Bergmeister, Stefanie Jegelka, Nikolas N\"usken, Carles Domingo-Enrich, Jakiw Pidstrigach

entry.summary: Introduces Reinforce Adjoint Matching for RL post-training of diffusion/flow-matching models, showing that KL-regularized reward maximization preserves the regression structure of pretraining. Combines adjoint matching with policy gradient to maintain scalability while aligning with rewards.

entry.title: Reliable Chain-of-Thought via Prefix Consistency

author.name: Naoto Iwase, Yuki Ichihara, Mohammad Atif Quamar, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: Discovers that truncating a CoT trace and regenerating the remainder yields a reliability signal: correct traces reproduce their answer more often. Uses this 'prefix consistency' to weight answers without log-probabilities or self-rating.

entry.title: MemQ: Integrating Q-Learning into Self-Evolving Memory Agents over Provenance DAGs

author.name: Junwei Liao, Haoting Shi, Ruiwen Zhou, Jiaqian Wang, Shengtao Zhang, Wei Zhang, Weinan Zhang, Ying Wen, Zhiyu Li, Feiyu Xiong, Bo Tang, Muning Wen

entry.summary: Introduces MemQ, which applies TD(λ) eligibility traces to memory management in LLM agents, propagating credit through a provenance DAG that tracks memory dependency chains. Replaces temporal distance with structural proximity for credit assignment in episodic memory.

entry.title: RewardHarness: Self-Evolving Agentic Post-Training

author.name: Yuxuan Zhang, Penghui Du, Bo Li, Cong Wei, Junwen Miao, Huaisong Zhang, Songcheng Cai, Yubo Wang, Dongfu Jiang, Yuyu Zhang, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen, Changqian Yu, Kelsey R. Allen

entry.summary: Introduces RewardHarness, a self-evolving agentic reward framework for image editing that aligns with human preferences using only ~100 examples by iteratively evolving tools and skills rather than optimizing model weights.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Evaluating Strategy Diversity in LLM Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Xia Yang, Xuanyi Zhang, Hao Hu, Feng Ji

entry.summary: Introduces a strategy-level evaluation framework for LLM mathematical reasoning, showing a pronounced decoupling between answer accuracy and strategy diversity. Models achieve 95-100% accuracy but recover far fewer strategies than human reference sets.

entry.title: DARE: Diffusion Language Model Activation Reuse for Efficient Inference

author.name: Natalia Frumkin, Bokun Wang, Hung-Yueh Chiang, Chi-Chih Chang, Mohamed S. Abdelfattah, Diana Marculescu

entry.summary: Identifies token-wise redundancy in diffusion LLMs' self-attention and introduces DARE, which reuses cached KV activations and output activations to speed up inference by exploiting temporal correlations across denoising steps.

entry.title: Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Consensus Systems

author.name: Xiaolin Sun, Zixuan Liu, Yibin Hu, Zizhan Zheng

entry.summary: Studies insider manipulation in multi-agent LLM consensus systems, formalizing how a malicious agent can delay or prevent agreement. Develops attack strategies and defenses for multi-agent communication.

entry.title: HTPO: Towards Exploration-Exploitation Balanced Policy Optimization via Hierarchical Token-level Objective Control

author.name: Xincheng Yao, Ruoqi Li, Cheng Chen, Daoxin Zhang, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Chongyang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes HTPO, a hierarchical token-level policy optimization method for RLVR that assigns different optimization objectives to different tokens in chain-of-thought reasoning, dynamically balancing exploration and exploitation at the token level.

entry.title: Robust Multi-Agent LLMs under Byzantine Faults

author.name: Haejoon Lee, Vincent-Daniel Yun, Hyeonho Oh, Dimitra Panagou, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy

entry.summary: Proposes Self-Anchored Consensus (SAC) for making decentralized multi-agent LLM systems robust to Byzantine faults, where agents iteratively exchange, filter, and refine responses without leader-based coordination.

entry.title: FactoryNet: A Large-Scale Dataset toward Industrial Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Karim Othman, Jonas Petersen, Matei Ignuta-Ciuncanu, Riccardo Maggioni, Camilla Mazzoleni, Federico Martelli, Philipp Petersen

entry.summary: FactoryNet introduces the first universal pretraining corpus for industrial time-series (51M datapoints, 23k task executions, 6 embodiments) with a Setpoint-Effort-Feedback-Context schema enabling cross-embodiment zero-shot transfer.

entry.title: The Trap of Trajectory: Towards Understanding and Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Agentic Memory

author.name: Luoxi Tang, Rupali Rajendra Vaje, Yuqiao Meng, Sakshi Sunil Narkar, Weicheng Ma, Zeyu Ding, Dazheng Zhang, Zhaohan Xi

entry.summary: Identifies and benchmarks spurious correlations in agentic memory systems, showing that while memory improves reasoning on clean inputs, it amplifies reliance on spurious patterns when present. Proposes mitigation approaches.

entry.title: Mixture of Layers with Hybrid Attention

author.name: Ivan Ternovtsii, Yurii Bilak

entry.summary: Mixture of Layers (MoL) replaces full-width transformer blocks with K parallel thin blocks at reduced dimensionality, connected via learned projections and top-k routing. Introduces hybrid attention pairing shared softmax with Gated DeltaNet linear attention.

entry.title: The Cartesian Shortcut: Re-evaluate Vision Reasoning in Polar Coordinate Space

author.name: Xia Hu, Zhenrui Yue, Brian Potetz, Howard Zhou, Leonidas Guibas, Chun-Ta Lu, Zhicheng Wang

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Cartesian Shortcut' vulnerability in visual reasoning benchmarks where models exploit grid-based layouts for text-based deduction. Introduces Polaris-Bench with 53 tasks in polar coordinates to test genuine visual understanding.

entry.title: Guaranteed Jailbreaking Defense via Disrupt-and-Rectify Smoothing

author.name: Zheng Lin, Zhenxing Niu, Haoxuan Ji, Haichang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Disrupt-and-Rectify Smoothing (DR-Smoothing), a guaranteed defense against LLM jailbreaking that disrupts input prompts then rectifies them to in-distribution form, providing certified safety guarantees.

entry.title: Rethinking Agentic Search with Pi-Serini: Is Lexical Retrieval Sufficient?

author.name: Tz-Huan Hsu, Jheng-Hong Yang, Jimmy Lin

entry.summary: Introduces Pi-Serini, a search agent showing that BM25 lexical retrieval paired with GPT-5.5 achieves 83.1% accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus, suggesting capable LLMs can compensate for simple retrievers in agentic search.

entry.title: Feature Rivalry in Sparse Autoencoder Representations: A Mechanistic Study of Uncertainty-Driven Feature Competition in LLMs

author.name: Harshavardhan

entry.summary: Introduces Feature Rivalry - negatively correlated SAE feature pairs - as a mechanistic signature of model uncertainty in LLMs, showing it localizes to specific layers and correlates with response entropy.

entry.title: NeuralBench: A Unifying Framework to Benchmark NeuroAI Models

author.name: Hubert Banville (Lucy), St\'ephane d'Ascoli (Lucy), Simon Dahan (Lucy), J\'er\'emy Rapin (Lucy), Marl\`ene Careil (Lucy), Yohann Benchetrit (Lucy), Jarod L\'evy (Lucy), Saarang Panchavati (Lucy), Antoine Ratouchniak (Lucy), Mingfang (Lucy), Zhang, Elisa Cascardi, Katelyn Begany, Teon Brooks, Jean-R\'emi King

entry.summary: Presents NeuralBench, a unified framework for benchmarking AI models of brain activity, accompanied by NeuralBench-EEG v1.0 covering 36 EEG tasks, 14 architectures, and 94 datasets. From Meta (Jean-Rémi King's group).

entry.title: ReLibra: Routing-Replay-Guided Load Balancing for MoE Training in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chao Jin, Xinming Wei, Yinmin Zhong, Chengxu Yang, Bingyang Wu, Ruidong Zhu, Zili Zhang, Yuliang Liu, Xin Jin

entry.summary: Proposes ReLibra for load balancing in MoE training during RL, exploiting the fact that rollout and training process the same tokens to enable routing replay for fine-grained micro-batch load balancing.

entry.title: CoDistill-GRPO: A Co-Distillation Recipe for Efficient Group Relative Policy Optimization

author.name: Soo Min Kwon, Ziteng Sun, Ananda Theertha Suresh, Himanshu Jain, Sanjiv Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes CoDistill-GRPO, a co-distillation algorithm that simultaneously trains large and small language models with mutual knowledge sharing during GRPO, addressing sparse reward problems for small models.

entry.title: Mean-Pooled Cosine Similarity is Not Length-Invariant: Theory and Cross-Domain Evidence for a Length-Invariant Alternative

author.name: Sibayan Mitra (BITS Pilani), Dhruv Kumar (BITS Pilani)

entry.summary: Proves that mean-pooled cosine similarity is not length-invariant under transformer anisotropy, with length ratio explaining 52-75% of cross-language similarity scores. Proposes Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) as a length-invariant alternative.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Learn Alike: Attention Entropy Reveals Heterogeneous Signals in RL Reasoning

author.name: Gengyang Li, Zheng-Fan Wu, Siqi Bao, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: Studies heterogeneous token-level learning signals in RL-based reasoning through attention entropy. Finds low-entropy 'anchor' tokens produce stable gradients aligned with reward, while high-entropy tokens are noisy. Shows 20% random subsets preserve full performance.

entry.title: Your Language Model is Its Own Critic: Reinforcement Learning with Value Estimation from Actor's Internal States

author.name: Yunho Choi, Jongwon Lim, Woojin Ahn, Minjae Oh, Jeonghoon Shim, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Proposes using LLM internal hidden states as a value baseline for RLVR, avoiding PPO's separate critic or GRPO's multiple rollouts. A lightweight probe predicts expected reward from internal states and token-entropy statistics at negligible cost.

entry.title: GazeVLM: Active Vision via Internal Attention Control for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Brown Ebouky, Gabriele Carrino, Niccolo Avogaro, Christoph Studer, Andrea Bartezzaghi, Mattia Rigotti

entry.summary: Proposes GazeVLM, a VLM architecture that internalizes active vision by generating gaze tokens that direct foveal attention to task-relevant details during reasoning, mimicking human metacognitive control over visual attention.

entry.title: Where Reliability Lives in Vision-Language Models: A Mechanistic Study of Attention, Hidden States, and Causal Circuits

author.name: Logan Mann, Ajit Saravanan, Ishan Dave, Shikhar Shiromani, Saadullah Ismail, Yi Xia, Emily Huang

entry.summary: Tests the assumption that concentrated attention in vision-language models indicates reliability, finding that attention structure is a near-zero predictor of correctness across three VLM families. Introduces the VLM Reliability Probe (VRP) pipeline for mechanistic analysis of model trustworthiness.

entry.title: Not All Turns Matter: Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking

author.name: Zhida He, Xiaoyu Wen, Han Qi, Ziyuan Zhou, Peng Yu, Xingcheng Xu, Dongrui Liu, Xia Hu, Chaochao Lu, Qiaosheng Zhang

entry.summary: Addresses credit assignment in multi-turn jailbreaking by proposing TRACE, a turn-aware framework that recognizes turn-level contributions are non-uniform and phase-dependent, rather than broadcasting uniform trajectory-level rewards.

entry.title: Forge: Quality-Aware Reinforcement Learning for NP-Hard Optimization in LLMs

author.name: Xiaozhe Li, Xinyu Fang, Shengyuan Ding, Yang Li, Linyang Li, Haodong Duan, Qingwen Liu, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Proposes OPT-BENCH for training and evaluating LLMs on NP-hard optimization through quality-aware RLVR, introducing Forge which uses quality-aware rewards that evaluate solution optimality rather than just correctness.

entry.title: BoostAPR: Boosting Automated Program Repair via Execution-Grounded Reinforcement Learning with Dual Reward Models

author.name: Yuanhao Li, Hongbo Wang, Xiaotang Shang, Xunzhu Tang, Yiming Cao, Xuhong Chen

entry.summary: Presents BoostAPR, a three-stage framework for automated program repair using RL with dual reward models - a sequence-level assessor and line-level credit allocator. Achieves 40.7% on SWE-bench Verified, a +2% improvement.

entry.title: Don't Click That: Teaching Web Agents to Resist Deceptive Interfaces

author.name: Yilin Zhang, Yingkai Hua, Chunyu Wei, Xin Wang, Yueguo Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes deception-aware web agent defense and proposes DUDE framework combining hybrid-reward learning with experience summarization. Introduces RUC benchmark with 1,407 deceptive UI scenarios. Reduces deception susceptibility by 53.8%.

entry.title: Cross-Family Universality of Behavioral Axes via Anchor-Projected Representations

author.name: Su-Hyeon Kim, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Introduces anchor-projection framework mapping hidden representations from different model families into a shared coordinate space, enabling cross-family transfer of behavioral directions without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Optimizer-Induced Mode Connectivity: From AdamW to Muon

author.name: Fangzhao Zhang, Sungyoon Kim, Erica Zhang, Yiqi Jiang, Mert Pilanci

entry.summary: Studies mode connectivity through the lens of optimizer-induced implicit regularization. Shows solutions from a single optimizer form connected sets at large width, while different optimizers (AdamW vs Muon) can converge to disconnected components.

entry.title: FormalRewardBench: A Benchmark for Formal Theorem Proving Reward Models

author.name: Zeynel A. Ulu\c{s}an, Burak S. Akbudak, Can S. Erer, G\"ozde G\"ul \c{S}ahin

entry.summary: Introduces FormalRewardBench, the first benchmark for evaluating reward models in formal theorem proving with Lean 4. Addresses the sparse credit assignment problem in RLVR-based theorem provers by enabling comparison of reward models without expensive RL training.

entry.title: TRACE: Distilling Where It Matters via Token-Routed Self On-Policy Alignment

author.name: Jiaxuan Wang, Xuan Ouyang, Zhiyu Chen, Yulan Hu, Zheng Pan, Xin Li, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE, a token-routed self-distillation method that applies KL divergence only on critical reasoning spans rather than all tokens. Addresses entropy rise and out-of-distribution degradation in on-policy self-distillation for math reasoning.

entry.title: CLEF: EEG Foundation Model for Learning Clinical Semantics

author.name: Peng Cao, Ali Mirzazadeh, Jong Woo Lee, Aleksandar Videnovic, Dina Katabi

entry.summary: Introduces CLEF, a clinically grounded long-context EEG foundation model that processes full sessions via 3D multitaper spectrogram tokens and aligns with clinical reports through contrastive objectives. Evaluated on 234 tasks across 260k sessions.

entry.title: Remember the Decision, Not the Description: A Rate-Distortion Framework for Agent Memory

author.name: Mingxi Zou, Zhihan Guo, Langzhang Liang, Zhuo Wang, Qifan Wang, Qingsong Wen, Irwin King, Lizhen Qu, Zenglin Xu

entry.summary: Casts agent memory as a decision-centric rate-distortion problem, measuring memory quality by loss in achievable decision quality from compression. Derives an exact forgetting boundary and memory-distortion frontier.

entry.title: A Unified Pair-GRPO Family: From Implicit to Explicit Preference Constraints for Stable and General RL Alignment

author.name: Hao Yu

entry.summary: Establishes a unified theoretical framework for preference-based RL optimization called the Pair-GRPO family, with Soft and Hard variants. Addresses instability, gradient ambiguity, and high variance in pairwise preference learning for LLM alignment.

entry.title: NoiseRater: Meta-Learned Noise Valuation for Diffusion Model Training

author.name: Fang Wu, Haokai Zhao, Da Xing, Hanqun Cao, Tinson Xu, Yanchao Li, Xiangru Tang, Zehong Wang, Aaron Tu, Kuan Pang, Hanchen Wang, Hongbin Lin, Zeqi Zhou, Yinxi Li, Peng Xia, Li Erran Li, Molei Tao, Jure Leskovec, Aditya Joshi, Yejin Choi

entry.summary: Introduces NoiseRater, a meta-learning framework that assigns importance scores to individual noise realizations in diffusion model training, enabling adaptive reweighting via bilevel optimization to improve downstream performance.

entry.title: When Language Overwrites Vision: Over-Alignment and Geometric Debiasing in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Harshvardhan Saini, Samyak Jha, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Investigates geometric over-alignment in VLMs where visual embeddings are excessively aligned with the text manifold, causing linguistic bias to overshadow visual evidence. Proposes geometric debiasing.

entry.title: LaWM: Least Action World Models for Long-Horizon Physical Consistency from Visual Observations

author.name: Qixin Xiao, Maani Ghaffari

entry.summary: Proposes Least Action World Models (LaWM), which embed the principle of least action from physics into latent world models to improve long-horizon physical consistency. This addresses energy drift and compounding errors in model-based RL by grounding predictions in variational physics principles.

entry.title: FlashSVD v1.5: Making Low-Rank Transformers Inference Actually Fast

author.name: Wenhao Wu, Zishan Shao, Kangning Cui, Jinhee Kim, Yixiao Wang, Hancheng Ye, Danyang Zhuo, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: FlashSVD v1.5 provides a unified inference runtime for SVD-compressed transformers, addressing the gap between theoretical FLOP savings and actual serving speedups through phase-specific kernels and runtime optimizations.

entry.title: MathConstraint: Automated Generation of Verified Combinatorial Reasoning Instances for LLMs

author.name: Viresh Pati, Zhengyu Li, Piyush Jha, Rahul Garg, Yatharth Sejpal, Vijay Ganesh

entry.summary: Introduces MathConstraint, an adaptive benchmark for evaluating LLM combinatorial reasoning using solver-verified constraint satisfaction problems that can scale difficulty as models improve. Reports GPT-5.5 at 87.6% and Gemini-3.1-flash-lite at 72.6%.

entry.title: Geometry Guided Self-Consistency for Physical AI

author.name: Yinwei Dai, Zhuofu Chen, Lijie Yang, Ravi Netravali

entry.summary: KeyStone introduces an inference-time self-consistency method for diffusion-based robot action generation that samples K candidate action chunks in parallel, clusters them, and returns the medoid of the largest cluster—no extra model needed. This addresses the brittleness of committing to single stochastic trajectories in physical AI systems.

entry.title: AdaPreLoRA: Adafactor Preconditioned Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Ziyun Liu, Fengmiao Bian, Jian-Feng Cai

entry.summary: AdaPreLoRA provides a unified framework for LoRA optimizers, revealing that the Jacobian rank-deficiency creates a fundamental optimization challenge. Proposes using Adafactor preconditioning to address interaction-coefficient starvation in low-rank adaptation.

entry.title: Fitting Is Not Enough: Smoothness in Extremely Quantized LLMs

author.name: Yuzhuang Xu, Xu Han, Yuxuan Li, Pengzhan Li, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Shows that extremely quantized LLMs suffer from systematic smoothness degradation beyond numerical precision loss, with rapid reduction of effective token candidates in the prediction neighborhood leading to generation quality collapse.

entry.title: ShadowMerge: A Novel Poisoning Attack on Graph-Based Agent Memory via Relation-Channel Conflicts

author.name: Yang Luo, Zifeng Kang, Tiantian Ji, Xinran Liu, Yong Liu, Shuyu Li, Lingyun Peng

entry.summary: ShadowMerge is a poisoning attack against graph-based agent memory that exploits relation-channel conflicts to inject malicious relations that survive extraction, merge into target neighborhoods, and get retrieved for victim queries.

entry.title: WorldSpeech: A Multilingual Speech Corpus from Around the World

author.name: Antonis Asonitis, Luca A. Lanzend\"orfer, Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: WorldSpeech is a 65k-hour multilingual speech corpus across 76 languages collected from parliamentary proceedings, broadcasts, and audiobooks. Fine-tuning on it yields 63.5% average relative WER reduction.

entry.title: WavesFM: Hierarchical Representation Learning for Longitudinal Wearable Sensor Waveforms

author.name: Peng Cao, Zhijian Yang, Tennison Liu, Jonathan Wang, Jiang Wu, Magdalena Proszewska, Arvind Pillai, Mingwu Gao, Amir Farjadian, Lawrence Cai, Emily Blanchard, Daniel McDuff, Pramod Rudrapatna, Matthew Thompson, Anupam Pathak, Mark Malhotra, Shwetak Patel, Dina Katabi, Paolo Di Achille, Ming-Zher Poh

entry.summary: WavesFM introduces a hierarchical foundation model for learning representations from longitudinal wearable sensor data (like PPG and accelerometry), addressing the challenge of processing extreme sequence lengths spanning weeks of recordings. It uses a self-supervised approach that bridges short morphological features with long-term behavioral dynamics.

entry.title: On Variance Reduction in Learning Mean Flows

author.name: Juanwu Lu, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: Identifies the source of MeanFlow training instability in one-step generative models: the conditional velocity field plays two distinct statistical roles (regression target and control variate) with the wrong coefficient. Derives the optimal coefficient in closed form.

entry.title: Skill-R1: Agent Skill Evolution via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yash Vishe, Rohan Surana, Xunyi Jiang, Zihan Huang, Xintong Li, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Tong Yu, Ryan A. Rossi, Jingbo Shang, Julian McAuley, Junda Wu

entry.summary: Skill-R1 uses reinforcement learning to optimize reusable natural language 'skills' for LLM agents from verifiable rewards, without updating the task LLM itself. This enables skill improvement even for closed-source models.

entry.title: DeepTumorVQA: A Hierarchical 3D CT Benchmark for Stage-Wise Evaluation of Medical VLMs and Tool-Augmented Agents

author.name: Yixiong Chen, Wenjie Xiao, Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Boyan Wang, Liang He, Xinze Zhou, Sezgin Er, Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Zongwei Zhou, Alan Yuille

entry.summary: Proposes DeepTumorVQA, a hierarchical benchmark for evaluating medical VLMs on 3D CT reasoning, decomposing tumor diagnosis into four stages: recognition, measurement, visual reasoning, and medical reasoning. Contains 476K questions across 42 clinical subtypes.

entry.title: Key-Value Means

author.name: Daniel Goldstein, Eugene Cheah

entry.summary: Presents Key-Value Means (KVM), a novel block-recurrence for attention supporting fixed-size or growing state, yielding O(N) chunked RNN or sublinear state growth transformer with standard operations and no custom kernels.

entry.title: Position: Academic Conferences are Potentially Facing Denominator Gaming Caused by Fully Automated Scientific Agents

author.name: Rong Shan, Te Gao, Hang Zheng, Yunjia Xi, Jiachen Zhu, Zeyu Zheng, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: Position paper warning about 'Agentic Denominator Gaming' - malicious actors using AI agents to flood conference submissions, inflating the denominator to increase acceptance probability of targeted papers under stable acceptance rates.

entry.title: Verifier-Free RL for LLMs via Intrinsic Gradient-Norm Reward

author.name: Xuexiang Wen, Hang Yu, Linchao Zhu, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes VIGOR, a verifier-free RL reward for LLMs that uses gradient-norm of teacher-forced NLL as an intrinsic preference signal, eliminating need for gold labels or domain-specific verifiers.

entry.title: G-Zero: Self-Play for Open-Ended Generation from Zero Data

author.name: Chengsong Huang, Haolin Liu, Tong Zheng, Runpeng Dai, Langlin Huang, Jinyuan Li, Zongxia Li, Zhepei Wei, Yu Meng, Jiaxin Huang

entry.summary: Introduces G-Zero, a verifier-free self-play framework for open-ended LLM generation using Hint-δ, an intrinsic reward measuring the predictive shift between unassisted and hint-conditioned responses, with concurrent Generator-Proposer co-evolution.

entry.title: Retrieve-then-Steer: Online Success Memory for Test-Time Adaptation of Generative VLAs

author.name: Jianchao Zhao, Huoren Yang, Hu Yusong, Yuyang Gao, Qiguan Ou, Cong Wan, SongLin Dong, Zhiheng Ma, Yihong Gong

entry.summary: Proposes a test-time adaptation framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in robotics that stores successful executions as memory and reuses them to improve reliability during persistent deployment. This addresses the gap between zero-shot evaluation and real-world repeated deployment scenarios.

entry.title: Generative AI Fuels Solo Entrepreneurship, but Teams Still Lead at the Top

author.name: Hyunso Kim, Hyo Kang, Jaeyong Song

entry.summary: Analyzes 160K+ Product Hunt launches to show that generative AI (post-ChatGPT) boosted solo entrepreneurship entry but teams still dominate highest-quality outcomes, suggesting AI lowers entry barriers without equalizing top performance.

entry.title: Toward an Engineering of Science: Rebalancing Generation and Verification in the Age of AI

author.name: Jiaqi W. Ma

entry.summary: Argues that AI-era science should treat epistemic infrastructure as an engineering problem, rebalancing generation and verification costs given that AI cheaply generates plausible but potentially unreliable scientific artifacts.

entry.title: Step Rejection Fine-Tuning: A Practical Distillation Recipe

author.name: Igor Slinko, Ilia Zavidnyi, Egor Bogomolov, Yaroslav Zharov

entry.summary: Proposes Step Rejection Fine-Tuning (SRFT), which uses a critic LLM to assess individual steps in failed trajectories, masking loss on erroneous steps while retaining them in context. Shows improvements on SWE-bench by leveraging partially correct trajectories.

entry.title: AssayBench: An Assay-Level Virtual Cell Benchmark for LLMs and Agents

author.name: Edward De Brouwer, Carl Edwards, Alexander Wu, Jenna Collier, Graham Heimberg, Xiner Li, Meena Subramaniam, Ehsan Hajiramezanali, David Richmond, Jan-Christian H\"utter, Sara Mostafavi, Gabriele Scalia

entry.summary: Introduces AssayBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs and agents on in silico phenotypic screening - predicting effects of cellular perturbations in unseen biological contexts, combining heterogeneous textual inputs with phenotypic outputs.

entry.title: ExecuTorch -- A Unified PyTorch Solution to Run AI Models On-Device

author.name: Mergen Nachin, Digant Desai, Sicheng Stephen Jia, Chen Lai, Mengwei Liu, Jacob Szwejbka, Raziel Alvarez, RJ Ascani, Dave Bort, Manuel Candales, Andrew Caples, Yanan Cao, Zhengxu Chen, Soumith Chintala, Gregory Comer, Tanvir Islam, Songhao Jia, Tarun Karuturi, Jack Khuu, Abhinay Kukkadapu, Tugsbayasgalan Manlaibaatar, Andrew Or, Kimish Patel, Siddartha Pothapragada, Lucy Qiu, Supriya Rao, Orion Reblitz-Richardson, Max Ren, Scott Roy, Anthony Shoumikhin, Scott Wolchok, Guang Yang, Angela Yi, Martin Yuan, Hansong Zhang, Jack Zhang, Jerry Zhang, Shunting Zhang, C. Cagatay Bilgin

entry.summary: Introduces ExecuTorch, a PyTorch-native deployment framework for edge AI that enables seamless model deployment across heterogeneous hardware from microcontrollers to SoCs with accelerators.

entry.title: What Time Is It? How Data Geometry Makes Time Conditioning Optional for Flow Matching

author.name: Alec Helbling, Sebastian Gutierrez Hernandez, Benjamin Hoover, Duen Horng Chau, Parikshit Ram

entry.summary: Analyzes why flow matching models can work without explicit time conditioning by decomposing the loss into coupling variance and a time-blindness gap. Shows that data geometry (low intrinsic dimensionality) naturally resolves the ambiguity, explaining why time-blind models succeed in practice.

entry.title: The Geometric Structure of Models Learning Sparse Data

author.name: Thomas Walker, T. Mitchell Roddenberry, Ahmed Imtiaz Humayun, Randall Balestriero, Richard Baraniuk

entry.summary: Formalizes 'normal alignment' as a geometric property explaining how models succeed in sparse data regimes where the manifold hypothesis doesn't apply. Proves normal-aligned classifiers minimize training objectives under norm constraints.

entry.title: PRISM: Fast Online LLM Serving via Scheduling-Memory Co-design

author.name: Xingyu Qu, Tianhao Lin, Yiqi Li, Zhiyu Chen, Sheng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PRISM, a scheduling-memory co-design for LLM serving that jointly optimizes request admission with KV-cache retention, exploiting prompt segmentation and hotspot skew patterns.

entry.title: LAQuant: A Simple Overhead-free Large Reasoning Model Quantization by Layer-wise Lookahead Loss

author.name: Euntae Choi, Sumin Song, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes LAQuant for quantizing large reasoning models, identifying KV-cache fidelity and Hessian alignment as key factors. Uses lookahead loss to maintain reasoning accuracy during quantization.

entry.title: Sparse Layers are Critical to Scaling Looped Language Models

author.name: Ryan Lee, Jacob Biloki, Edward J. Hu, Jonathan May

entry.summary: Shows that Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformers enable looped language models to scale much better than dense looped models. Different experts activate per loop pass, recovering expressivity without additional parameters. MoE looped models show better compute-quality tradeoffs.

entry.title: Dimension-Free Saddle-Point Escape in Muon

author.name: Yanlin Long, Yufei Gu, Zeke Xie

entry.summary: Proves that Muon optimizer achieves dimension-free saddle-point escape, avoiding the O(D) curse that traps element-wise adaptive optimizers like AdamW. Uses resolvent functional calculus and spectral perturbation theory.

entry.title: Model Capacity Determines Grokking through Competing Memorisation and Generalisation Speeds

author.name: Yiding Song, Hanming Ye

entry.summary: Provides an information-theoretic explanation of grokking by showing it emerges from competition between memorization speed and generalization speed, both functions of model parameter count. Derives a closed-form phase boundary predicting when grokking occurs.

entry.title: BCJR-QAT: A Differentiable Relaxation of Trellis-Coded Weight Quantization

author.name: Venugopalan Iyengar

entry.summary: Introduces BCJR-QAT, enabling quantization-aware training for trellis-coded quantization of LLMs by replacing the non-differentiable Viterbi argmax with the differentiable BCJR forward-backward algorithm. Achieves new SOTA at 2-bit LLM quantization with a fused Triton kernel providing 6.57x speedup.

entry.title: Alice v1: Distillation-Enhanced Video Generation Surpassing Closed-Source Models

author.name: Wang Xiaoyu, Phong Nguyen, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: Presents Alice v1, a 14B parameter open-source video generation model that surpasses teacher model quality through consistency distillation with score regularization (rCM). Demonstrates that distillation can exceed teacher quality through mode-seeking objectives and targeted synthetic data.

entry.title: Structured Recurrent Mixers for Massively Parallelized Sequence Generation

author.name: Benjamin L. Badger

entry.summary: Introduces the Structured Recurrent Mixer architecture that algebraically converts between parallel training representation and recurrent inference representation without specialized kernels, achieving both training efficiency and inference throughput.

entry.title: Phases of Muon: When Muon Eclipses SignSGD

author.name: Elliot Paquette, Noah Marshall, Lucas Benigni, Guangyuan Wang, Atish Agarwala, Courtney Paquette

entry.summary: Analyzes Muon and spectral optimizers on high-dimensional matrix problems, showing phase transitions between square-root preconditioning and SignSGD-like behavior depending on batch size.

entry.title: Sharp feature-learning transitions and Bayes-optimal neural scaling laws in extensive-width networks

author.name: Minh-Toan Nguyen, Jean Barbier

entry.summary: Studies information-theoretic limits of learning wide teacher networks with hierarchical features, deriving sharp characterizations of Bayes-optimal generalization error via fixed-point equations. Reveals sharp feature-learning phase transitions and neural scaling laws.

entry.title: The Text Uncanny Valley: Non-Monotonic Performance Degradation in LLM Information Retrieval

author.name: Zekai Tong, Ruiyao Xu, Aryan Shrivastava, Chenhao Tan, Ari Holtzman

entry.summary: Discovers a U-shaped performance curve ('Text Uncanny Valley') when LLMs process text with increasing word-boundary corruption. Proposes a mode transition hypothesis where LLMs switch between word-level and character-level processing, with degraded performance at intermediate corruption levels.

entry.title: Safe, or Simply Incapable? Rethinking Safety Evaluation for Phone-Use Agents

author.name: Zhengyang Tang, Yi Zhang, Chenxin Li, Xin Lai, Pengyuan Lyu, Yiduo Guo, Weinong Wang, Junyi Li, Yang Ding, Huawen Shen, Zhengyao Fang, Xingran Zhou, Liang Wu, Fei Tang, Sunqi Fan, Shangpin Peng, Zheng Ruan, Anran Zhang, Benyou Wang, Chengquan Zhang, Han Hu

entry.summary: Introduces PhoneSafety, a benchmark of 700 safety-critical moments from real phone interactions across 130+ apps, distinguishing whether phone-use agents avoid harm through genuine safety recognition versus inability to act.

entry.title: TextLDM: Language Modeling with Continuous Latent Diffusion

author.name: Jiaxiu Jiang, Jingjing Ren, Wenbo Li, Bo Wang, Haoze Sun, Yijun Yang, Jianhui Liu, Yanbing Zhang, Shenghe Zheng, Yuan Zhang, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: Proposes TextLDM, applying the visual latent diffusion recipe to text generation with a Transformer-based VAE that maps tokens to continuous latents enhanced by Representation Alignment with frozen pretrained LMs. Standard DiT performs flow matching in this latent space.

entry.title: MatryoshkaLoRA: Learning Accurate Hierarchical Low-Rank Representations for LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Ionut-Vlad Modoranu, Mher Safaryan, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Proposes MatryoshkaLoRA, a rank-adaptive LoRA variant that learns accurate nested low-rank representations at multiple ranks simultaneously, eliminating the need for exhaustive rank grid searches during fine-tuning.

entry.title: The Position Curse: LLMs Struggle to Locate the Last Few Items in a List

author.name: Zhanqi Zhang, Hua-Dong Xiong, Robert C. Wilson, Mikio Aoi, Marcelo G. Mattar, Li Ji-An

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Position Curse' - LLMs fail to retrieve the last few items in short lists despite handling needle-in-haystack tasks well. Even Claude Opus 4.6 misidentifies the second-to-last line in two-line code snippets most of the time.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders as Plug-and-Play Firewalls for Adversarial Attack Detection in VLMs

author.name: Hao Wang, Yiqun Sun, Pengfei Wei, Lawrence B. Hsieh, Daisuke Kawahara

entry.summary: Proposes SAEgis, using sparse autoencoders as plug-and-play adversarial attack detectors for VLMs. Finds that learned sparse latent features from standard reconstruction training naturally capture attack-relevant signals for reliable detection.

entry.title: Personal Visual Context Learning in Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Zihui Xue, Ami Baid, Sangho Kim, Mi Luo, Kristen Grauman

entry.summary: Formalizes Personal Visual Context Learning for LMMs integrated with wearable devices like smart glasses, enabling reasoning over user-specific visual information. Introduces Personal-VCL-Bench benchmark and reveals a significant context utilization gap in frontier models.

entry.title: On the Generation and Mitigation of Harmful Geometry in Image-to-3D Models

author.name: Yule Liu, Yilong Yang, Jiale Teng, Hanze Jia, Zeren Luo, Jingyi Zheng, Zifan Peng, Ke Li, Yifan Liao, Zhen Sun, Jiaheng Wei, Yang Liu, Zhuo Ma, Xinlei He

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic measurement study of harmful geometry generation in image-to-3D models, examining how these models can be misused to create physically dangerous objects (weapons, hazards) and evaluating existing safeguards.

entry.title: When Agents Overtrust Environmental Evidence: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Benchmarking Evidence-Grounding Defects in LLM Agents

author.name: Strick Sheng, Ziyue Wang, Liyi Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmarking framework for testing whether LLM agents remain grounded in true environment state when observations are stale, incorrect, or malicious, addressing evidence-grounding defects in agentic systems.

entry.title: Learning to Explore: Scaling Agentic Reasoning via Exploration-Aware Policy Optimization

author.name: Xingyuan Hua, Sheng Yue, Ju Ren

entry.summary: Proposes an exploration-aware RL framework for LLM agents that adaptively explores only when uncertainty is high, using variational inference to evaluate exploratory actions by their potential to improve future decisions.

entry.title: Done, But Not Sure: Disentangling World Completion from Self-Termination in Embodied Agents

author.name: Ying Chen, Rui Jiang, Lihuang Fang, Mingxu Wang, Zhifeng Gu, Lei Yi, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Introduces VIGIL, an evaluation framework that separately measures task completion (world-state) and terminal commitment (knowing when to stop) in embodied agents, revealing that these are distinct failure modes collapsed in standard benchmarks.

entry.title: From Holo Pockets to Electron Density: GPT-style Drug Design with Density

author.name: Jiahao Chen, Letian Gao, Yanhao Zhu, Wenbiao Zhou, Bing Su, Zhi John Lu, Bo Huang

entry.summary: Uses electron density maps from cryo-EM/X-ray as physically grounded conditions for de novo drug design, leveraging density information that captures conformational flexibility better than rigid pocket representations.

entry.title: FRACTAL: SSM with Fractional Recurrent Architecture for Computational Temporal Analysis of Long Sequences

author.name: Mengqi Li, Wensheng Lin, Jinshuai Yang, Lixin Li

entry.summary: Proposes FRACTAL, a state space model integrating fractional measure theory into recursive memory updates, balancing retention of long history with detection of short-term variations through fractional calculus-based projections.

entry.title: MDGYM: Benchmarking AI Agents on Molecular Simulations

author.name: Vinay Kumar, Satyendra Rajput, Mausam, N. M. Anoop Krishnan

entry.summary: Introduces MDGYM, a benchmark of 169 expert-curated molecular dynamics simulations for evaluating AI agents on autonomous computational science workflows across LAMMPS and GROMACS.

entry.title: Ambig-DS: A Benchmark for Task-Framing Ambiguity in Data-Science Agents

author.name: Josefa Lia Stoisser, Marc Boubnovski Martell, Sidsel Boldsen, Kaspar M\"artens, Robert Kitchen

entry.summary: Introduces Ambig-DS benchmark for detecting when data-science agents silently commit to incorrect task framings. Covers prediction-target ambiguity and evaluation-objective ambiguity across 112 tasks.

entry.title: Primal-Dual Guided Decoding for Constrained Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Federico Tomasi, Dmitrii Moor, Alice Wang, Mounia Lalmas

entry.summary: Proposes primal-dual guided decoding for constrained generation in discrete diffusion models, using adaptive Lagrangian multipliers updated via mirror descent to enforce global property constraints at inference time.

entry.title: SLASH the Sink: Sharpening Structural Attention Inside LLMs

author.name: Yiming Liu, Bin Lu, Xinbing Wang, Chenghu Zhou, Meng Jin

entry.summary: Discovers that LLMs spontaneously reconstruct graph topology internally via 'sawtooth' attention patterns, but this structural understanding is diluted by attention sinks. Proposes SLASH to sharpen structural attention without training.

entry.title: The Safety-Aware Denoiser for Text Diffusion Models

author.name: Amman Yusuf, Zhejun Jiang, Mijung Park

entry.summary: Proposes SAD (Safety-Aware Denoiser), a framework for steering text diffusion models toward safe outputs by modifying the iterative denoising process. Provides provable safety guarantees at inference time without retraining.

entry.title: SPECTRE: Hybrid Ordinary-Parallel Speculative Serving for Resource-Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Jincheng Xie, Yawen Ling, Qi Xiao, Feiyu Zhang, Zhongyi Huang, Wen Hu, Yu Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes SPECTRE, an LLM serving framework that reuses underutilized tail-model services as remote drafters for heavily loaded models through parallel speculative decoding.

entry.title: WebTrap: Stealthy Mid-Task Hijacking of Browser Agents During Navigation

author.name: Zhichao Liu, Wenbo Pan, Haining Yu, Ge Gao, Tianqing Zhu, Xiaohua Jia

entry.summary: Introduces WebTrap, a mid-task hijacking attack against browser agents that injects malicious instructions during navigation, achieving high attack success while maintaining system usability to avoid detection.

entry.title: A meshfree exterior calculus for generalizable and data-efficient learning of physics from point clouds

author.name: Benjamin D. Shaffer, Brooks Kinch, M. Ani Hsieh, Nathaniel Trask

entry.summary: Introduces MEEC, a meshfree exterior calculus for learning physics on point clouds that satisfies discrete conservation exactly, and MEEC-Net, a data-efficient surrogate that transfers across resolutions, geometries, and physical parameters.

entry.title: When Child Inherits: Modeling and Exploiting Subagent Spawn in Multi-Agent Networks

author.name: Ziwen Cai, Yihe Zhang, Xiali Hei

entry.summary: Models security risks from subagent spawning in multi-agent LLM networks, showing how inherited memory from compromised parent agents can propagate malicious instructions to child agents.

entry.title: Transformers Can Implement Preconditioned Richardson Iteration for In-Context Gaussian Kernel Regression

author.name: Mingsong Yan, Dongyang Li, Charles Kulick, Sui Tang

entry.summary: Shows that standard softmax transformers can implement preconditioned Richardson iteration for in-context Gaussian kernel ridge regression, providing an end-to-end prediction-error guarantee for nonlinear ICL.

entry.title: Slipstream: Trajectory-Grounded Compaction Validation for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Zhuofu Chen, Rui Pan, Yinwei Dai, Ravi Netravali

entry.summary: Proposes Slipstream, an asynchronous compaction validation system for long-horizon LLM agents that runs validation off the critical path by checking if compacted summaries lead to equivalent agent behavior.

entry.title: Explanation Fairness in Large Language Models: An Empirical Analysis of Disparities in How LLMs Justify Decisions Across Demographic Groups

author.name: Gautam Veldanda

entry.summary: Introduces the Explanation Fairness Taxonomy (EFT) with five dimensions measuring whether LLMs justify decisions with equal quality across demographic groups. Finds systematic disparities in verbosity, sentiment, hedging, and lexical complexity across 80 prompt templates and four decision domains.

entry.title: SimReg: Achieving Higher Performance in the Pretraining via Embedding Similarity Regularization

author.name: Yan Sun, Guoxia Wang, Jinle Zeng, JiaBin Yang, Shuai Li, Li Shen, Dacheng Tao, DianHai Yu, Haifeng Wang

entry.summary: SimReg proposes an embedding similarity regularization loss for LLM pretraining that encourages tokens with the same label to cluster while separating different-label tokens. Claims to improve pretraining efficiency by reducing intra-class variance.

entry.title: LLM-Agnostic Semantic Representation Attack

author.name: Jiawei Lian, Jianhong Pan, Lefan Wang, Yi Wang, Tairan Huang, Shaohui Mei, Lap-Pui Chau

entry.summary: Proposes Semantic Representation Attack (SRA), an LLM-agnostic jailbreak method that targets malicious semantic representations rather than exact affirmative text templates, achieving better cross-model generalization.

entry.title: Tracking the Truth: Object-Centric Spatio-Temporal Monitoring for Video Large Language Models

author.name: Tri Cao, Khoi Le, Thong Nguyen, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Quynh Vo, Anh Tuan Luu, Chunyan Miao, See-Kiong Ng, Shuicheng Yan, Bryan Hooi

entry.summary: STEMO-Bench evaluates video LLMs on spatio-temporal monitoring—persistent tracking of object identities, states, and relations over time. Shows current models fail at intermediate reasoning even when final answers appear correct.

entry.title: A Geometric Perspective on Next-Token Prediction in Large Language Models: Three Emerging Phases

author.name: Gianfranco Lombardo, Giuseppe Trimigno, Stefano Cagnoni

entry.summary: Investigates the geometry of predictive information across LLM layers using representation lenses on the Grassmann manifold. Identifies three emergent phases in how predictive information evolves across depth.

entry.title: ProactBench: Beyond What The User Asked For

author.name: Sepehr Harfi, Ahmad Salimi, Dongming Shen, Alex Smola

entry.summary: ProactBench measures 'conversational proactivity' - an LLM's ability to notice and act on implied but unstated user needs. It decomposes this into three types (Emergent, Critical, Recovery) and uses multi-agent evaluation with information asymmetries to prevent scoring artifacts.

entry.title: RuPLaR : Efficient Latent Compression of LLM Reasoning Chains with Rule-Based Priors From Multi-Step to One-Step

author.name: Xiaocheng Luo, Kang Wang, Zaifu Zhan, Yuechi Zhou, Xiangyu Duan

entry.summary: RuPLaR compresses Chain-of-Thought reasoning into a single latent step using rule-based priors, training an LLM to generate latent reasoning tokens in one training stage. Addresses error propagation and coordination overhead in multi-step latent CoT.

entry.title: Sparsity Moves Computation: How FFN Architecture Reshapes Attention in Small Transformers

author.name: Gabriel Smithline, Chris Mascioli

entry.summary: Studies how FFN architecture choices (dense, GLU, MoE) reshape attention computations in small transformers. Finds that sparse MoE routing can shift computation from FFN to attention, with frozen random routing nearly matching learned routing.

entry.title: Pretraining large language models with MXFP4

author.name: Musa Cim, Poovaiah Palangappa, Miro Hodak, Ravi Dwivedula, Meena Arunachalam, Mahmut Taylan Kandemir

entry.summary: Studies why full FP4 training of LLMs diverges, finding that quantizing weight gradients (Wgrad) is the primary driver of convergence degradation, while FP4 in forward and activation gradients introduces only modest overhead.

entry.title: Pseudo-Deliberation in Language Models: When Reasoning Fails to Align Values and Actions

author.name: Sushrita Rakshit, Hanwen Zhang, Hua Shen

entry.summary: Introduces 'Pseudo-Deliberation' - when LLMs appear to reason about values but fail to align actions accordingly. Proposes VALDI framework with 4,941 scenarios to measure value-action gaps across five domains.

entry.title: When Does Non-Uniform Replay Matter in Reinforcement Learning?

author.name: Michal Korniak, Miko{\l}aj Czarnecki, Yarden As, Piotr Mi{\l}o\'s, Pieter Abbeel, Michal Nauman

entry.summary: Systematically investigates when non-uniform replay helps in reinforcement learning, identifying replay volume, expected recency, and sampling entropy as governing factors, providing practical guidance for replay design.

entry.title: Phoenix-VL 1.5 Medium Technical Report

author.name: Team Phoenix, :, Arka Ray, Askar Ali Mohamed Jawad, Biondi Lee, Elijah Seah, Eva Lim, Fiona Teo, Grace Toh, Guang Xiang Teo, Jun En Tan, Jia Hui Bong, Jiale Wang, Jonathan Ng, Justin Tan, Kai Zhe Yew, Matthew Ong, Shun Yi Yeo, Wen Jett Lam, Wen Xiu Tan, Ze Yu Zhang, Gee Wah Ng, Chee Wee Ang, Mistral AI, :, Adrien Sad\'e, Guillaume Kunsch, Jia Sin Loh, Nicolas Schuhl, Rupert Menneer, Umar Jamil, Vincent Maladi\`ere, Yimu Pan

entry.summary: Introduces Phoenix-VL 1.5 Medium, a 123B-parameter multimodal/multilingual model adapted from Mistral Medium 3.1 for Singapore context with 1T+ tokens of continued pretraining and regional language adaptation.

entry.title: Infinite Mask Diffusion for Few-Step Distillation

author.name: Jaehoon Yoo, Wonjung Kim, Chanhyuk Lee, Seunghoon Hong

entry.summary: Proposes Infinite Mask Diffusion Model (IMDM) that uses continuous mask states instead of binary masks to reduce factorization errors in masked diffusion models, enabling few-step distillation for language modeling.

entry.title: Acceptance Cards:A Four-Diagnostic Standard for Safe Fine-Tuning Defense Claims

author.name: Phongsakon Mark Konrad, Toygar Tanyel, Serkan Ayvaz

entry.summary: Proposes Acceptance Cards, a four-diagnostic evaluation protocol for safe fine-tuning defense claims, showing that SafeLoRA fails all diagnostics on Gemma-2-2B-it under strict evaluation.

entry.title: ALAM: Algebraically Consistent Latent Transitions for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zuojin Tang, Haoyun Liu, Xinyuan Chang, Changjie Wu, Dongjie Huo, Yandan Yang, Bin Liu, Zhejia Cai, Feng Xiong, Mu Xu, jiachen Luo, De Ma, Zhiheng Ma, Gang Pan

entry.summary: Introduces ALAM, which learns latent transitions from action-free video that satisfy algebraic consistency constraints (associativity, invertibility), enabling better policy generation for robot manipulation from video priors.

entry.title: DataMaster: Towards Autonomous Data Engineering for Machine Learning

author.name: Yaxin Du, Xiyuan Yang, Zhifan Zhou, Wanxu Liu, Zixing Lei, Zimeng Chen, Fenyi Liu, Haotian Wu, Yuzhu Cai, Zexi Liu, Xinyu Zhu, WenHao Wang, Linfeng Zhang, Chen Qian, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: Introduces DataMaster for autonomous data engineering, where an agent optimizes the data pipeline (discovery, selection, cleaning, transformation) for a fixed learning algorithm to improve downstream performance.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Discretization Error of Diffusion Models

author.name: Samuel Hurault, Thomas Moreau, Gabriel Peyr\'e

entry.summary: Derives first-order asymptotic expansions of discretization error for diffusion model sampling, providing geometry-aware analysis that is sensitive to diffusion schedule parameters and data geometry. More informative than existing worst-case bounds.

entry.title: CUDABeaver: Benchmarking LLM-Based Automated CUDA Debugging

author.name: Shiyang Li, Haoyang Chen, Mattia Fazzini, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: Introduces CUDABeaver, a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based CUDA debugging from real failing workspaces, detecting when models simplify code rather than truly fixing bugs (degeneration).

entry.title: Finer is Better (with the Right Scaling)

author.name: Clemens Schaefer, Gil Tabak

entry.summary: Investigates the paradox where finer microscaling block sizes degrade LLM quality, showing it's caused by heavy-tailed distributions interacting poorly with FP4 quantization bins rather than being inherent to finer granularity.

entry.title: The Extrapolation Cliff in On-Policy Distillation of Near-Deterministic Structured Outputs

author.name: Xin Li, Hao Jiang, Annan Wang, Yichi Zhang, Chau Yuen
